title: Escape with the Summer Wind
author: Peanut Tree
synopsis:
At fifteen, the boy, carrying the orange-gold summer wind, barged into Si Qing's world without warning.
Qi Fang came from a prominent family in the capital, wearing the skin of a carefree playboy, his gaze seemingly never lingering on anyone.
In her first year of university, a video of Si Qing giving a speech as a freshman representative was pinned to the top of the forum.
The girl was graceful and elegant, like a distant moon over the mountains, drawing admiration from all who saw her.
No one would ever associate the gentle, aloof little fairy with the indifferent young master who never took anything seriously.
Until later, someone witnessed the usually arrogant young master leaning against a windowsill, patiently braiding the little girl's hair.
---
In a hidden corner, the tall boy bent low before the girl, his eyes gentle, his fingertips lightly brushing her palm.
"Si Qing, look at me."
Qi Fang's voice, deep and smooth, coaxed softly, "Let's try, okay?"
"I'm yours to mold."
*
[In the third decade of snowfall, I was the first to covet the moon]
---
"I escape with the summer wind, waiting to meet you."
[Gentle, Sweet, and Good at Coaxing × Elegant Rascal Who Flirts and Acts Coy]

chapters.title: His Frequency
chapters.content:
*By Peanut*

"I escape with the summer wind, waiting to meet you."

---

The wind of September silenced the cicadas' clamor, and the heat squeezed itself into the crowd.

The bustling atmosphere of Capital University during the start of the school year was no less lively than a marketplace, with the sounds of horns, conversations, and rolling suitcases blending together.

Si Qing got out of the taxi early and headed straight for the North Gate.

She was studying finance, part of the School of Management, along with the Schools of Economics and Finance, all under the business category. Their welcome ceremony was at the North Gymnasium.

The gym was well air-conditioned. The wooden floor had colored guide stickers, divided by schools and further by majors, making it clear at a glance.

The class assistants, all seniors, were seated in their respective areas handling freshman registration.

The Finance Department had no new students at the moment, so a few assistants were chatting among themselves.

Ke Mingyuan stared at a message on WeChat and laughed, "The teaching assistants for the Medical School drew the short straw and have to welcome new students at the South Field. After two days, they've painlessly become African citizens."

"No wonder. I thought the person I saw in the cafeteria yesterday was an international student. Turns out it was a med student," Li Qingyu sipped the strawberry milkshake on the table and frowned, "Wow, this is so sweet, I need insulin."

"Don't complain when you're getting free stuff," Ke Mingyuan shot him a look. "A classmate from the Law School brought it for Brother Qi. You just got lucky, you greedy little thing."

Li Qingyu bit the straw and took several big gulps, "I deserve it for covering his shift."

The others joked around for a bit longer.

Soon, a light-colored figure stopped in front of Ke Mingyuan's desk. "Senior."

Her voice was clear and crisp.

Everyone turned to look.

The girl stood tall and graceful, wearing a simple light blue fitted T-shirt and light-colored slightly flared jeans. Her black hair was gathered at the nape of her neck in a simple low side bun.

From Li Qingyu's angle, he could only see a small part of her profile, but judging by the half-hidden, half-revealed glances from others, this girl was undoubtedly a great beauty.

The group, afraid of making the girl uncomfortable, quickly averted their eyes.

Si Qing handed over her admission notice with both hands, "I'm Si Qing from Finance Class 1, here to register."

The girl's round, bright deer-like eyes were clear and transparent, her features distinct and delicate. The overhead lights in the gym cast a soft, silvery glow around her, as if outlining her with a thin layer of light.

Ke Mingyuan was stunned for a moment, but not just because of her stunning appearance.

A few days ago, during the business school assistants' meeting, he had seen her transcript. This girl was this year's top scorer from Mountain City.

In Capital University, where exceptional people were everywhere, both achievements and grades commanded respect.

Ke Mingyuan quickly regained his composure, handed her the forms and a carbon pen, and pointed towards Li Qingyu, "Freshman, please fill out the registration form. There are chairs over there where you can sit."

Si Qing's gaze swept over the pink nameplate standing at the corner of Li Qingyu's desk, and her eyelashes trembled almost imperceptibly.

Commercial School Guide Assistant - Qi Fang.

The name, carved into the secret corner of her heart, suddenly surfaced. Her fingers, holding the form, unconsciously tightened.

Although the boy sitting at the assistant's desk was not him, Si Qing could roughly guess that the person who was supposed to be there might not have shown up for some reason.

She had come to Capital University for her future, and also to step into the world where Qi Fang existed.

So, she knew that there couldn't be another Qi Fang at Capital University.

Si Qing lowered her lashes and sat down, filling out the form as required. After handing it back to Ke Mingyuan for his signature, she pushed her suitcase towards the back door of the gymnasium.

Behind her, a rustling sound gradually arose, growing louder as it approached.

After a moment, a male voice called out to her, "Freshman, you forgot your receipt."

Si Qing turned around at the sound of his voice. Ke Mingyuan was running towards her with the dormitory check-in receipt.

Seeing how urgent he looked, Si Qing jogged towards him to take the receipt. As she turned her head slightly, she caught a glimpse of the assistant's desk where a new person had appeared.

In the blurred peripheral vision, the first thing she recognized was the frequency in her chest, the one that belonged solely to Qi Fang.

Thanks to his exceptionally striking appearance, the subtle glances directed at him were countless, and she was one of them.

The boy leaned against the edge of the assistant's desk, his posture relaxed, wearing a plain white T-shirt and black jeans. His long legs were stretched out carelessly, with one foot resting on the crossbar of the chair she had just sat on.

His demeanor was relaxed, but not excessively lazy.

Just like in her memories, there was always a lively atmosphere around him.

Like a bright, clear sun, dazzling yet distant.

She curved her lips slightly, lowered her gaze, and averted her eyes, walking out of the gymnasium.

A wind carrying a hint of osmanthus fragrance blew over, soothing her heart rate. Si Qing took out her phone, which had been vibrating frequently.

The dormitory group chat, *Crazy Week (4)*, was buzzing with messages.

Capital University had four-person dorms. The three girls sharing a dorm with Si Qing had arrived a day earlier and were waiting for her to check in and say hello.

So, a green bubble appeared in the group chat: "Squeak"

Cen Weiying was the first to reply: "Baby! You're such a cute little hamster!"

Zhu Xing: "Qingbao, you're finally here! We just left the cafeteria. We'll send you our location. The sisters will come pick you up. ~"

Si Qing was about to tell them not to trouble themselves when a message popped up as if anticipating her: "Find a shady spot to wait. We'll be there quickly on our bikes. It's no trouble."

Her eyes were about to cry from the sweetness.

She opened the food delivery app, ordered some desserts and low-calorie fruit teas for the girls, then put her phone away and stood under a camphor tree across the square.

---

Si Qing had chosen a good spot.

Not too far, not too close, she could see the assistant's desk from the back door with just a glance.

Qi Fang tilted his head carelessly. When he spoke, occasionally a small dimple would appear at the corner of his left lip.

Si Qing lowered her eyelashes and lightly bit the soft flesh inside her lip.

A dimple, typically a feature of sweet girls, didn’t seem out of place on him. Unfortunately, she didn’t have one.

Girls in the throes of unrequited love always tried to find common ground between themselves and the person they liked.

If there was none, they would inevitably feel a little down.

But there had always been very little intersection between them.

He was passionate and outgoing, while she was gentle and reserved. They were from two different worlds.

Among their few intersections, perhaps... people (?) could be considered one?

Si Qing stared at her shoelaces, lost in her own little world.

Sunlight filtered through the gaps in the leaves, casting irregular patches of light that danced on her eyebrows and lashes.

As the wind blew, the light and shadows shifted, her hair swayed, and the whole scene came to life.

Occasionally, admiring glances would fall on her, but they all tacitly chose not to disturb her.

The three girls who had come to pick up Si Qing parked their shared bikes and stood at the intersection. They stared at the girl under the tree for a long time before suddenly taking a deep breath.

"Are you saying that the fairy under the tree is Qingbao, the same person who plays stupid little games with us on voice chat every night?" Cen Weiying cleared her throat.

"Are you saying that a gorgeous beauty has been playing abstract games with me for half a month?" Zhu Xing twitched the corner of her lip.

How could someone so stunning not have a single photo in her moments?!

Only Tan Lexi, after standing still for a moment, rushed forward.

"Qingbao!"

Si Qing reacted, blinking her eyes in delight, "Qiqii!"

There was a sense of familiarity, as if they had met many times before, not for the first time.

Back at the gymnasium, Ke Mingyuan looked at the group of girls laughing and chatting across the street, clicking his tongue, "Youth."

"Enough from you. The girl is leaving, and you're still staring," Li Qingyu rolled his eyes, then withdrew his gaze, sweeping past the person at the assistant's desk, and suddenly let out a sound.

Nine out of ten, a rare sight.

When had Qi Fang ever stared at a girl like that?

It was as fresh as burning paper money for his father. Absolutely fresh.

Li Qingyu leaned in, "Even a blind man can't resist a beauty."

A burst of laughter came from the back door of the gymnasium, dispersing in the wind, sounding a bit muffled.

Si Qing looked in the direction of the sound.

Unexpectedly, she locked eyes with a pair of deep, fox-like eyes.

At the moment their gazes met, Qi Fang tilted his head slightly.

Si Qing tried her best to maintain her composure.

This man's thoughts were harder to guess than the methods of a murderer in a Conan case. She didn’t know why he was looking her way.

She knew Qi Fang had seen too many glances directed at him. Even if it was just based on experience, he could probably tell the general feelings behind them.

Si Qing's dormmates looked over with her.

The three girls exchanged a glance.

Cen Weiying: "Capital University's male actor, pretending to be blind and deaf?"

Tan Lexi: "Capital University's must-eat list, give him a home?"

Zhu Xing: "Is that him?"

With each new term, Si Qing's eyes widened a little more.

She guessed these were probably forum terms related to Qi Fang, but—

Capital University's must-eat list... really?

Cen Weiying noticed the confusion in her eyes and pinched her cheek, "Let's go back to the dorm and tell you all about it. Look at your face, it's all red from the heat."

Si Qing panicked and blinked, pulling her gaze away from Qi Fang and touching her burning cheeks.

So her blush was that obvious!

She touched her nose and pulled her suitcase, "Let's go."

The summer wind blew, lifting the loose strands of hair around her ears.

Under the shadow of her dark hair, her fair cheeks and the nape of her neck were exposed, glowing with a hint of pink under the sunlight, unguarded, falling into the eyes of the person behind her.

Qi Fang's eyebrows twitched slightly.

The little girl seemed to have gotten sunburned; her face was quite red.

Li Qingyu saw Qi Fang staring intently outside with no sign of stopping, his eyes wide in surprise.

"Bro, tell the truth. Is there a girl among the freshmen who looks like money?"

Previously, there had been a post on the forum discussing this person's ideal type.

Somehow, the discussion had derailed, leading to a conclusion.

"Qi Fang's daily life: eating, sleeping, making money—so he likes girls who blush like a 100-yuan bill!"

It was originally a joke.

But what was surprising was that Qi Fang himself had liked that post.

...

Qi Fang withdrew his gaze from the girl's soft, delicate profile.

"Probably."

---

**Peanut's Reading Guide**

1. Si Qing: A first-year finance student, a top-tier, gentle, and naturally beautiful girl. A clear-headed and self-sufficient academic elite who knows how to pursue her goals with quiet determination. A cool, humorous, and charming little treasure.

2. Qi Fang: A second-year student who transferred from Law to International Economics and Trade. Outwardly playful but inwardly passionate, and very flirtatious. For love, he is willing to be tamed, also known as Qi the Charming. Under his playful exterior, he is a proud, sharp-tongued young master who pursues pure love.

3. Pure in body and mind, mutual chase, slow-burn romance, full sugar, no angst.

4. No deep male secondary characters, no vicious female supporting characters, no dog-blood drama, no real-life prototypes. Please do not role-play.

5. The author's writing is average, soft-hearted but fragile. If you provoke me, I will become fluffy, letting you punch cotton and warm your hands in the process :)

May 5, 2025, Start of Summer

[Welcome everyone in this passionate summer to fall in love with the Qi-Si CP]

chapters.title: The Moon and the Wind
chapters.content:
Si Qing’s dormitory was in Building 25 of the South District. A few girls strolled to the entrance, picked up their takeout from the self-service lockers, and headed upstairs.

The dorm room was 616—a lucky number, but unfortunately, the building had no elevator.

Under Beijing’s scorching 38-degree heat, they climbed the six flights of stairs, exhausted. After tidying up, Si Qing slipped into the bathroom for a shower.

Due to the dorm’s low voltage, high-wattage appliances like hair dryers had to be used in the laundry room.

When Si Qing came out, her hair was still dripping.

She flicked a damp strand from her forehead and asked her roommates, “Where’s our laundry room?”

The three girls looked up in unison, frozen.

They felt like fish—every time they saw her after a short absence, their perception of her beauty refreshed.

Si Qing’s features were sharp-angled, yet her exquisite delicacy softened any aggression. Her jawline was perfectly tapered, her lips full and glossy, and her doe-like eyes, misted with moisture, gleamed like tea crystals—clear and mesmerizing, inviting a closer look.

A natural beauty, devastating to all genders.

Si Qing blinked, rubbing her face with the back of her hand. “Do I have something on my face?”

“Shocking beauty,” Cen Weiying propped her chin.

Tan Lexi: “I want to slide down your nose.”

After spending half a month together, Si Qing knew their antics well.

She curved her eyes. “There’s still some water in my collarbone. You can swim for a bit.”

The girls laughed until their shoulders shook.

“Perfect timing—I need to grab my clothes. Let’s show off my fairy roommate.”

Zhu Xing, done laughing, grabbed the hairdryer and tried to hook her arm around Si Qing’s neck, only to find it awkward. She settled for linking arms instead.

Zhu Xing was 167 cm tall, and Si Qing looked to be over 170.

“Qingbao, how tall are you?”

“173, according to my college entrance exam physical.” Si Qing tilted her head. “But a lot of people at our school said the measurements were off.”

“I think they’re accurate,” Zhu Xing asked, “Were the ones saying it was off mostly guys?”

Si Qing widened her eyes. “How did you know?”

“…” Zhu Xing smirked. “Same as some guys at our school.”

They reached the laundry room. Si Qing dried her hair while Zhu Xing collected the clothes.

Over the hum of the dryer, Si Qing heard Zhu Xing’s wail: “My earphones!”

She peeked over. “What’s wrong, Zhuzhu?”

“I just realized I washed my earphones,” Zhu Xing laughed bitterly. “It’s fine, I’ll try blasting them with a vibration frequency later to see if they’ll work.”

On their way back to the dorm, as soon as they pushed the door open, Tan Lexi and Cen Weiying rushed over with their phones. “Qingbao, check the forum.”

It was a trending post on the Capital University freshmen forum: #Are you commercial majors trying to debut?

Cen Weiying tapped on a comment thread where a photo of Si Qing, taken during her admission registration, was posted.

「1L: Si Qing! We went to the same high school! I was lucky enough to ask her for help with a problem—she’s incredibly kind! She was this year’s second-highest scorer in Shancheng Province. Our school even put up a banner for her!」

「2L: Damn, a top student *and* a beauty….」

…

「64L: I stood next to her today and didn’t even dare to look at her twice. She’s too beautiful… crying.jpg」

「65L: I get it! If I saw Liu Yifei, I’d probably forget how to speak too.」

Zhu Xing, who was in the same class as Si Qing, knew she had the top score in their major but didn’t realize it was *this* impressive.

“Damn, Shancheng had 99.8 million test-takers this year…”

Si Qing pressed her lips together, touching her nose. “I just performed exceptionally well.”

During her first mock exam, her scores had plummeted to around 500th in the province, making it nearly impossible to get into Capital University.

Shancheng used the 3+3 exam model, and she had chosen history, geography, and biology—a crowded track that year, making it hard to score high.

At her lowest point, she had almost sacrificed sleep entirely.

But fortunately, the payoff was worth it.

“Modest, aren’t we?” Cen Weiying sipped her fruit tea, then remembered something. “Oh right, I was supposed to show Qingbao that senior’s post.”

Tan Lexi and Zhu Xing dragged their chairs over to Cen Weiying’s side, casually handing Si Qing a bag of melon seeds.

“Let’s see.”

Si Qing, bewildered, was arranged into position. Then she saw the text on Cen Weiying’s tablet.

It was a post from the start of the previous academic year.

The comment section under 【Capital University’s Male Drama King】 was full of jokes.

「The CP I ship must be real: Today I saw a phenomenon-level handsome guy and wanted to ask for his WeChat, but he seemed like a visually impaired person. Not sure if he’s from our school.」

「Friendship Building B: Is he the tall one with a half-tied wolf tail haircut and dimples?」

「The CP I ship must be real: Yes!」

「Friendship Building B: Oh no, another victim.」

「Awoo: Don’t even get me started. I asked him for his WeChat, and he used sign language with me. I thought he was hearing-impaired, so I left in disappointment. Then, just as I walked away, I heard his friend laugh, and he told his friend to ‘get lost’….」

「Turkey-Flavored Crisp: 666, not even trying to act anymore.」

「Awoo: He’s actually a good person, at least he didn’t reject me directly. It’s just… thinking about it later makes me want to laugh and cry.」

「The CP I ship must be real: HAHA! So he was NEVER blind at all!」

「I’m a fan: See? Another one tricked.」

An epic anti-depression post.

Si Qing only curved her eyes, saying nothing.

Qi Fang—trusted in high school, mocked online in university, reckless and flamboyant.

After enrollment, as people got to know him, these little jokes died down.

They scrolled to the bottom of the post, and Cen Weiying switched to 【Capital University’s Must-Eat List】.

The title had been updated this year. The comments listed Capital University’s handsome men over the years.

It was as comprehensive as an encyclopedia, categorized meticulously, rivaling Baidu Baike.

In Qi Fang’s section, there were photos of him from various periods.

Si Qing’s gaze settled on one from September of last year.

Back then, Qi Fang’s hair was longer, reaching the nape of his neck, half-tied at the back.

The last time she had seen him was in a video call between Tang Youmin and Qi Fang, when his hair was about that length.

Tang Youmin was the younger brother of Si Qing’s stepfather, only one year older than her. By seniority, she should call him “Little Uncle.”

Among Si Qing and Qi Fang’s limited social circles, he was one of the few connections.

After Qi Fang transferred back to Beijing from Shancheng in the second half of his sophomore year, he went through a rough patch.

Living alone, his routine was irregular. He even missed parts of his transfer exams because he overslept.

During high school, Tang Youmin boarded at school and only got his phone on Friday afternoons. Occasionally, he would call Qi Fang to check if he was still alive.

One day, Tang Youmin returned from grocery shopping, and Si Qing heard him on the phone with someone.

“You don’t even look human anymore.”

The other person’s voice was too low and hoarse for Si Qing to recognize.

“Stop being so dramatic,” Tang Youmin laughed, storming toward her with the phone. “Say hi to Si Qing.”

At the sound, Si Qing looked up.

The screen was dim, as if the curtains were drawn and the lights were off.

The blue glow of the computer monitor outlined the sharp contours of the boy’s face. His brows and lashes were lowered, and he barely glanced at the phone screen.

In the faint light, Si Qing recognized Qi Fang.

He looked terrible—nothing like the bold, unrestrained boy she remembered.

“Doesn’t he look like a ghost?”

Qi Fang had the kind of looks that could effortlessly charm anyone. Si Qing thought he’d look good even in a burlap sack.

Tang Youmin calling him a ghost was an exaggeration.

At the time, the “homeless” aesthetic was trendy.

“This is… *homeless*… style.”

She tried to explain to Tang Youmin, but before she could finish, his phone nearly hit her face.

Si Qing leaned back, trying to finish her sentence, but Tang Youmin had already pulled the phone away.

“Look what you did to her,” Tang Youmin glared at Qi Fang through the screen, striding toward the kitchen. “Did you hear that? She called you a homeless man.”

Great Auntie, how unfair!

Si Qing stretched out her leg to chase after Tang Youmin.

The next second, the call ended with a beep, freezing her in place.

“…” The world had ended.

Lost in thought, a fair hand waved in front of her face.

Tan Lexi stared at her, rubbing her chin.

With so many handsome photos on the screen, she watched as Si Qing’s gaze grew increasingly distant.

After a moment, she concluded: “Is Qingbao sleepy?”

She had heard before that people from Shancheng and Shanxi provinces had the habit of taking afternoon naps—some even got drowsy at the same time every day.

Si Qing snapped back. “I’m fine.”

In high school, she didn’t like napping—sleeping too little or too much left her groggy.

When she felt drowsy in class, she’d stand by the window at the back, and the breeze would clear her head.

But Tan Lexi’s reminder made Zhu Xing check the time. As if triggered, she yawned. “My Shanxi blood is awakening. I’m passing out, everyone.”

Cen Weiying also closed her tablet, changed into her pajamas, and climbed into bed. “I’ll sleep for a bit too.”

Si Qing and Tan Lexi instinctively fell silent, each busy with their own tasks in their chairs.

The cicadas’ buzzing was muffled outside the glass window, fading into the stifling heat of late summer.

Si Qing narrowed her eyes, suddenly recalling those shallow, sly fox-like eyes with a hint of a smile. Her heartbeat grew lively, like a fluttering bird.

She leaned on the desk, her fingertips opening Weibo.

Si Qing rarely used Weibo. This account was registered with an old phone number back in junior high.

This was her safe space, a little tree hollow she had built for herself.

At first, she only occasionally posted about plants, sunsets, and brick walls.

Until September 30, 2021—a private post visible only to herself.

「My heart yearns for the wind and the moon, but the wind and the moon do not know.」

—The uncertain wind of late summer, the untouchable moon of the night.

That was her view of Qi Fang.

The latest post was from 10:29 AM on September 9, 2024—the day she stood under a tree, watching him from afar.

「Long time no see.」

From February 8, 2022, to September 9, 2024—944 days since Qi Fang left Shancheng until today.

Long time no see, Qi Fang.

---

West District, Building 14, Male Dorm 102.

Tang Youmin carried dinner, lifting his knee to push open the dorm door. A figure immediately lunged toward him like a starving wolf.

Li Qingyu had just returned from welcoming freshmen and was now ravenous.

Tang Youmin stepped inside and kicked the door shut. “Make sure you grab the right one.”

【No green onions, ginger, garlic, or cilantro. No spice, no numbing, extra sugar, half vinegar】

Li Qingyu singled out the order with the longest note. “Got it. This one’s Qi Fang’s.”

Tang Youmin glanced at the empty space under the innermost bunk. “Where’s Qi Fang?”

As if on cue, the bathroom door unlocked.

“Hmm?” Qi Fang pushed his damp hair back from his forehead.

Tang Youmin smirked. “What’s with the attitude?”

At the mention of attitude, Li Qingyu had plenty to say.

“Today during freshmen welcome, Qi Fang kept staring at some girls,” he forked a meatball into his mouth, chewing. “It’s like spring in September.”

Tang Youmin perked up.

In all the years he’d known Qi Fang—from freshman to sophomore year—he had never seen him give a second glance to any unfamiliar girl.

“Which girls?” he asked, amused.

Qi Fang pulled out a chair and sat down, silent, just lifting his eyelids to stare at Tang Youmin.

That face, that gaze—if it were directed at a girl, she probably wouldn’t be able to resist.

But to Tang Youmin, it was just creepy, like a Siberian wolf entering the village.

He kicked the leg of Qi Fang’s chair. “Who are you playing mute with?”

Qi Fang kicked back without hesitation.

The chair leg scraped against the tiles with a short, sharp sound.

Tang Youmin rubbed his ear and heard Qi Fang drop three words lightly.

“Yours.”

chapters.title: Fang Fang
chapters.content:
The low hum of the air conditioner settled into an eerie silence.

The dumpling in Li Qingyu’s mouth slipped into the soup, splashing with a "plop."

Just as he was dazed, the dormitory door was pushed open from the outside.

A boy with dark red streaks in his hair walked in, casually hanging his bag on the wardrobe before sitting down and starting to complain.

"The bugs on the South Campus field are like cultivated insects," he said, his gaze sweeping around as he spoke. "123, wooden man?"

"Fang is digging under Min’s wall, and the two of them are in a deathmatch." Li Qingyu summarized succinctly, twisting the facts beyond recognition.

Qi Fang laughed and cursed, "Get lost. Your top priority right now is to find your cabbage and noodles."

Li Qingyu: ?

Lu Yeti, whose hometown was in the three northeastern provinces, instantly understood Qi Fang’s meaning. "He’s calling you a pig. Can’t you tell?"

"..." Li Qingyu closed his eyes and rolled them weakly in frustration.

*God’s braised pork with noodles.*

This guy’s mouth is like a bamboo spirit that’s reverted to youth—now he’s a bamboo shoot.

Tang Youmin picked up the earlier topic and asked Qi Fang, "Did you see Si Qing today?"

Qi Fang’s fingertips traced the cap of a mineral water bottle, recalling the pair of eyes that had caught his attention that morning.

Dark, clear, calm as a breeze.

"Yeah."

It’s just that the little girl seemed not to recognize him.

He had looked over to say hello, but Si Qing had been as indifferent as if she were seeing a stranger.

"Oh. I thought the iron tree had bloomed," Tang Youmin smirked. "Turns out you ran into a little iron tree. Birds of a feather flock together."

Qi Fang tilted his head back and took a sip of water.

Listening to their conversation, Li Qingyu felt his brain evolving.

After a moment, he finally caught on.

"You both know each other, right?" Li Qingyu grabbed a handful of his hair, exasperated. "Then why were you two being so cryptic just now? Treating your bro like an invader?"

Lu Yeti collapsed onto the table laughing, shaking the desk.

When Ke Mingyuan came to visit the dorm, he pushed the door open to see—

A dad calmly drinking water, a mom indifferently watching the show, a brother convulsing wildly, and himself on the verge of shattering.

"So lively today," Ke Mingyuan leaned against Lu Yeti’s desk. "Did I miss something?"

Li Qingyu dramatically recounted the events.

Ke Mingyuan, hearing it involved a new student from his class, remembered the purpose of his visit and smoothly took over the conversation. "Fang, tomorrow afternoon is the school’s day off. Do you have plans?"

Qi Fang lifted his eyelids. "What’s up?"

"I didn’t take the final exam for the Ideological and Moral Cultivation course last semester because I broke my leg. The teacher just notified me that the makeup exam is rescheduled to tomorrow at 1:30 PM."

Ke Mingyuan and Lu Yeti were in a band. Last semester, they had a performance by the sea in Tianjin.

The guys had recreated Sun Wukong’s nine consecutive photos by the sea. Only Ke Mingyuan had bad luck—stepping on an inflatable ring, he ended up with a fractured left ankle and a sprained right wrist.

Lu Yeti: "Can the makeup exam time be changed just like that?"

"1v1, I have to be ready at any time." Ke Mingyuan dryly laughed. "If you knew I was the only one in the entire Business School taking the makeup exam, you’d think my life is miserable."

He continued the interrupted topic. "Tomorrow at 2 PM, the freshmen get their books. I can’t go. Can you help me pick mine up, Fang?"

Tang Youmin: "Why ask him? Anyone else would do."

Ke Mingyuan: "He’s the only one free."

Everyone present was busy.

Tang Youmin was in the External Liaison Department, currently busy with attracting investments.

Lu Yeti was the director of the Student Affairs Office and the band leader, busy with freshmen registration files, welcome performances, and still a struggling medical student—24 hours a day wasn’t enough for him.

Li Qingyu was the new military training head instructor for the Business School freshmen, starting training tomorrow.

As for Ke Mingyuan’s other roommates, the medical and chemistry students had experiments, and the remaining one was a lovebird with a date.

That left Qi Fang. The Student Union hadn’t started recruitment, no teaching assistant work had been assigned, and he had no girlfriend to accompany.

Who else could he ask?

Li Qingyu: "He might not even be awake by that time in the afternoon."

This guy had no schedule for sleeping during the holidays. When he woke up was purely up to fate.

Today, fate was kind—he woke up a little after 10 AM. Not only did he wake up, but he also went to work.

It was as rare as a sow climbing a tree.

Unexpectedly, the ancestor agreed readily. "Sure."

"Who’s talking!" Li Qingyu looked like he’d seen a ghost. "Whoever you are, get out of him!"

"..." Ke Mingyuan suddenly felt like he’d walked into a trap.

Qi Fang was loyal, tough on the outside but soft-hearted. To get him to do something, you had to beg and plead. It usually took a lot of effort.

But now he agreed so readily. Ke Mingyuan felt uneasy instead.

People were just like that—always needing a bit of suffering to feel at ease.

Ke Mingyuan narrowed his eyes. "Bro, don’t tell me you’ve taken a liking to our class’s Si Qing and are looking for an excuse to hit on her."

Qi Fang lazily lowered his eyelids. "Then find someone else."

"Qi Fang and Si Qing?" Tang Youmin found it funnier the more he thought about it. "Two iron trees seeing who’s harder?"

Others might not know, but he did.

Back in high school, at Shancheng No. 1 Middle School, there were East and West campuses.

Qi Fang was in the West campus, and Si Qing was in the East.

When it came to being hard to pursue, they were second to none.

Moreover, apart from seeing each other at school honor boards and flag-raising ceremonies, Tang Youmin had never seen them interact.

At most, they knew of each other’s existence but hadn’t even added each other on WeChat.

The only time they might have communicated was when he and Qi Fang were on a video call, and Si Qing appeared for a few seconds.

Besides, Qi Fang had been half-dead in that video. Si Qing probably didn’t even recognize him.

They chatted a bit more about the topic.

The person in question remained silent, just listening.

Before long, Qi Fang stood up, throwing the empty water bottle into the trash can. "You all chat. I’m going to sleep."

Ke Mingyuan glanced at his watch—it wasn’t even 7 PM yet. "Going to bed already?"

Tang Youmin looked at Qi Fang’s untouched meal. "Are you trying to be a god?"

"Full from water."

Tang Youmin: "..."

---

The next morning at 10:30 AM, the freshmen familiarized themselves with the campus. Tan Lexi, who woke up the earliest, went to the cafeteria and brought back several breakfasts.

After finishing breakfast, they all went downstairs together.

Peking University had a large campus, and with so many people in the heat, just walking around made several of them dizzy.

The class assistant, combining lecture and tour, took nearly two hours for the whole loop.

When Si Qing returned to the dormitory, she smelled a faint scent of Huoxiang Zhengqi Water.

Tan Lexi was lying on her bed, stiff as a corpse, with a cooling patch on her forehead.

Beijing had recently experienced typhoon weather, with high humidity, and the past few days had been hot and stuffy.

Tan Lexi was a girl from Sichuan, but she couldn’t adapt well to the hot and humid climate. Back home, she often suffered from heatstroke.

The other girls quietly tidied up and went to the cafeteria for lunch, bringing back an egg fried rice and a watermelon fruit platter for Tan Lexi.

Zhu Xing and Si Qing weren’t far from where Tan Lexi was supposed to pick up her books, so they took the opportunity to get them for her.

In the afternoon, Si Qing carried a suitcase to hold her, Zhu Xing’s, and Tan Lexi’s books and military training uniforms.

On her way upstairs, she met a few classmates. They had gotten to know each other a bit during the campus tour and could exchange a few words.

"Did you hear that all first-year Business School students have morning self-study? We have to be in the classroom before 7 AM."

"My roommate is from the School of Mathematics. They have evening self-study, so they don’t have to wake up early. I’m so envious."

"School of Mathematics... In a couple of years, they’ll all be bald. Then you won’t be envious anymore."

"Can studying mathematics make you go bald faster than studying law?"

"Studying law doesn’t necessarily make you go bald. Look at Qi Fang—his hair is still thick."

At Peking University, his name could come up anywhere, anytime.

By the second day of school, Si Qing had already realized this.

"Then why do you think he transferred to Business School after just one year?"

"Come on, even the president has hair loss problems?"

"Hahahahahaha!"

As she stepped onto the last step of the third floor, Si Qing pushed her suitcase toward the direction of Finance Class 1. Just past the glass door at the corner, she saw an extremely eye-catching figure.

Qi Fang was lowering his brows, spacing out, idly twirling a silver pen between his fingers.

His burgundy shirt was half-unbuttoned, the shoulder line broad and straight. The sleeves loosely hung at his forearms, perfectly revealing his beautiful muscle lines. The hem of the shirt, along with a black undershirt, was tucked into black casual trousers, exuding an air of noble nonchalance.

Compared to yesterday, today was a completely different style.

Peking University had its own Miracle Nikki.

A somewhat cute phrase suddenly popped into Si Qing’s mind.

Miracle Fang Fang.

...

After putting away her and Zhu Xing’s books, Si Qing stood up to sign the military training uniform registration form.

There were only three pens on the table, and they had just been taken by the three students in front of her to fill out their forms.

At this moment, Qi Fang was leaning back in his chair, playing on his phone. She stood diagonally in front of him.

Recalling the girls’ teasing earlier, she suddenly became curious.

Qi Fang was tall. Standing shoulder to shoulder with him, she’d be lucky to see his chin, let alone the top of his head.

This was a perfect opportunity.

Qi Fang’s peripheral vision caught a figure leaning slightly in his direction. His tongue pressed against his lower lip.

Si Qing stood on her tiptoes, and just as her gaze flickered over, the man turned his face toward her.

She quickly averted her eyes, her hands unconsciously making eight hundred fake movements.

At this moment, the busiest person in the world was standing in front of Qi Fang.

The girl’s eyelashes were long, trembling like a sieve.

"You’ll fan yourself into a cold."

Si Qing was startled and hastily dug out a "thank you" from her mental vocabulary.

A few seconds later, she realized and closed her eyes in despair.

What was she even thanking him for!

Wasn’t this like someone stepping on her foot and her apologizing in return?

It wasn’t until the table in front of her was tapped twice that she opened her eyes again.

A hand with fine, long knuckles was loosely suspended, the middle finger slightly curved as it knocked on the table.

His skin was pale, his fingertips slightly upturned, the veins on the back of his hand slightly raised, and his joints had a faint pinkish hue.

Qi Fang’s fingertips pinched the pen cap, gently unscrewing it. His middle and index fingers, holding the cap, retreated, leaving the pen barrel at her side.

"Use it."

Qi Fang was very considerate—she had known that since the first time she met him.

Si Qing took the pen. "Thank you, Senior."

"No problem."

In a moment, the girl’s fair and slender hand, holding the pen and paper, reached out to him.

"Senior, here’s your pen back."

The game had just started a new round. Qi Fang took the form from her hand and placed it on the corner of the table, leaving only the pen lying across her palm.

Si Qing watched as the pen cap, pressed by the pad of his finger, slowly screwed onto the tip of the pen in her hand.

At this distance, she could even feel the warmth of his palm.

It wasn’t until he slowly tightened the cap that Qi Fang pulled the pen from her hand.

The entire motion was fluid and graceful. Even Zhang Hao, the class assistant from Class 2 sitting at the next table, almost had his eyes pop out.

Did Qi Fang even know what he was doing?!

Even without any physical contact, anyone who saw it would ask: What’s your relationship?

Fortunately, everyone around was busy with their own tasks. No one was paying attention, or else they’d definitely be posted on the forum and gossiped about endlessly.

Zhang Hao waited until Si Qing left before speaking. "Bro, if you’re drunk, go back to the dorm to sleep, okay?"

But Qi Fang seemed completely unaware of how ambiguous his actions had been. He continued spinning the pen as if nothing had happened.

After a few moments of silence, Qi Fang casually said, "No," and continued focusing on playing *Jin Chan Chan*.

Si Qing took a couple of steps with her suitcase before snapping out of her CPU-overload state.

It was because Qi Fang was playing a game and couldn’t free his hands to take the pen, so he had conveniently pressed the pen cap onto the pen in her hand.

Unrequited love was most taboo when it came to overthinking.

High expectations only led to greater disappointment when the ideal response wasn’t received.

Arbitrary expectations and despair were forbidden—they would disrupt her peace of mind.

Her top priority at Peking University was to study hard. She couldn’t keep being led by the nose by baseless emotions.

Her phone vibrated. Si Qing gathered her thoughts, put on her headphones, and pressed answer.

Zhu Xing’s voice, mixed with subtle static, came through. "Qing Bao, Seven’s books are so heavy! I can barely carry them! I won’t come upstairs to find you for now. Let’s meet at the entrance of Building 7, okay?"

"Okay. Put the books down somewhere first. I’ll be right there."

Si Qing arranged the military training uniform and closed the suitcase. She heard Zhu Xing’s broken voice again. "What did you say? Your voice is too soft. I can’t hear clearly."

Si Qing repeated herself. Zhu Xing’s end had even worse reception. "Are you telling me to find a place to walk around with the books?"

That was too cruel.

"It’s *Fang Fang*."

Si Qing suddenly remembered that Zhu Xing’s headphones had been water-damaged, so she raised her voice and enunciated clearly, repeating once more.

"*Fang—Fang*."

A strange sense of déjà vu.

...Fang Fang?

Suddenly realizing, Si Qing instinctively looked toward Qi Fang’s direction. Her heart was about to leap into her throat as she silently prayed.

*He didn’t hear it, he didn’t hear it, he didn’t hear it...*

Two gazes collided across the sparse figures between them—

The fox-like eyes held a hidden smile, announcing an undeniable fact.

Soon after, she saw the man silently mouth a word.

"Calling me?"

chapters.title: Cat
chapters.content:
Si Qing’s face remained calm, but her heartbeat roared in her ears.

"Zhu Zhu, can you hear me?" She forced herself to calm down, deliberately raising her hand to emphasize the presence of the Bluetooth headset. "Put the book down somewhere first. I’m coming over now."

The subtext of this action was: I’m just on the phone, not calling you. Don’t get the wrong idea.

Qi Fang was so smart—he must have understood her meaning.

---

By the time she finished getting the book and returned to the dormitory, it was already 3:20. Tan Lexi had just gotten out of bed.

All freshmen across the school were scheduled to have a class meeting at 4 PM. The hallway echoed with shouts of "Hurry, hurry, we’ll be late!"

Footsteps filled the corridor as a group of people dropped their books and sprinted downstairs to grab shared bikes.

"Today’s been absurdly busy! Just biking cost me 7.50 yuan!"

"Who can compensate me for this absurdity?!"

A bitter complaint drifted up from the first-floor lobby.

Si Qing and Zhu Xing’s class was in Building 1. After turning out of the South District dormitory and crossing the road, they arrived.

The two found a corner seat.

Due to the homeroom teacher’s personal schedule, the class meeting was hosted by the class assistant, Ke Mingyuan. The originally planned election of class officers was also postponed until after military training.

Midway through, the homeroom teacher made a brief appearance. He was a middle-aged man with slightly thinning hair. Standing at the door, he gave a quick self-introduction, hastily picked a scapegoat from the roster to temporarily take charge, and then left again.

Si Qing, who was at the top of the list due to her entrance exam scores, was predictably chosen as the unlucky one—beautifully justified as "greater ability, greater responsibility."

"Greater ability↑, greater responsibility↓." Zhu Xing curled her lip, rolling her eyes so hard they nearly reached the back of her head. She looped her arm through Si Qing’s and ranted all the way from Building 1 to the Central Cafeteria.

The Central Cafeteria was a disaster zone of carbon dioxide, thanks to the freshmen swarming in like locusts, compounded by the new self-serve hotpot on the fourth floor. A single breath felt like it could knock you out from CO2 poisoning.

Cen Weiying had arrived early and secured a sofa seat by the staircase.

By the time Si Qing and Zhu Xing bought their milk tea on the first floor and reached the fourth, the hotpot was already on the table.

Tiny bubbles burst in the steaming broth, and Tan Lexi’s extra-spicy pot was particularly intense—just passing by her seat, Zhu Xing sneezed twice.

"Sichuan girl, terrifying indeed." Zhu Xing rubbed her nose and looked around. "Where’s Qiqi?"

Cen Weiying lifted her chin toward the staircase. "Isn’t she coming now?"

Tan Lexi took a big step up the last stair. "Our class’s selection of class officers took forever. I’m starving."

Si Qing inserted the straw into the milk tea and pushed it toward her. "Drink some red bean milk tea first to pad your stomach. Eating spicy food on an empty stomach can make you uncomfortable."

"Thanks, Qingbao." Tan Lexi sat down, catching her breath, then moistened her lips and blurted out everything she’d been holding in. "Guys, I just saw that ‘Best Actor’ senior on the road! It was the first time I’ve seen him standing—he’s got to be at least 190 cm tall! Those legs! Longer than my life!"

She snapped open a pair of disposable chopsticks, took a breath, and continued, "And when I passed by him, I could smell the scent of oranges. I almost asked him what perfume he was wearing. It was fragrant from miles away."

Hearing this, Si Qing tilted her head slightly.

She had also smelled a citrusy, fruity scent on Qi Fang today.

A crisp, slightly bitter grapefruit note mixed with a subtle hint of soap.

Clean, with a boyish charm.

"Speaking of which, someone on the forum was just discussing this." Cen Weiying pushed her phone toward Tan Lexi. "Here’s every brand Qi Fang is wearing from head to toe."

"From head to toe? That’s intense." Tan Lexi didn’t believe it at first, but when she looked down, her defenses crumbled. "What’s the big deal if there’s one more rich person in the world?"

[Next life, if I study fashion again, I’ll die: His perfume is LV’s *Après la Plage*, his outfit is Gucci’s 2024 Spring-Summer limited edition, and don’t even get me started on his watch—it’s worth my life. Don’t ask how I know. It’s basic knowledge for us fashion people.]

Cen Weiying bit her chopsticks and clicked her tongue. "I say, guys should really dress themselves up. Look at him—even if you can’t date him, just looking at him puts you in a good mood, right, Qingbao?"

Suddenly put on the spot, Si Qing’s lashes fluttered. She then curved her lips and nodded. "Right."

But not entirely.

Humans are greedy creatures.

Now that she stood at the door of Qi Fang’s world, she no longer just wanted to stand in the wind and admire the moon.

She wanted to keep the wind, to pluck the moon.

But before that, she needed to be ready to ring his doorbell.

---

Freshman military training began one week after school started and lasted for 14 days.

But before military training, they had to endure a series of relentless sessions: the freshman mobilization meeting, collective study and exams on freshman regulations, and a barrage of lectures on dormitory safety, water and electricity use, telecom fraud, and more, not to mention the student organization interviews.

For four consecutive days under the blazing sun, they crisscrossed the university to attend meetings in different lecture halls, as busy as some VIP.

And they hadn’t even started military training yet, but traces of African heritage were already showing.

"I’m gonna blow up the school!"

A loud crash of cosmetics being thrown came from Room 616 of the 25th Building’s female dormitory.

Cen Weiying, retrieving her dried clothes from the balcony, pushed open the door to see Tan Lexi slamming an empty sunscreen bottle into the trash can.

Because they had just received notice that class monitors and representatives had to go register files, Tan Lexi had a minor meltdown—until Si Qing returned with a large cup of fruit tea to soothe her.

At a little past 3 PM, Si Qing and Tan Lexi set off for their respective colleges.

The registration was centralized in Room 313 of the Management Building’s C section.

After entering, Si Qing pulled out her assigned file from the stack of manila folders on the mahogany table and found an empty seat.

The light streaming through the glass window softened from blinding to gentle. The people in the activity room gradually dispersed.

Si Qing had arrived a bit late, and with the Finance Department having fewer classes but more students, by the time she finished, she was the only one left.

From the counselor’s office across the hall came the sighs of a few young teachers.

"Five minutes before closing, and he remembers to call a meeting. Unbelievable."

"Well, looks like we’re not going home. Guess we’re staying in the dorm."

A childish voice piped up, "Mom, when are you coming back?"

"Xiaofeng, go play with the big brother on duty in 312 first. Mom will take you to buy cake later."

"Then I’ll wait for you. Hurry, okay?"

The footsteps gradually faded.

Si Qing tidied up the activity room, turned off the lights, and stepped out.

The light in neighboring Room 312 was still on. Occasionally, the sound of something rubbing against a leather sofa and a child’s complaints drifted out.

It was the boy who had been called Xiaofeng earlier.

"Big brother, why aren’t you waking up?"

"Big brother, are you even alive?"

"Big brother, you died from taking too many tonics."

In just three seconds, "big brother" was declared dead.

Si Qing stood by the door and peeked inside.

Xiaofeng was wriggling on the sofa, his head pillowed on the outstretched leg of the person next to him.

Light gray sweatpants, red and white basketball shoes.

She recalled someone who particularly favored such bright colors.

She tilted her head, her gaze shifting slightly, finally settling on the person who had just been declared "dead."

The young man had his arms crossed over his chest, his silver-white over-ear headphones draped around his neck in reverse. He leaned back against the sofa, eyes closed, chin lifted.

The sensual Adam’s apple in his throat was outlined by the white overhead light, falling unobstructed into her view.

Si Qing’s eyes curved slightly.

Qi Fang, like this, resembled a good-tempered cat exposing its belly—no matter how much you messed with him, he wouldn’t get angry, or perhaps he was just too lazy to.

She had always thought Qi Fang was like a kitten.

Noble, beautiful, aloof, with a strong curiosity and desire to explore.

Of course, that was only if he encountered a ball of yarn to his liking—only then would he bother to move.

"Big brother—play with me for a bit—"

Xiaofeng pouted, aggrieved, and tugged at Qi Fang’s sleeve.

Truly pitiful.

Si Qing raised her hand toward the little boy, suppressing her voice. "Xiaofeng."

The child’s ears were sharp. He turned at the sound and saw Si Qing.

The two exchanged silent glances, agreeing to go to Room 313 to play. Si Qing went ahead to turn on the lights.

Qi Fang noticed the weight on his leg disappear. As he opened his eyes, he caught a fleeting glimpse of a light-colored skirt hem at the doorway. His brows twitched imperceptibly.

Then his gaze shifted to Xiaofeng, who was pulling toys out of the duty room cabinet. "Where are you going?"

The little boy, arms full, lifted his chin toward Qi Fang. "I’m going to play."

The light from Room 313 next door spilled through the frosted glass partition above the cabinet.

Qi Fang withdrew his gaze and asked again, "With whom?"

"With the pretty sister." Xiaofeng trotted toward the door, then suddenly remembered something. He turned back and added, "A super pretty sister, okay?"

The child’s intentions were not hard to guess—he simply wanted Qi Fang to come along.

He closed his eyes, shifting into a more comfortable position and settling back into the sofa.

"Not going."

---

chapters.title: Little White-Eyed Wolf
chapters.content:
The TOEFL listening section ended. Qi Fang lifted a finger to remove his headphones, then casually picked up the Rubik’s Cube Xiaofeng had left on the table. He idly scrambled it and solved it again.

"Sister, did you lose on purpose?" came the child’s laughter from next door.

"You’re just too smart, Xiaofeng."

In the neighboring room, Xiaofeng collected the chess pieces from the score sheet and sorted them by color.

"Sister must be smarter than me. Mom said that all the brothers and sisters who get into this school are the smartest."

"And the hardest-working," Si Qing helped organize the pieces. "Sister falls into the latter category."

"Then Sister is still the most amazing!" The boy’s eyes sparkled. "Sister is the prettiest girl I’ve ever seen, besides Mom!"

Si Qing could easily tell from Xiaofeng’s words and mannerisms that this child had grown up surrounded by plenty of love.

Polite, well-mannered, and good at expressing himself.

"You’re the cutest child Sister has ever met." She smoothed out the score sheet and asked gently, "Want to play another round of Gomoku?"

The boy’s dark eyes flickered for a moment. He had assumed Sister would only play with him for a little while before leaving.

He had even prepared himself to play alone, but he hadn’t expected Sister to stay.

"Yes!"

The two happily started their second game.

Halfway through, Si Qing fell into deep thought.

Controlling the score really wasn’t easy—before she knew it, she had played herself into a position where every move led to victory.

As she pondered whether to place her piece in the corner, a hand with distinct knuckles reached over from behind her, scooping several white stones from her side of the bowl.

A crisp grapefruit scent tickled her nose. She could feel the back of her chair being leaned on by someone.

Qi Fang pinched a stone between his fingers and, without ceremony, placed it on the path she had laid out for certain victory.

"Checkmate."

Then he placed another stone in a second spot. "Checkmate."

Another. "Checkmate."

And finally—

"Checkmate."

Xiaofeng: (╯°□°）╯︵ ┻━┻

Si Qing: 1261·09610338 Thank you, Your Majesty, for the thorough humiliation.

When it came to making someone lose face, this man truly stood alone at the peak.

The little boy tilted his head, full of grievance.

Qi Fang gave him a cold glance, nudging the leg of Xiaofeng’s office chair with his shoe.

"Make some room for me, kid."

Xiaofeng pointed to the empty space on his other side. "Big brother, you can sit here."

Qi Fang didn’t respond, his lashes lowering to hide his expression.

Si Qing guessed he was too lazy to move.

She shifted to the adjacent chair, leaving the middle seat empty. With a slightly upturned tone, she hummed in agreement, signaling he could sit.

Qi Fang pondered the girl’s tone as he pulled out the office chair and sat down, his fingertips tracing the edges of the Rubik’s Cube in his hand.

Talking to him like he was a child.

"Big brother—" Xiaofeng pouted pitifully, "You pushed Sister so far away. How am I supposed to play with her now?"

At his words, Qi Fang glanced at the distance between himself and Si Qing.

There was enough space between them to fit a Mixue Bingcheng.

Si Qing heard Xiaofeng and was about to move closer, but Qi Fang’s gaze suddenly swept over. She froze.

He had deep-set eyes with thin lids.

When he looked up at someone, his brow bones created shallow dimples, making his eyes appear like large double eyelids at first glance. That’s why Si Qing had been surprised to discover he was actually a single eyelid.

After a moment, as if thinking of something, a small dimple suddenly appeared at the corner of his lips.

Qi Fang stretched out his legs, hooking the leg of her chair and pulling her closer.

"Little brother wants you closer, Sister."

The distance shrank abruptly, and the hidden smile in his voice was unmistakable.

"Okay." Si Qing lowered her lashes.

Her eardrums were filled with the sound of her own heartbeat.

Xiaofeng, lying on the table, stared at the two of them before suddenly saying, "Big brother, Sister is mine. You’re too old, so you should call her little sister."

He remembered Si Qing had mentioned earlier that the big brother on duty in Room 312 was a senior.

A senior meant someone older. He knew that.

Qi Fang seriously doubted his own ears.

He was only nineteen, and already old?

Then in a few years, he’d be ready for cremation.

He laughed in exasperation. "What? Didn’t catch that."

"Big brother, when you’re old, you get hard of hearing. I just—mmph!"

Qi Fang pinched the boy’s soft cheek with one hand, rubbing it up and down. "Repeat it. Big brother doesn’t like hearing that."

"Gug... guh... stop squishing me, I... I won’t..."

Qi Fang had no temper with children and was easy to coax.

"You say, ‘Brother Qi Fang is the handsomest person I’ve ever seen besides Dad,’ and Big Brother will forgive you."

The child sniffled and obediently repeated the words.

Si Qing found the phrase strangely familiar.

Ah, right—earlier, when she and Xiaofeng were chatting here, he must have been listening from next door.

Not only had he heard, but he had memorized every word.

She couldn’t help but curve her lips into a smile.

And she managed to suppress it before Qi Fang noticed.

Si Qing had always felt there was an indescribable steadiness to him.

Rational, meticulous, with a youthful spirit and just the right edge, as well as a hidden tenderness beneath his pride—every aspect of him struck a chord with her.

And today, she discovered that he could be adorably childish too.

Qi Fang didn’t miss the fleeting spark of amusement in the girl’s eyes.

He didn’t know whether to call her foolish or what.

Laughing at him behind his back—how was that different from shouting into a microphone?

And she still thought she was hiding it.

Qi Fang pulled out the Monopoly board, rolling it into a cylinder between his thumb and forefinger. He tapped it lightly against the back of the girl’s hand resting on the table. "Laughing at me, Si Qing?"

Si Qing froze.

This was the first time she could recall him calling her by name.

The girl’s eyes were watery, brimming with fragmented light, just staring at him without a word.

Qi Fang’s fingertips, holding the paper tube, went slightly numb.

"Oh, so Big Brother knows Sister?"

Xiaofeng cupped his chubby cheeks with both hands. "Then why did Sister say you don’t know each other?"

"Huh?"

Qi Fang’s gaze shifted to her. Si Qing gave an awkward smile, asking him, "Do we count as knowing each other?"

She couldn’t gauge Qi Fang’s boundaries, so she couldn’t define it.

"...Wow."

Qi Fang had never known before that extreme speechlessness could make a person laugh.

He spun his phone in his hand for half a turn before unlocking it.

Xiaofeng saw him open the dialer interface and tilted his head. "Big brother, who are you calling?"

"The Wildlife Protection Bureau." He dropped the words coldly.

"Did something happen?"

The girl leaned slightly toward him, her scent reaching his space first.

A faint woody fragrance with a hint of mint.

He glanced sideways at the ends of her hair, which had fallen onto the armrest of his chair.

Dark chestnut, shimmering softly like silk under the light.

His fingertips unconsciously rubbed the edge of the phone’s power button.

He stared for a while before picking up her question.

"There’s a little white-eyed wolf on the loose."

chapters.title: Pretty Nice
chapters.content:
Si Qing looked up, and he was gazing down at her, their faces only about ten centimeters apart.

His dark eyes were deep and expressive, yet revealed no emotion.

But she could tell— the little white-eyed wolf was talking about her.

Realizing the distance might be crossing a line, she slid her chair back a bit before responding, "I'm not a white-eyed wolf. I remember you."

The girl's voice was clear and gentle, with a soft, almost coaxing tone whenever she spoke.

Watching the subtle way she had shifted away, Qi Fang reached out and pressed his hand against the back of her chair.

"No school gate to stop you, and you'd slide right out of the country."

Si Qing: "..."

*In her mind: If he keeps licking his lips while eating, he might get poisoned by me.*

While the two of them stared at each other, Feng Feng had already laid out the Monopoly board.

Children’s enthusiasm came and went quickly. Halfway through the game, he found it boring, so he dug through his backpack, pulled out a sketchbook, and tugged Si Qing into drawing with him.

Qi Fang leaned back in his chair, spacing out. A few light laughs drifted over, and his gaze naturally settled on the little girl in front of him.

Her neck, half-hidden by her hair, was fair and slender. The thin, pale blue knit sweater revealed the delicate outline of her collarbones and the faint shape of her shoulder blades.

She seemed to have lost a lot of weight and grown taller.

He remembered seeing her once before— she had been wearing Shanyi High School’s winter uniform, small and standing there like a little thermos.

A red thermos, festive and cheerful.

Perhaps without the uniform suppressing her personality, a realization quietly formed in his mind—

"Brother, look at the bird I drew!" Feng Feng turned around, holding up his sketchbook to show him.

"Pretty nice."

Feng Feng hugged his drawing, puffing his cheeks as he glanced at Qi Fang. "You didn’t even look and you already said it’s nice. You’re just humoring me."

"Wronged." Qi Fang pinched the boy’s cheek. "Brother didn’t say *your* drawing was nice."

The child thought for a moment, then let out a wail, accusing, "Sister, Brother said my drawing was *ugly*—"

Si Qing, her sleeve tugged by Feng Feng, leaned closer. "It’s very nice. Brother’s just teasing you."

She said, "Brother likes teasing kids, especially cute ones."

As she leaned in, her black hair fell over the boy’s distinct, refined knuckles. She didn’t notice at all.

Feng Feng pouted, "Brother, you’re bad!"

Si Qing only silently curved her eyes, unusually not responding to Feng Feng.

Qi Fang looked at the quiet girl sitting beside him, expecting her to join Feng Feng in teasing him.

"Aren’t you going to help your little brother scold me?"

The man’s lazy, smiling voice poked at Si Qing’s heart. She turned back. "Senior, your request is weird."

Qi Fang found the little sounds she occasionally made amusing, so he enjoyed teasing her.

"What’s weird about it?"

"..."

Si Qing could tell he was deliberately mimicking her, his tone laced with teasing or playful mockery.

She turned her face away, her voice slightly muffled. "Don’t copy me."

The strand of hair wrapped around his fingertip slipped away, and Qi Fang’s eyelids twitched.

It wasn’t until his gaze accidentally brushed over the faint red at her earlobe that he finally gave up on teasing her, letting out a low laugh. "Fine, I won’t."

After all, she was just a little girl— even when angry, she was gentle.

Twilight gathered the last of the daylight, and the orange-pink hue from the sky seeped through the windowpanes.

Si Qing glanced at the time on her phone screen— four minutes to 7:30.

At that moment, footsteps and a familiar sigh came from the hallway.

"In a meeting for an hour and a half, they said 'then' 74 times, 'ah' 62 times, 'must be implemented thoroughly' 55 times, and 'our backbone' 21 times."

"You’re just as idle."

So recording the verbal tics of leaders or teachers was a nationwide pastime, Si Qing thought.

As soon as Teacher Yang returned, she headed straight for her son. Seeing the light on in Room 313, she peeked inside.

At that moment, Feng Feng was carefully drawing a simple sketch with Si Qing, while Qi Fang, hand propping up his temple, watched with lowered eyes.

Teacher Yang was the counselor for the 2023 Business School class. She recognized Qi Fang. The girl next to him was probably the new student who had come to file her records that afternoon— she had seen her before.

Teacher Zhou, leaning on Teacher Yang’s shoulder, said, "Oh, Si Qing is still here?"

The three people in the meeting room looked over.

Si Qing gave a slight nod. "Hello, Teacher Zhou, Teacher Yang."

Feng Feng held up his newly drawn little rose and ran to his mother. "Mom, Sister taught me this— it’s all one stroke!"

Teacher Yang smiled and ruffled Feng Feng’s hair, then looked back at the two of them. "Has Feng Feng been giving you trouble?"

Si Qing’s eyebrows curved slightly. "Feng Feng’s been very good."

Teacher Yang noticed that the boy sitting next to Si Qing had been staring at her the whole time without saying a word.

Counselors also loved gossip in their free time. The teachers in the Law School and Business School basically all knew Qi Fang.

Good grades, good character, ambitious— he always brought back excellent results from competitions big and small.

And he hadn’t transferred to Business because of poor grades. In fact, his major grades were in the top 10%, and he had to pass the Business School’s final exams to be eligible for the transfer.

So he was the only one who had successfully transferred this year.

Moreover, this boy seemed to have bought property on the confession forums and walls.

Every day, people confessed to him, but he had never been seen with a girlfriend.

He was always surrounded by the same group of guys.

Today was different, though.

Teacher Yang glanced at the two of them, pondering for a moment.

How was she supposed to know that Qi Fang had been spacing out the whole time?

Because of those expressive eyes, Teacher Yang couldn’t help but feel he had taken a liking to the girl.

"Good thing the Western restaurant hasn’t closed yet."

Teacher Yang cleared her throat. "Qi Fang, as a senior, if your junior needs anything, take good care of her. We’ll be leaving now."

Considering she shouldn’t ignore the girl’s feelings and blindly set them up— besides, young people had their own pace— she left it at that.

After saying her piece, the two teachers took Feng Feng back to the office to pack up.

Silence returned, save for the faint hum of the central air conditioning.

"Does the junior need anything?"

The boy’s bangs hung obediently over his forehead, his sharp, refined features softened by the warm white light. His eyelashes cast a small shadow.

She had heard him talk to others before— always in this tone. She knew he occasionally spoke like this, a little sticky.

Of course Si Qing wanted to spend more time with him, but his question wasn’t easy to answer.

She couldn’t tell if Qi Fang was asking out of sincerity or just being polite.

After a moment’s thought, she stood up first, putting her phone back in her bag. Then she looked down at him. "Senior, where is the Western restaurant?"

Her implication was: *Are you giving directions, or going together? You choose.*

Not wanting to overthink, she simply threw the question back to him.

The girl’s tone was light, but Qi Fang somehow detected a hint of coquettishness in it.

Not the kind that came from deliberate flirtation, but rather an innate, almost unconscious charm that made people want to take care of her.

She gave off strong little sister vibes.

The mischievous part of his nature was stirred by her.

"Asking for directions, or do you want to go together?"

chapters.title: Bad Egg
chapters.content:
Good news: He understood her meaning.

Bad news: He pretended he didn’t.

Si Qing scraped her nail against her knuckle.

They said no spirits after the founding of the nation, but here was a fox!

Engaging with this man was risky— without a stable core, you could be completely at his mercy in no time.

True, Qi Fang was outstanding, but she now stood on the same ground as him. She had the confidence to be a little more assertive in front of him.

She liked him, but she wouldn’t let herself be controlled.

Si Qing said softly, "Directions."

Qi Fang raised an eyebrow. "For directions, use Gaode Maps. Seniors don’t do that."

"..."

Meaning he had intended to go together all along and was just teasing her.

Si Qing had a little vengeful streak too. Instead of engaging, she smoothly opened Gaode Maps.

"Then what does Senior want to eat? I’ll bring some up for you."

Her deer-like eyes were dark and clear, looking genuinely sincere.

—Assuming Qi Fang hadn’t caught the flicker of mischief in her gaze.

Should he say, as expected of someone from a province known for civil service exams?

She had social skills down to a T, leaving no room for him to get upset.

Qi Fang let out a soft laugh. "You’re doing it on purpose."

Si Qing curved her eyes slightly.

A moment later, her gaze followed him as he stood up, his movement blocking out the light in front of her.

"Bad egg." The words were so soft that Si Qing only barely made them out by reading his lips.

He lowered his eyes, tilting his chin toward the door. "Let’s go. Together."

Si Qing lowered her lashes, crisply responding with an "Okay," and turned to walk in front of him.

Just like a cat, she thought.

A couple of meows, and even if he didn’t mean it that way, it sounded like he was being coy.

She bit her lip to steady her steps, trying not to let him catch even the slightest flaw.

---

The Western restaurant was on the first floor of Zone A. Taking the elevator down from Zone B, they emerged right in front of the restaurant’s back door.

As soon as the two stepped out of the elevator, they heard two boys gagging as they walked out of the Western restaurant.

"Everyone who eats here has such a tight lip... How come no one mentioned that the sauce for the Italian meat sauce pasta is fermented bean curd?!"

"I thought the red on the steak was myoglobin, but it turned out to be red-fleshed dragon fruit juice."

Qi Fang usually relied on Tang Youmin for meals, so he had no idea the Capital University had such bizarre dishes.

Si Qing was wondering if she could stomach something so sinister when she was suddenly pulled back to her senses by a clear, magnetic voice.

"Over here."

As he spoke, the man behind her pressed his upper abdomen against her shoulder.

It was just a brief touch, and before she could react, she was already being led away from the Western restaurant.

Si Qing looked up. "Where are we going?"

Qi Fang casually averted his gaze. "Let’s go out to eat. See what you want."

Si Qing opened a food delivery app and searched for restaurants near the school. She finally settled on a well-reviewed beef donburi place near the North Gate.

The clouds drifted slowly, the last trace of light at the horizon blurred into a deep blue, dotted with fragments of stars.

A warm summer breeze carried the scent of laurel, and Si Qing turned her head slightly toward the man beside her.

His bangs were lifted by the wind, and the light danced across his hair and lashes.

His fingers were slightly curled around his phone, his knuckles delicate and sensual. His fingertips tapped lightly on the screen, as if he were messaging someone.

Qi Fang seemed quite busy.

Si Qing clasped her hands behind her back, her gaze wandering, blinking in disbelief.

Although the North District was a bit remote, university students had plenty of free time.

It wasn’t that late, so it was strange that there were barely any people around.

After a moment, her phone buzzed in her bag. Tang Lexi was frantically posting videos in the group chat.

【Crazy Week (4)】

*Want Some Late-Night Snacks*: "There’s a street dance performance by the Dance Club at the West Campus field. Wanna come join the fun? @cc @Shan Qing @Zha Zha Zha Zhu"

No wonder there was no one around the North District— everyone had gone to the West Campus field.

*cc*: "Let’s go! Zhu and I are just changing clothes! Where’s Qingbao?"

Si Qing lowered her head to type: "Qingbao needs to solve the food problem first. At the North Gate. Any orders, princesses?"

*Want Some Late-Night Snacks*: "shake head.jpg I bought turkey noodles. Wanna try some tonight?"

*Shan Qing*: "nod.jpg"

*Zhu Xing*, who was on a diet, painfully typed: "Not good! Sour! Stinky!"

*Want Some Late-Night Snacks*: "Ah... Suddenly really want lo mein. Maybe we should have that for late-night snack instead."

*Shan Qing*: "nod.jpg"

*cc*: "Your uncle spoils her dad @Shan Qing"

After Qi Fang finished handling the messages in the innovation and entrepreneurship group, he lifted his gaze and saw the slight bulge in Si Qing’s cheeks beneath her bangs, as if she were smiling.

Her features were soft, the light from above spilling down, even revealing the fine fuzz on her face.

For no reason, he thought of the day she registered, when a few girls had pinched her cheeks.

She hadn’t gotten angry, just stood there letting them tease her.

He rubbed his fingers together and said softly, "Si Qing."

Si Qing turned off her phone. "What?"

The smile in her eyes was gone.

"Nothing."

Si Qing was speechless. *Even children don’t tease people like this.*

Little did she know, he had just used her to test a hypothesis.

Qi Fang had discovered that Si Qing’s guard varied depending on the person.

For example, around him, her guard was heavy.

To the point where, every time she looked at him, her reaction was occasionally a second or two slower.

She would first stingily hide the liveliness in her eyes, then give him a calm and proper glance.

Like a human-machine.

But after thinking it over, he decided that it was a good thing for a little girl to be cautious around strangers.

After all, he wasn’t exactly a good person.

---

From the North Gate, a left turn led to the restaurant.

As the two of them approached, the young woman at the entrance thoughtfully held the door open.

The glass wind chime on the eave tinkled.

"Welcome→to→"

The young woman’s gaze followed them. If it weren’t for her damn professional ethics keeping her manners in check, she would have sighed "national treasure" three times by now.

What an authoritative pair of faces.

The girl had a straight and slender figure, a delicate neck.

Dark hair, fair skin, bright eyes, dark eyebrows, a straight nose, cherry lips— her side braid hung loosely, and her temperament was gentle and detached.

One glance and you knew she was a beauty. Two glances, and she didn’t even seem human— more like a fairy.

As for the man following behind her—

It felt like the ceiling height of their restaurant was a bit cramped for him.

Probably because his top-tier, intense features were too striking. His expression was blank, yet it seemed like "don’t touch me" was written all over his face.

Cold-faced, kingly aura, devastatingly handsome.

She craned her neck, observing and imagining.

Soon, the two reached the entrance to a private booth. The fairy-like young woman turned to him. "Is this okay?"

The man’s coldness melted away, his eyes warming considerably. "Okay."

Sparing with words, yet putting on a dramatic transformation.

Like he was waiting for his wife to look at him.

Look, look.

He was completely under her spell.

chapters.title: Spoiled Like This
chapters.content:
Just then, the store was playing *Addicted*.

The melody was lazy and ambiguous.

Warm-toned lights enveloped the two tall figures in the interplay of light and shadow.

The essence of shipping lay in how a single glance, paired with different background music, could be interpreted in countless ways.

With faces this good-looking, who cared if they were dark or fair—everything could be imagined as... something else.

But in reality, the two of them were so unfamiliar they had nothing to talk about.

From ordering to the food arriving, they barely exchanged a few words.

Si Qing and Qi Fang simply had too few common topics, and Qi Fang’s thoughts were a bit scattered.

Every time he said something, she had to think for a while before responding.

Before replying, she always had to consider whether it was appropriate, if it would be boring, or if it would reveal something.

Cautious and uncharacteristic, yet she had no choice.

After all, the person across from her was Qi Fang—a master of social manipulation.

What made him formidable was that he didn’t put on the distant, untouchable air of a young master, yet he could precisely control social distance—neither too close nor too distant.

Lost in thought, Qi Fang’s phone on the table vibrated.

Her shoulders subtly trembled, as if caught daydreaming. She unconsciously lowered her head and took a sip of tea.

Under the warm yellow light, the girl’s rounded ears glowed with an unmistakable blush.

Qi Fang silently stared for a moment.

Si Qing noticed his gaze, her scalp tingling. She muttered, “What’s wrong?”

“Nothing.”

A moment of silence.

Seeing that he had already placed his chopsticks neatly back on the rest, Si Qing casually changed the subject, “Are you full?”

The transition was too abrupt. To Qi Fang’s ears, it carried a hint of reproach.

Did she think he was staring at her?

“You think I’m full and have nothing better to do?”

He found that explanation perfectly reasonable.

“…Huh?”

Si Qing hadn’t realized the ambiguity in her words.

She raised her pitch by two notes, “I didn’t mean that.”

Qi Fang leaned back against the chair, his dark eyes cold. “Oh, so you’re scolding me.”

Her eyes widened slowly, but fearing he’d think she was glaring, her lashes drooped. She hugged her teacup, swaying her head slightly.

After who knew how long, Si Qing heard a faint rustle of fabric from under the table. She glanced sideways.

Qi Fang stretched out his long legs, his shoe tip pressing against the base of her side of the sofa. His knee swayed idly a couple of times.

It seemed like he simply found the seat cramped and was stretching his legs to relax.

But she ended up subtly enclosed in a tiny space.

“Feeling wronged?”

A subtle, unfamiliar warmth lingered and spread across her back, sending a jolt of electric tingles through her spine.

She didn’t change her posture, cupping the teacup with both hands. Her clear, dark-rimmed deer-like eyes, veiled by the rising steam, shimmered brightly. “No.”

Her heart rate climbed tirelessly under his indifferent gaze.

Qi Fang tapped her side of the sofa with his shoe. “Then why scold someone and not even coax them afterward?”

This man seemed completely unaware of how overwhelming he was.

But the conversation had finally gotten going. If she argued further, they might run out of things to say.

Si Qing pressed her lips together and softly asked, “Senior, are you upset?”

Qi Fang’s gaze fixed on her.

After a pause, he neither confirmed nor denied, “Say something nice, and I’ll forgive you.”

Si Qing’s lashes fluttered. “But you must have heard plenty of compliments already.”

A person like him, praised wherever he went—his ears must have been softened by flattery long ago.

Did he really need her unoriginal words?

“You won’t even let the top scholar of Mountain City compliment you?”

“…” How did the news about the Mountain City top scholar even reach him?

Si Qing wasn’t good at complimenting people. The words usually used to describe Qi Fang were simple and blunt—top male model, max-level demon charm—too exaggerated.

What fresh, elegant praise hadn’t he already heard?

She puffed out her cheeks slightly. “Does complimenting the capital’s top scholar require credentials?”

Qi Fang lazily lifted his gaze. “You know quite a lot.”

“Your interview video was played on a loop at the entrance of Mountain No. 1 for a month and a half.”

A 25-minute video, stitched together from several post-exam interviews.

It was clear that Qi Fang had given many interviews back then. By the latter half of the video, his impatience was visible.

When the host asked for his secret to becoming the top scholar, he went from initially thoughtful responses to eventually slouching back on the sofa—
