Si Qing leaned back, mimicking the scene from the video. “As long as you have hands.”

Qi Fang’s long lashes lowered as he let out a soft laugh.

She was still just a little girl—no matter how casually she carried herself, her voice remained consistently soft and gentle.

So cute.

Si Qing curved her lips slightly, seeing that he was appeased. She fell silent, saying no more.

It was nearly 8:15 when they finished eating. Qi Fang went to pay, and while Si Qing waited for him outside, Tan Lexi sent her a WeChat message asking when she’d be back.

After replying with a simple update that she was safe, Si Qing put her phone away and closed her eyes to enjoy the breeze.

The late summer wind was always gentle, carrying a hint of moisture as it brushed past her cheeks—very comfortable.

The evening breeze lightly stepped on the clouds, and the leaves of the street trees rustled in the wind.

Until the wind chime under the eaves swayed, she slowly opened her eyes. From the corner of her vision, she caught Qi Fang’s profile.

Once, even the tiniest connection with him had been enough to make her day.

And now, he stood within her sight.

“Let’s go.” He turned his head.

Si Qing made a soft “oh” sound, secretly curving her lips, and quickened her steps to follow him.

As they reached the school gate, Qi Fang took a call.

She couldn’t tell what was said on the other end, but his expression didn’t look good.

At the end, he glanced at Si Qing briefly.

Si Qing vaguely felt that the call might be from someone she knew.

“Is it Tang Youmin?” she asked.

“Mhm.”

Si Qing and Tang Youmin had a distant familial connection. Qi Fang had no intention of hiding it from her. “He wants me to pick him up from the police station. He didn’t say why.”

Si Qing clenched the straps of her backpack, taking a long while to snap out of her daze. A thin layer of sweat formed in her palms. “The police station?”

She confirmed again.

“Don’t worry, he sounded fine.”

He turned slightly, bending a little to meet her gaze. His voice, rarely this soft, said, “I’ll take you back first. He can explain to you later.”

The little girl was timid and nervous—she must be scared.

Si Qing lifted her head. “Senior, I’ll go with you.”

Her moist, deer-like eyes, brightened by the humidity, collided directly with his.

That pitiful look genuinely made his scalp tingle.

The two of them turned back toward the school exit.

Si Qing had a small habit—when flustered, she tended to overthink.

“The police station is far from the school? Is it easy to get a taxi at this time?”

She’d heard that rush hour in the capital lasted a long time, making it difficult to hail a cab even as late as 8 or 9 PM.

She had just opened the ride-hailing app when she realized she’d forgotten to ask which police station Tang Youmin was at.

Anxious and flustered, she carelessly stepped on the edge of the automatic sliding door’s track. Her vision blurred as she stumbled.

Almost simultaneously, a warmth not her own pressed against her back.

A crisp grapefruit and pomelo scent enveloped her.

Qi Fang’s palm supported her forearm, steadying her.

Si Qing exhaled shakily, still catching her breath.

The girl’s thin shoulders trembled slightly. Small as she was, leaning against him gave little sense of weight—soft, as if boneless.

Qi Fang’s gaze paused, then slowly settled on her.

How could someone be so…

---

chapters.title: She Will Catch Up to Him
chapters.content:
“It’s to pick someone up from the police station, not to bail someone out. What are you so nervous about?”

Si Qing: “...”

He’d pinpointed the crux of her anxiety with surgical precision.

But for most people, the first reaction to hearing “police station” was exactly that. Si Qing was no exception.

Moreover, Uncle Tang—her stepfather—was very strict with Tang Youmin.

After all, as the elder brother, he had to prevent his younger brother from becoming a spoiled rich kid. Allowances could be cut off without warning.

Ever since Si Qing had known Tang Youmin, she’d known he was always tight on cash.

Later, when he started university, his family gave him a hot spring resort to manage as a trial.

Tang Youmin had a knack for business and worked hard. In less than a year, he turned around the nearly failing operation.

And then—he ended up in a police station.

The contrast was as stark as the Mariana Trench. Even O. Henry wouldn’t dare write such a twist.

As blood slowly circulated back, Si Qing regained her balance. “Sorry, I’ve caused you trouble.”

The weight on Qi Fang’s palm disappeared.

“The car’s booked. The police station is on Wutong Road, not far from the school. We’ll be there in ten minutes.” With that, he walked ahead, one hand in his pocket.

Si Qing was briefly stunned.

Just now, in her panic, she’d blurted out questions, and he had answered each one.

For a moment, the world seemed to lose all sound, leaving only the clear beat of her heart.

The wind carrying a faint citrus scent brushed past her.

Everything she could perceive emphasized Qi Fang’s presence.

Si Qing gripped her backpack straps and quickened her pace toward him.

The girl’s skirt, lifted by the breeze, formed beautiful folds. Her light steps concealed the heart of a fifteen-year-old girl.

“Senior.”

Hearing her, he stopped and turned to see the little girl running toward him.

“Did I walk too fast?”

“No.” The wind lifted her bangs, revealing her smooth, fair forehead. Her eyes and brows held a smile. “I can keep up.”

You don’t need to wait. I’ll catch up to you.

The warm white light of the streetlamp outlined two figures, subtly converging at a point.

---

One hour earlier, at the mediation room on the first floor of Wutong Road Police Station.

Tang Youmin sat in the corner chair of the mediation room, his gaze hollow as he watched two police officers take turns comforting the woman who had brought him to the police station.

According to his schedule, he was supposed to meet with investors that afternoon to secure funding for next semester’s activities.

But unexpectedly, the investor—a young woman—had looked at him as if he were a ghost. Without a word, she burst into tears, accusing him of ghosting her for two months in a cold, abusive manner.

It sounded like she had mistaken him for her online romance partner.

Thinking that this woman was a key figure in the student union, he patiently explained.

But then she pulled out a photo and asked, “Isn’t this you?”

This was absurd.

The person in the photo was indeed him.

But he truly didn’t know her.

Who could have predicted that when he said he didn’t know her, she would turn around and call the police, accusing him of fraud?

The amount involved was no small sum—120,000 yuan.

Bewildered, he was taken into the interrogation room and questioned for over twenty minutes while handcuffed to the chair.

Later, when they checked the IP address from the contact information she provided, they discovered that her online romance partner was indeed a notable figure.

He was the core member of a fraud ring that had been busted two months ago.

That scammer had used Tang Youmin’s photo to swindle her out of 120,000 yuan.

He thought that once his innocence was proven, the matter would be resolved. But then the woman pulled out a card and pressed it against his chest.

“I genuinely like you.”

As she said this, she even pinched his grandfather’s lover’s cheek. “If you’re with me, you’ll have plenty of money. Deal?”

Tang Youmin took a step back. “Please respect yourself.”

“We have feelings for each other. Are you just going to discard me like this?”

As she spoke, she started crying again, screaming and cursing him as a heartless man, pulling out all the stops—crying, making a scene, threatening suicide.

She even punched him twice. Furious but unable to retaliate, he could only take it.

Fortunately, two police officers eventually intervened, restraining her and arranging for him to sit in the corner.

Tang Youmin closed his eyes and pinched the bridge of his nose, then took out his phone to message Qi Fang: *Where are you?*

No reply.

Little did he know that at that moment, the guy was having dinner with a little girl.

The woman’s sharp cries occasionally echoed through the room. Tang Youmin raised a hand to rub his ear.

As he turned his head, his peripheral vision caught two figures entering through the back door—one in dark clothing, the other in light.

The dark-clad figure was a police officer in uniform.

The light-clad one leaned forward, about to look in his direction.

Tang Youmin’s gaze shifted slightly, just in time to meet a pair of searching eyes.

The girl was wrapped in a white towel, her hair clearly wet, with a few strands sticking to her cheeks.

Her small, oval face was fair and delicate, her features refined, and her eyes still held a lingering curiosity.

The moment he saw her face, Tang Youmin felt as if his heart had been viciously squeezed.

“Chen…”

A syllable caught in his throat, then faded as if he’d thought better of it.

His first love, who had unilaterally dumped him and disappeared without a trace, on his worst day, in a police station—

He had encountered her.

If he had to describe his current mood:

It was frustration upon frustration, with a touch of groundless annoyance.

He let out a slow breath. “Shen Shangyue.”

Tang Youmin didn’t miss the flicker of shock in her eyes.

Clearly, she recognized him.

Shen Shangyue blinked, slowly raising her hand after a moment of hesitation. “Hi?”

Her composure made Tang Youmin doubt for a second whether the person who had once been with him was really her.

“...”

The policewoman beside Shen Shangyue, seeing that she knew the young man in the room, helped her into the mediation room.

After seating the girl next to Tang Youmin, she pulled aside a colleague to discuss the situation.

chapters.title: Heartache
chapters.content:
"I was helping her look for a place to stay when we passed by here. I noticed she knew the boy in this house, so I thought I'd let them talk while I go verify the situation with the people who were there. If it was just an accidental fall into the water, not a suicide attempt, then we can let her go."

After a pause, the policewoman lifted her chin toward the woman who was crying and shouting about wanting to support Tang Youmin. "Why don't you take that lady next door to calm down? Officer Xiao Zhang said the room next door will be free soon."

Soon, a crowd of people bustled out, and she followed at the end. "I'll be outside. Call me if you need anything. Also, contact your family and friends to come over. There are some procedures to handle."

As she finished speaking, the door was gently closed.

The central air conditioning was running, sending cool air gusting over.

Tang Youmin glanced at the girl's hand, which was clutching the corner of a towel, shaking violently.

Shen Shangyue noticed the gaze from the person beside her and tilted her head slightly. "What's wrong?"

"Are you cold?" he asked.

The girl's eyes shifted subtly, and she curled up, clutching the towel. "A little."

"My spot has less wind. Let's switch."

Tang Youmin stood up and, by the way, called Qi Fang to come pick them up.

After hanging up, he saw that Shen Shangyue wasn't shaking as much, so he carefully asked, "Is there something troubling you?"

He had overheard a bit of what the policewoman said earlier.

"Hmm?" Shen Shangyue heard the subtext in his words and looked up. "Do you think I tried to kill myself?"

As she spoke, she pulled down the towel draped over her shoulder.

On her fair arms, several abrasions were a shocking red.

"A group of fishermen were setting up bait by the river. I stepped on their bait bucket, sprained my ankle, and fell into the river. I'm aching all over from the fall."

Tang Youmin unconsciously furrowed his brow. "Did you get it treated?"

She lightly hummed, "Just put some hydrogen peroxide on it. It'll be fine in a few days."

The young man's phoenix eyes lowered, his gaze falling on the long scratch on her forearm, dark and inscrutable.

Tang Youmin had a pair of very beautiful eyes.

His lower lashes were long, the shape of his eyes sharp and clean, but his gaze was soft.

Shen Shangyue stared at him for a while. "What's with that expression? It's easy to misunderstand."

He looked up. "Misunderstand what?"

"Misunderstand that you feel sorry for me." The girl propped her chin up and joked.

Her smiling voice fell into a sudden silence.

Tang Youmin's sympathy was far from overflowing.

Those extra questions just now were at most out of classmate camaraderie.

He wasn't so foolish as to fall for the same person twice.

Feel sorry for her?

"As if." He leaned back in the chair casually, lowering his lashes to withdraw his gaze.

...

When Si Qing and Qi Fang arrived, in the large mediation room, a man and a woman occupied two opposite corners of the conference table.

Tang was leaning back with his legs crossed, playing on his phone in the chair.

His relaxed posture was as if he were at his own home.

On the other hand, the girl in the white T-shirt across from him looked up first.

Shen Shangyue narrowed her eyes. "Qi Fang?"

She, Tang Youmin, and Qi Fang were in the same junior high school. She and Tang Youmin were in Class 2, while Qi Fang was in Class 1.

In the second semester of junior high, she had an outstanding performance and was admitted to Class 1, where she became Qi Fang's classmate for half a year.

But Class 1 was no place for humans. Everyone was like a study machine with almost zero social life. After several years, you might not even recognize all your classmates.

Among the freaks, the most outrageous was Qi Fang.

He was the kind of person who excelled in all aspects—morally, intellectually, physically, aesthetically, and in labor.

Later, he was suppressed to the point of being somewhat reclusive. When he dropped back to Class 2, Shen Shangyue even found the class teacher, who had a preference for boys over girls, to be rather handsome.

Si Qing followed behind Qi Fang. Seeing him nod slightly, she guessed they probably knew each other, so she didn't speak.

Tang Youmin asked him, "Do you know her?"

The man replied with a straightforward face, "No."

Tang Youmin rolled his eyes smoothly. "If you don't know her, why did you nod?"

Qi Fang glanced at him indifferently. "Are you jealous? Are we dating?"

He knew too many people. It wasn't strange that someone could call out his name.

Out of politeness, he gave a reaction.

Tang Youmin laughed and cursed at him, "You're such a flirt."

Qi Fang kicked his calf. "Si Qing is here too. As an elder, watch your language."

"?"

Tang Youmin's gaze swept around and finally landed on the white skirt hem behind him.

Qi Fang stood in such a way that he completely blocked her. He really didn't notice that there was another ancestor behind the ancestor.

After a moment, a small, fluffy head slowly peeked out. "Hi?"

Tang Youmin: ...

What was going on tonight?

One after another, they all greeted him with "hi."

"Do you have to follow too?" he asked.

Hearing Tang Youmin's voice, Si Qing took a small step forward from behind Qi Fang and explained, "I was afraid the police might call Tang Uncle, so I came to see the situation first. If you really did something wrong, I need to think of a countermeasure."

From her tone, it seemed she was going to cover for Tang Youmin.

Qi Fang glanced at her. "A good student like you is going to bend the rules?"

Si Qing shook her head. "I'm helping Tang Uncle pick a handy tool in advance. It'll save some effort when beating him up."

A light laugh came from the corner, then quickly stopped.

Shen Shangyue rested her chin on the table, holding back laughter until her shoulders trembled.

"Laughing?" Tang Youmin turned his head displeasedly.

She pouted. "Can't even laugh now? It's my mouth. Why are you so possessive?"

Tang Youmin scoffed lightly. "What possession could I have over your mouth?"

"..." Shen Shangyue's smile froze for a moment.

Back and forth, even though Si Qing and Qi Fang had just arrived, they could see that these two knew each other.

At this moment, the door frame was knocked twice, and the police officer walked in, taking someone to the next room to sign a settlement agreement.

Originally, Si Qing planned to follow, but Tang Youmin insisted on dragging Qi Fang along.

Under the pretext of not letting the girls take the blame.

Qi Fang glanced at him with dark eyes, probably knowing what he was calculating.

In the end, he still didn't say much and followed.

As a result, just as they stepped into the next room, the next second they heard a scream from inside the room.

The source of the voice was a woman sitting between two police officers, covered in jewelry, looking intently at Qi Fang.

Then she slowly took out a card and placed it on the table. "Money is not a problem. Be good to me, baby."

"I really like you."

The two police officers who had been persuading her for a long time: ...

In the past, life was slow, and one lifetime was only enough to love one person.

Now with 5G, in just ten minutes, she had fallen for two.

The rope always breaks at the thinnest part; fate toyed with the lecher.

Tang Youmin crossed his arms, leaning against the door frame. "If you've taken a fancy to him, you can't support me anymore."

Qi Fang lazily glanced at the idiot beside him and bit the tip of his tongue with his tiger tooth.

If he didn't kick his pants off tonight, it would be a waste of this bastard's swagger.

---

chapters.title: Go With Him
chapters.content:
After Qi Fang and Tang Youmin left, Si Qing found a nearby seat and sat down.

Soon, a policewoman appeared at the door and called Shen Shangyue over.

As the girl passed by, Si Qing accidentally noticed the stain on the back of her jeans, and her eyes flickered.

Then she stood up and followed behind, gently patting her shoulder.

"Do you have a sanitary pad?" Si Qing asked softly.

Hearing this, Shen Shangyue opened her eyes wide, took a breath, and shook her head awkwardly.

Probably because of falling into the cold water, her period had come early, and she wasn't prepared.

Si Qing understood and took off her outer jacket to give to her.

Considering that different people might be allergic to certain materials or brands of sanitary pads, she decided not to borrow from the policewoman.

"What brand of sanitary pads do you usually use? Mesh or cotton surface? I'll go buy some."

Hearing this, Shen Shangyue was stunned for a moment.

She was about to say it wasn't necessary, but then she heard Si Qing's voice again.

"The convenience store is nearby. It's not troublesome," she said with a slight smile. "And I have nothing else to do right now."

The girl's black eyes sparkled, and her smile was bright and warm.

Pure and kind goodwill always touched people's hearts.

Shen Shangyue didn't refuse anymore and reminded her to be careful on the way.

Si Qing bought the sanitary pads as requested and checked out just before her phone ran out of battery and shut down.

The bathroom on the first floor of the police station was under repair, so Si Qing and Shen Shangyue went to the second floor together.

Si Qing was originally a slow-warming person, but she couldn't resist Shen Shangyue's lively nature.

Along the way, the floodgates of conversation opened, and the two went from talking about Beijing's mung bean juice to the dragon fruit steak at the Peking University cafeteria.

It was then that Si Qing learned that Shen Shangyue was also a student at Peking University.

She was in the same junior high school and grade as Tang Youmin and Qi Fang. After graduating from junior high, she moved from Mountain City to Deep City, took a year off, and then started high school. Now she was one grade below them, the same as Si Qing.

Coincidentally, in the same month and year that Shen Shangyue left Mountain City, Si Qing moved from Deep City to Mountain City with her mother due to a job transfer.

The distance between girls was easily closed, especially when their life trajectories carried a touch of fateful missed connections.

The two walked down the stairs together, chatting about the club recruitment the next day. Just as they turned the corner, they bumped into Qi Fang and Tang Youmin coming out of the mediation room.

Standing still and waiting for them to approach, Si Qing asked, "Is it over?"

Tang Youmin hummed in response and casually glanced at the person beside Si Qing, who was looking everywhere but at him. "Is the unlucky one done too?"

The unlucky one: ...

Shen Shangyue puffed out her cheeks, not wanting to engage with him, but not wanting the atmosphere to be awkward. She reluctantly squeezed out a hum from her throat.

The four of them left the police station two by two.

Peking University was east of the police station, about a 30-minute walk away.

When they reached the wutong tree at the entrance, Shen Shangyue separated from the group, pointing in the opposite direction. "I asked the counselor for leave, so I won't go with you."

She explained, "I just moved into a new dorm today and haven't tidied up yet. I'll stay at the rented apartment for one night."

It was dark, and Shen Shangyue's phone was soaked and turned off. Si Qing was worried about her going alone.

Just as she was about to do something, she suddenly felt her fate being gripped by the back of her neck—

Qi Fang's fingers loosely hooked her backpack strap, exerted a little force, and pulled her back.

Si Qing's eyes still carried a trace of surprise as she suddenly collided with the deep, fox-like eyes behind her.

"You don't need to worry."

Qi Fang lifted his chin toward the person pretending to be dead beside him. "Shen Shangyue has someone to take her."

Just now, in the next room, he heard the police call her name and vaguely felt it was familiar. Combined with the faint sense of estrangement between the girl and Tang Youmin, he remembered who she was.

Tang Youmin finally realized that he was the "someone," which amused him.

After weighing it in his mind, he didn't refuse.

Business was business, but there was still some camaraderie left between classmates.

If he had to take her, so be it. It wasn't like he would lose a piece of flesh.

But as for Qi Fang—

"Didn't you just say you didn't know her? Now you remember?" he teased with a smile.

Qi Fang curled his lips. "I used to call her by that name for a while. You forgot?"

Tang Youmin: ...

He remembered. He remembered everything.

When he broke up with Shen Shangyue, it was during summer vacation.

At that rebellious age, he was obsessed with angsty literature.

Afraid of being beaten to death by his brother for drinking at home, he went to Qi Fang's place to drink.

According to Uncle Wen, who took care of Qi Fang at the time, after he blacked out, he often hugged Qi Fang and called out Shen Shangyue's name.

He said he didn't know why he always woke up with bruises on his body.

It must have been this bastard taking advantage of the chaos to hit him.

Back then, he was too young and stupid. His cringeworthy actions were beyond redemption.

Now, thinking back, it gave him goosebumps.

His entire life's black history was in Qi Fang's hands. If he wasn't careful, this guy would expose a bit of it.

Tang Youmin gritted his teeth and punched his shoulder. "Can you shut up? You're such a dad."

Qi Fang sidestepped to avoid it and sneered mockingly, finally taking mercy and falling silent.

After a while of silence, the atmosphere began to feel a bit awkward.

Shen Shangyue didn't want to waste everyone's time. She sighed lightly. "I live in the south of the city. It's not on the way..."

"It is on the way."

Tang Youmin glanced lightly at the coat tied around her waist, then looked away. "I'll take you."

He should take her, regardless of whether she was Shen Shangyue or not.

A girl having her period and falling into the water was standing right in front of him. He couldn't just ignore it.

"How about you help me call a taxi? I'll go back by myself."

Shen Shangyue didn't like to trouble others, especially not Tang Youmin.

"I said I'll take you." Tang Youmin flicked her forehead. "If you keep being stubborn, I'll hit you."

The boy's strength was great. Even if he held back, it still hurt a little when it landed on a girl's skin, but not much.

Shen Shangyue raised her hand to rub the spot and muttered softly, "Whether I'm stubborn or not, I still get hit..."

Tang Youmin didn't hear her. After taking a couple of steps, he remembered there were still two people behind him. "Are you two coming? After dropping her off, we can go back to school together."

"Okay." Si Qing was about to nod when she suddenly felt a warm touch on top of her head.

"No." Qi Fang said indifferently.

Tang Youmin, whose invitation was directly rejected: ?

Shen Shangyue, who suddenly encountered a sweet surprise: 636363

Si Qing, who was pressed in place and didn't dare to move: ...

The warmth of his palm seeped into her skin, spreading like wildfire through her limbs.

Her fingertips stiffened slightly, and she looked up to meet his gaze. "Aren't we going together?"

Good, her voice sounded normal.

As she lifted her head, the girl's soft hair brushed against his palm.

The texture was unexpectedly good.

Better than the belly of the neurotic cat at his home.

Qi Fang pressed her head again before slowly withdrawing his hand. "The counselor is checking the dorm at 9:40. They just notified us."

As he finished speaking, Si Qing raised her hand to look at her wristwatch.

It was five minutes to nine.

The warmth that had risen to her cheeks suddenly cooled down.

Was a surprise dorm check a Peking University tradition?

Or was Qi Fang teasing her again?

"Was it mentioned in the group chat?"

She took out her phone to check the notification, then suddenly remembered that her phone had been turned off since they left the convenience store. She felt a bit dead inside.

Qi Fang opened the group chat, pinched the edge, and turned it around before handing it over.

Si Qing took his phone with a mix of belief and doubt, lowering her eyes to scan it, and more or less figured it out.

He had opened the freshman group where the counselor wasn't present. Inside, the chat was lively, with no mention of a dorm check.

"Dancing on the playground was too fun! Everywhere I look, there are beautiful girls and handsome guys."

"Are the couple from the street dance club in our Business School? They look really good to my eyes."

"Is our Business School going to debut?"

"Swipe my campus card! Send them all to debut!"

Si Qing swiped a couple more times and finally confirmed that Qi Fang had just been talking nonsense.

She cursed him in her mind, completely unaware that Tang Youmin had already walked up behind her.

"Really checking the dorm?"

His sudden voice startled Si Qing. She jumped, and the phone almost slipped from her hand. Fortunately, she reacted quickly and grabbed it firmly.

"You walk without making any sound," she shrank her neck, not answering his question.

Tang Youmin frowned. "Oh, should I march and shout one-two-one?"

Si Qing: "Have you seen a doctor at the mental hospital?"

Tang Youmin: ...*%￥&#@

Qi Fang crossed his arms and lowered his eyelids to watch the show.

Who came up with this little thing called Si Qing?

Too interesting.

Watching her render Tang Youmin speechless, he pressed his tongue against his lower lip and asked her, "Was there a notification in the group?"

Si Qing saw the dimple on his cheek deepen, his teasing intentions obvious.

The only downside to having dimples was that it was hard to hide a smile.

Her gaze steady, there was a hint of emotion in her voice that even she wasn't aware of. "Did you say there was?"

There wasn't at all.

Qi Fang, trying not to laugh, said, "I said there was."

"So now you have to go with me."

chapters.title: Two Dogs
chapters.content:
The sky is vast, the earth is vast, but the Chairman is the greatest.

How dare she undermine him?

Before parting, Shen Shangyue asked Si Qing for his phone number.

"I'll definitely contact you as soon as I get my spare phone home! Wait for my WeChat, baby!"

Qi Fang's dark eyes shifted slightly, glancing at the word "baby."

"Okay."

The girl's cheeks flushed pink, her lashes curled with a smile, extending like a crescent moon from the corners of her eyes.

His eyebrows subtly lifted.

Can a girl call someone so intimately?

And she even said "okay."

Isn't she usually very guarded around strangers?

She and Shen Shangyue hadn't known each other for long either—today was the first time they met.

What about him?

They went to the same high school, had seen each other a few times, but in her eyes, he only qualified as "do we even count as acquaintances?"

Tsk.

Cold.

And double standards.

After saying goodbye, the four of them went their separate ways.

Outside the narrow alley of the police station, the sound of traffic began to seep into the wind.

The two of them walked to the main road intersection. Seeing Qi Fang stop to open his phone, Si Qing also stopped.

It looked like he was going to take a taxi back.

The time she could spend with him was running out.

Her lashes drooped, a hint of melancholy rising in her heart, when suddenly she heard his voice.

"In a hurry to go back?"

Si Qing looked up and said she wasn't.

On the way to the police station, she had told her roommate she would be back late.

Qi Fang lightly tapped his phone screen, as if replying to someone.

"Then take a walk?" His usual indifferent tone.

Just a simple question.

But to Si Qing, it was as precious as a star falling into her palm.

She tightened her sweaty palm, calmly agreeing.

---

On the way, they passed a convenience store, and Qi Fang went in to buy something.

While waiting for him outside, Si Qing encountered a chubby little Corgi.

It was yellow and white, with a docked tail, its little butt wiggling as it walked toward her.

Approaching with dignity, the little guy suddenly dashed forward, pulling the leash so hard that the owner—a young man—let out a classic Chinese exclamation of surprise.

"Ai wo cao."

The dog scurried over on its short legs, rubbing against her legs, its tail wagging fiercely, its face sweetly smiling.

Its dark, shiny eyes seemed to say: Human, pet my head.

Si Qing's heart felt as if it had been gently squeezed, her hand itching to touch it.

But since the dog's owner didn't say anything, she didn't dare move.

The young man, who had been pulled off balance, was about to give the dog a little "love education" when he looked up.

His yellow-and-white "deadpan mantou" (steamed bun) was staring wide-eyed at a girl.

The key point was—this girl was...

Huge, beautiful, and radiant!

Si Qing was so focused on the chubby little dog that she didn't notice someone was watching her.

Until she heard the owner speak.

"It wants you to pet it."

"Is that okay?" Si Qing looked up, her delicate brows and eyes tinged with a hint of expectation.

Seeing the young man nod, she neatly tucked her skirt and squatted down, poking the fluffy hair on the dog's head with her fingertips.

Seeing the dog whimpering and nudging into Si Qing's palm, the young man also squatted down, pressing the leash at the dog's neck.

"Pocky, don't bother Sister."

The dog let out a wronged whimper and sprawled on the ground, legs splayed.

The young man scratched his head and apologized to her, "Sorry, it's a bit too friendly. Did it offend you?"

Si Qing, amused by the dog, comforted it while looking up to reply, "No, Pocky is very cute."

The lingering smile in the girl's eyes hit him like a wave.

—And it was perfectly captured by someone inside the convenience store.

"..."

Qi Fang's tongue flicked against his canine tooth, unconsciously tugging at the corner of his lips.

The cashier, a girl, slowly packed his purchases into a bag, her movements slower than usual.

It was the first time she had seen such a handsome man in person, and she was a little nervous.

He was so handsome that even the coldest woman in the world would smile at his face.

"Hurry up." he said.

Oh my god, his voice was so nice too.

She sped up, handing over the shopping bag, "Here you go."

"Have a nice day."

"Not necessary."

The man coldly dropped that line, his long fingers hooking the bag, his long legs striding out of the store with a crisp step.

It wasn't until she watched him leave that she realized—

Did he just say "not necessary"??

What?! Is he not alive anymore?!

Meanwhile, Si Qing found herself in an unexpected dilemma.

The dog's owner said he had another cat at home that could do backflips, and he would send her a video someday.

The young man rubbed his nose, "So, do you want to add me on WeChat?"

As soon as the words left his mouth, Pocky seemed to see something and suddenly got excited, its short legs stepping backward in place, its dark eyes flickering.

The dog's owner followed its gaze and froze.

Then he looked back at his "deadpan mantou" with grievance—couldn't this dog stop liking beautiful women and handsome men? Such a flirt!

Si Qing's peripheral vision caught the flattened shadow on the ground, cast by the light.

Tilting her head, she turned around just in time to meet the indifferent gaze of the man behind her.

"You're back." She stood up and walked to his side, her eyes curving slightly. "I played with this dog for a while while waiting for you."

She rarely encountered situations where strangers suddenly asked for her WeChat, and she didn't handle it well.

In unfamiliar and confusing situations, people tend to lean toward what's familiar.

To the point that Si Qing didn't realize her unconscious closeness was actually a sign of dependence.

But Qi Fang noticed.

The girl's voice was soft, her smile sweeter than ever, and she wasn't avoiding him like he was a thief.

Using him as a shield against admirers, huh.

Qi Fang didn't expose her. "Which dog?"

Dog owner: Is there a second dog here?!

Si Qing thought she had blocked his view and took a step back.

"Here." She spread her palm toward the short-legged creature on the ground. "Its name is Pocky."

Qi Fang lowered his eyelids and glanced. "Oh, that one."

The young man crouching across from them felt something was off.

Why did their conversation imply there was another dog here?

He looked up, and at just the right moment, caught the other man's seemingly casual glance toward him. Finally, he got it.

Damn! So the second dog here is me, the single dog.

The magical attack hit home, more painful than a direct beating.

Annoyed as he was, he had to admit it was his fault for hitting on someone else's girlfriend first. He couldn't blame the other guy for the cold shoulder.

Being in the wrong, he accepted it.

An adult's dignity meant not exposing the truth, not lingering, and shamelessly pretending nothing happened before walking away smoothly.

After the young man left, Si Qing relaxed, letting out a soft sigh.

Qi Fang bent down to meet her gaze. "What's with the sigh? Can't bear to part with your little dog friend?"

The deep, fox-like eyes suddenly invaded her space. Si Qing instinctively leaned back, her body tensing. "No."

"Let's go, senior."

Qi Fang didn't miss her evasive movement.

This was the first time in his life he'd been used as a tool, and he didn't expect the user to be a carpenter—

Burning the bridge after crossing the river.

"Ungrateful."

Si Qing's cheeks had just returned to normal temperature when she heard him say that.

His voice carried a smile, but his expression was anything but.

The young man's eyes were cold and distant, the sharp, refined lines of his face exuding a hint of pressure.

"Used me to fend off admirers and then discarded me. Tell me, how can someone be so heartless."

Si Qing stared at him in shock, her clear, bright eyes taking a while to process that she was the so-called heartless one.

After a moment, she felt his fingertip touch her forehead.

Dry, warm, familiar yet strange.

A soft, light breeze rushed past her ears, mingling with the faint, low sound in the flutter of her heartbeat.

"Talking about you."

---

chapters.title: The Young Lady
chapters.content:
Qi Fang lightly tapped her forehead, then withdrew his hand as if nothing had happened.

Leaving Si Qing in emotional turmoil.

After teasing her so lightly, he casually walked away.

Who was the heartless one here?

She pressed her lips together, restraining the urge to glare at him, and spoke in her defense: "I didn't use you to fend off—"

Before she could finish, Qi Fang straightened up. "Repeat that. I don't like hearing it."

"..."

Sometimes, Si Qing really envied him.

If he heard something he didn't like, he could just make them take it back—only exhausting others, never himself.

He lived like an emperor.

She sighed helplessly. "Then what does Senior like to hear?"

"Does Senior have no name?"

Si Qing: "..." Was she stepping on a landmine already?

She took a subtle breath.

The strange yet unfamiliar freshness of addressing him by his name was hard to ignore.

"Qi Fang."

The girl's clear, crisp voice wafted over. Qi Fang's expression rarely went blank for a moment.

Simple as the two characters were, hundreds or thousands of people had called him that.

But none like her.

No hint of flattery, yet charming, purely attractive.

After a moment of silent contemplation, he gave a low "mm."

"This, I like hearing."

After saying that, he stuffed a power bank into the outer pocket of her small shoulder bag, then poked the little charm on her bag.

Si Qing's gaze flickered slightly, scanning the power bank in her bag, then curved her eyebrows at him in thanks.

If Qi Fang wanted to, he could take good care of almost everyone around him.

So even though Tang Youzhen always said he was a difficult master to serve, he still trusted and relied on him the most.

Being meticulous and considerate was in his bones, so she didn't think much of it.

Si Qing plugged in her phone and put both the phone and the power bank back into her bag.

No one spoke.

The street vendor's hawking over the loudspeaker and the occasional rustling of the plastic bag in his hand were amplified by the silence.

Si Qing lowered her gaze to the items in the shopping bag.

She recognized them—cigarettes.

A whole carton.

She remembered Qi Fang didn't smoke.

At least, he didn't used to.

Because they hadn't seen each other for a while, she only occasionally heard bits of news about him from Tang Youzhen.

Now that they had met, she couldn't help but wonder if something unhappy had happened to him in the years she had missed.

Lost in her thoughts about him, she didn't realize that the person in her mind had been watching her for a long time.

The girl kept staring at the bag in his hand, hesitating, her thoughts written all over her face.

"Something to say?" Qi Fang lowered his eyes.

Si Qing let out an "ah," her thoughts snapping back, the belated embarrassment of being caught creeping up to her eartips.

But she had no right to ask if he smoked or not.

What was her position here? Minding other people's business.

Si Qing knew this clearly in her heart.

"It's nothing, I just remembered a survey I read before." She said, "It's said that every cigarette smoked shortens life by 13.8 minutes. A pack a day means ten years less."

So you should take good care of your body.

Seeing her serious face trying to scare him, Qi Fang couldn't help but curve his lips.

So cute.

"You scared the wrong person." He looked at her, half-smiling. "I don't smoke."

The cigarettes were for Lu Yeti.

Qi Fang valued his life greatly. Apart from drinking a little at social occasions, he didn't touch any other bad habits.

He had understood a principle since he was a child.

—Living longer meant he could squander more of his dad's money.

With such a good life, how could he bear to die.

As they talked, the two of them had already entered the south gate of Jingda University.

A right turn led to a small path behind Building 25.

The path was lined with a wall of climbing roses, their light yellow buds clustering and drooping. During the day, many people came to take photos.

Si Qing had taken a couple when she passed by before, only to be fiercely roasted by Tan Lexi.

She said that if someone found Si Qing's phone and opened her photo album, they might think it belonged to a 50 or 60-year-old elderly person.

Si Qing didn't believe it at first, but after looking at her photos, she did.

A journalism major was indeed professional.

This place was scenic, bustling during the day, and even more so at night in a different way.

This was Qi Fang's first time witnessing the diverse species at the foot of the girls' dormitory building.

Every five steps, someone said, "Your hands are so small," every ten steps, someone asked, "Is this okay, baby?" and every fifteen steps, someone directly got a French kiss.

Tsk, the atmosphere.

Then he looked at the girl quietly walking beside him.

She looked extremely calm on the surface, but her ears were honest.

They were bright red.

"Thin-skinned." He sneered lightly.

"..." She didn't react like this when passing by others kissing. Wasn't he right beside her?

It was like enjoying a kissing scene between the male and female leads, but if a parent or someone you cared about was watching with you, you'd feel embarrassed and cover your eyes.

She didn't say anything, and Qi Fang didn't seem to have the intention to tease her further.

Building 25 was a freshman dormitory. Those who liked to go out were at the west campus field joining the fun, so the area in front of the building was unusually quiet.

The two of them walked to the side door. Si Qing looked up and smiled at Qi Fang. "Thank you for today."

Military training hadn't caused any trouble for the teaching assistants, so unless something unexpected happened, Qi Fang wouldn't participate in freshman activities.

They weren't in the same department, nor the same grade, and their major courses and general courses didn't overlap.

If they didn't take the initiative, opportunities like today might never come again.

She rubbed her thumb against the edge of her phone, and as she thought about what to say next, her throat felt dry.

"Let me treat you to a meal sometime."

She tried her best to ignore her increasingly rapid heartbeat, speaking naturally. "So, do you want to add me on WeChat?"

The intense tension pressed against her senses.

Her perception of time seemed to stretch indefinitely.

The few seconds she waited for his response were among the rare moments of tension in Si Qing's life.

Different from the tension of realizing the answer sheet wasn't filled in before the exam papers were collected during the college entrance exam, this time, she was uncertain.

Her chest felt as if it was stuffed with a cloud soaked in moisture, the steam spreading through every vein with a scorching temperature.

The last of her courage was being burned away when she finally heard his voice.

"Sure."

Qi Fang lowered his head and tapped his phone a few times, pulling up a green QR code.

A short sentence, delivered in his usual indifferent tone, was enough to make her feel like she had ridden a roller coaster.

Too torturous, this man.

She had just opened the scanning frame when Qi Fang, as if having second thoughts, said, "But."

Si Qing: "..." A line of lyrics suddenly flashed in her ears.

—What's wrong now, my young lady.

She first ignored his strange attempt to scare her, calmly and swiftly scanned the code, and sent the request before replying, "But what?"

"But I don't accept empty promises."

Qi Fang lazily lowered his eyelids, glancing at the verification message. It only had two simple characters: Si Qing.

"So, when is 'sometime'? Do you need to tell me now?"

chapters.title: Orange
chapters.content:
She asked him, "When do you want to?"

"Listen to me?"

Si Qing nodded. "You're busier. Whenever you're free."

He slightly lowered his head, meeting her upturned deer-like eyes.

She had grown much taller. Now she didn’t look like a warm thermos anymore—more like a small figurine.

His gaze shifted slightly, landing on her jet-black hair before adding a prefix.

A fluffy little figurine.

Qi Fang rubbed his fingers together, barely restraining the urge to ruffle her hair. "Then next time I catch you."

That made it sound like she was always avoiding him.

"What 'catch'?" Si Qing tapped the ground with her toe. "I’m not avoiding you."

The boy’s expression was indifferent, his deep and alluring fox-like eyes flicking up.

"Is that so."

He probably didn’t realize that when he was scheming, it was as if there was a big, fluffy tail swaying behind him.

Like a cat lowering its body and raising its tail before causing trouble.

Seemingly distracted, but ready to pounce at any moment.

Sure enough, as soon as he finished speaking, Si Qing saw his hand lift.

Pale, slender, with slightly raised knuckles—relaxed yet seductive.

A perfect combination of hand, leg, beauty, and intellectual attraction. A bundle deal even the biggest sales event wouldn’t dare offer.

The next second, a warmth slightly higher than her body temperature poured down as his palm precisely landed on her head.

He just held it there, no further movement.

Si Qing’s heart thudded heavily.

Instinctively, she wanted to shrink her neck and dodge, but a sudden thought made her abandon the idea.

Her intuition told her that Qi Fang was deliberately provoking her to dodge. If she did, she’d be playing right into his hands.

Then who knows what new role he’d assign her next.

After all, today alone, she had already been a wild animal escaping from a zoo, a vicious monster who cursed and glared at him, and a heartless woman who used him to block peach blossoms before discarding him.

When his prideful little temper flared, no amount of explanation would satisfy him. If he was displeased, he’d make her start over.

Though he was reliable most of the time, his childishness could be helplessly frustrating.

Qi Fang watched the little girl standing still, the dimples at the corners of his lips deepening. "Really not dodging?"

"Grown up." He ruffled her hair again before slowly withdrawing his hand.

"..."

Treating her like a ball of yarn, poking at her now and then.

But it had nothing to do with romance—pure hedonism.

Realizing this, Si Qing felt a little deflated.

On one hand, she was secretly pleased by his affection.

On the other, she couldn’t help but wonder: How could he be so intimate with a girl he didn’t even like?

Her emotions were like duckweed floating in mist—neither rising nor sinking.

An inexplicable discomfort.

"Senior, you should head back too." She said softly, "It’s getting late."

Then she noticed the boy’s pale, sensual Adam’s apple bob.

"Senior again? Don’t you know my name?"

"Qi Fang." Si Qing corrected herself smoothly.

She wanted to say goodnight but feared it might be abrupt. The words twisted at her lips. "Bye."

Qi Fang gave a low "mm" and tilted his head. "Go."

From the entrance of the South District, faint laughter echoed—probably from the West District’s field event ending.

Si Qing stepped into the dormitory, circled to the window by the first-floor water room, and propped herself up to secretly watch him.

The boy’s figure was relaxed, his shoulders broad, his steps as steady as ever.

It sounded exaggerated, but back in high school, just watching him walk could make many girls lose their hearts.

Qi Fang always carried an indescribable air of leisure—elegant, relaxed, effortlessly balancing everything.

This aura wasn’t something cultivated by noble birth; it was more like an innate refinement, absorbed and internalized over time.

She remembered that Qi Fang could play the guqin.

It was during her first year of high school. Someone had shown her an article from the school’s official account.

At that time, Si Qing didn’t know Qi Fang yet. She only occasionally heard her desk mate mention this senior from the West Campus.

His achievements were countless: winning Best Debater in the provincial debate competition for the school, leading the badminton team to provincial and national academic competitions, breaking school records, and more.

In short, he was a remarkable figure. Rumor had it that many students in the West Campus would visit the honor roll to pay respects before exams.

Even Si Qing, who usually paid no attention to such things, couldn’t avoid hearing his name.

Though the East and West campuses were only separated by a library, the two rarely interacted except during morning exercises and flag-raising ceremonies. Even meal times were staggered.

Moreover, the school’s strict discipline prohibited unnecessary cross-campus movement. Getting caught meant a demerit.

So, the freshmen in the East Campus were most curious about one thing: What did this legendary handsome senior from the West Campus actually look like?

Until one day, a well-connected classmate somehow obtained a photo of Qi Fang playing the guqin at the previous year’s school anniversary.

Though the angle was awkward—only capturing his side profile—it was far clearer than the blurry, mosaic-filled long shots from the official account.

The boy in white robes, fingers plucking the strings, exuded an ethereal charm.

At the time, this photo was as precious as wartime footage.

After all, bringing a phone into a school as strict as this was like smuggling contraband into a high-security prison. The person who managed it was either a master thief or a war correspondent.

Rumor had it that this "war correspondent" had been "captured" after taking the photo—his class teacher confiscated his phone, only returning it after he ranked in the top 100 of the grade.

To get his phone back, the war correspondent spent nearly half a year.

So, the moment he got it back, he immediately posted the precious image on the student forum, finally giving everyone a taste of last year’s "leftovers."

At that time, Si Qing was focused on entrance exams and didn’t have much energy to spare for this heavenly senior.

She only knew that the school assigned classes based on the first exam of each semester. If you didn’t rank in the top 60, you had no chance of entering the experimental class.

As her desk mate put it, her romantic feelings had been stolen by Principal Wang Baochang.

Principal Wang Baochang was their grade director, nicknamed "The Matchbreaker," a specialist in breaking up couples. No pair of lovers could escape his iron fist.

It was true that she hadn’t developed any romantic feelings back then, but to say she wasn’t curious about Qi Fang would be a lie.

Si Qing’s admiration for the strong drove her to want to know more about him.

After all, this was someone who could score full marks on the school’s self-designed math exams every time. She genuinely wanted to know what he ate to grow so capable.

However, from the start of the semester to the first monthly exam, Qi Fang was often away for competitions. She never had the chance to see him during flag-raising or morning exercises.

The more mysterious he was, the more her curiosity grew.

Until the volleyball league match hosted by Huayue High School at the end of September. The school was invited to participate.

The next day was the National Day holiday, and with the competition, the school simply arranged an afternoon of self-study.

Si Qing and two other girls from her class were chosen as spectators and took a bus to Huayue.

Huayue was a private school, newly built in recent years. Its facilities were far more advanced than those of the First High School. Upon arrival, they were first taken on a tour (ostensibly to show off).

Before the match started, there was half an hour of free time. One of the girls had brought a CCD camera and took photos along the way.

As a result, when they realized the match was starting in less than 15 minutes, they hurriedly crossed the entire school, taking shortcuts to the back of the gymnasium.

A few boys in black and red jerseys were washing their faces at a water fountain.

The path was narrow, only allowing them to pass single file. Si Qing was pulled along, running past them.

Several hurried footsteps came to an abrupt stop as the boy at the far end suddenly straightened up and turned around.

The next second, a crisp, refreshing scent filled her nose.

The smell of orange-scented laundry detergent.

---

chapters.title: The Brightest Person
chapters.content:
Si Qing’s forehead bumped directly into the boy’s chest. A muffled groan mixed with a soft, pained cry escaped her lips.

The girl pulling her wrist hadn’t reacted yet. Sensing Si Qing had stopped, she turned back and saw an imposing figure blocking their way—jersey number 8.

Judging by his height, he was at least a head and a half taller than them. At just over ten years old, he was already over 185 cm tall. His biceps, the taut muscles of his forearms, the veins faintly bulging on his clenched fists...

...He looked ready to throw a punch.

It was their fault for not watching where they were going. They had pulled Si Qing along too fast, causing her to crash into him.

The area behind the building was secluded, with few people around and no visible cameras.

If they got hit here, there would be no evidence to plead their case.

Her mind raced. She took a big step forward, rushing to Si Qing’s side and wrapping an arm around her, whispering, "Qingqing, don’t be afraid. If he comes at us, we’ll run. If we can’t escape, you drop to the ground, and I’ll cover you. Let him try to hit me if he dares..."

She felt the girl’s palm growing damp with sweat. Si Qing patted her hand reassuringly and said it was fine.

Then, from the corner of her eye, she noticed several tall figures approaching from behind—probably the boys who had been washing their faces at the fountain earlier.

Front and rear pincer attack. Now it really looked like they were about to fight.

Huayue was notorious for its poor discipline, earning the nickname "Express Train to Juvenile Detention." The number of troublemakers there was more than the hairs on Sun Wukong’s body.

Not long ago, a fight between a first-year and a second-year student at the street basketball court had made quite a stir. Her desk mate had mentioned it.

Apparently, the two had argued over who would carry the flag, with the winner becoming the school’s boss.

Very childish, very primitive—like a tribal chieftain’s power struggle.

As a result, one ended up with a skull fracture in the hospital, while the other, though injured, had won.

At this moment, anyone wearing a volleyball jersey at Huayue was either a host or an invited guest.

Judging by the First High School’s basketball and soccer team uniforms, this boy had neither a school emblem nor a school name on his chest. He must be from Huayue.

A chill ran down Si Qing’s neck, and goosebumps rose like an electric current.

—So these boys were the infamous, aggressive, and xenophobic Huayue students, more like wolves than humans.

Unfortunately, they were still wearing First High School uniforms, practically advertising, "We’re from another school."

...Precisely stepping on a landmine.

They couldn’t run, and they couldn’t fight.

Either way, they were doomed. Might as well grovel first.

Even a tough guy wouldn’t hit someone who was already down. He was a street-smart guy; he must understand this logic.

Si Qing pursed her lips, adopting a resigned air, and lifted her head. "I’m sorry. We’ll be more careful next time. We’re really sorry for bumping into you."

As her gaze focused on the face before her, her breathing unconsciously shallow.

The boy’s damp bangs were casually pushed back from his forehead, falling on either side of his temples.

His skin was pale, his features sharp and refined, his nose straight and prominent, his jawline clean. A drop of water clung to his chin, about to fall. His eyes, though downcast, were sharply defined.

Even his fierce demeanor couldn’t overshadow his striking appearance.

"You—" The wolf let out a pleasant sound.

But his brows furrowed, making him seem even more intimidating.

Si Qing’s courage wilted under the latent aggression in his gaze. Instinctively, she pulled the girl beside her—who was clutching her arm and silently shedding tears—behind her.

"Yes?"

"Did you cry?" he asked. "Did it hurt?"

She slowly lifted her head again, her eyes widening in disbelief as she blinked twice.

...Unexpectedly civilized.

It seemed that no matter where you went, good people were still in the majority. Huayue had its reasonable ones too.

The boy’s gaze fell on her forehead. Probably seeing the red mark, he asked the question.

Si Qing had thin skin—literally.

It didn’t actually hurt; the tears were from fear.

"No." She quickly raised her hand to cover her forehead.

From behind, a few stifled laughs could be heard. The boys standing behind her had been watching the whole time. One of them joked, "Wake up before talking to a girl. You’re scaring us too. Maybe she cried because of you."

The group burst into laughter.

"Tsk."

The cheerful laughter came to an abrupt halt.

Si Qing: ...Ah, the leader of the pack. /(Rational Edition)

The boy glanced at them indifferently, then tugged at his collar, leisurely wiping the water droplet sliding down his chin. He propped himself up on his knee and bent down.

"Here to watch the game?"

His handsome face suddenly loomed large before her eyes, his downward gaze leveling out.

Si Qing was taken aback.

Coming back to her senses, she realized this boy had extremely beautiful fox-like eyes.

His eyelashes were slightly upturned, his eyelids thin, with a shallow crease formed by his brow bone.

Even the most alluring fox eyes couldn’t soften the cold and detached spirit he carried.

Her nails were almost tearing at the hem of her uniform before she managed to muster a bit of courage and nodded in response to his question.

The boy in jersey number 12 came over and hooked an arm around his shoulder, laughing. "Stretch a bit. The game’s starting soon. Don’t just stand there radiating charm."

Number 9: "Isn’t this stretching? Bending over to look at a girl isn’t easy, you know."

After saying that, he got elbowed and quieted down.

The group of boys didn’t linger much longer. They joked around as they walked away.

Before leaving, the boy in jersey number 12 specially turned back and told them to enter through Gate 2 of the gymnasium, which led directly to the stands without detours.

The other girls, who had been separated from Si Qing and Zhang Yingqi, had run back and were now peeking from around the corner. They saw a circle of 185+ cm tall boys surrounding two small, pitiful, and helpless girls.

They wanted to call for help, but when they reached for their phones, their pockets were empty.

Then, with a horrifying realization, they remembered: First High School didn’t allow smartphones. :)

They cursed themselves for not having a small, genius phone watch.

The first-year students of First High School were assigned to the second row of the stands. Not long after Si Qing and the others took their seats, both teams entered the court.

On the LED screen, the First High School team was the same group they had encountered behind the building earlier.

The girls’ eyes widened, exchanging glances. The upperclassmen from the second-year level behind them were already laughing so hard they were almost in tears.

"Usually, they just serve us decent meals, but how come the volleyball team is also cobbled together from other teams?"

"The team was assembled yesterday afternoon. There are no substitute players or cheerleaders. The jerseys were bought this morning. First High School is just one big makeshift troupe."

"No choice. Huayue has a lot of face. Our school’s most handsome guys are all here."

"I can’t imagine how funny it’ll be watching a bunch of amateurs play volleyball."

The whistle blew, and the game began.

Compared to Huayue, First High School’s team was in disarray, each player’s form varying wildly.

One even treated the volleyball like a basketball, dribbling it between his legs and handing a point to the opponent.

It was easy to tell who was from the basketball team and who was from the soccer team.

Si Qing finally understood how in martial arts dramas, people could identify a fighter’s sect from just one move.

As the upperclassman behind them put it, First High School’s team was as loose as an old man’s pants—each player moved like a leisurely old man out for a stroll.

This continued until the boy in jersey number 8 rotated to the back row serving position.

Si Qing inexplicably held her breath.

The boy leaped lightly, his hair flying, his posture graceful.

Amid the collective gasp of the crowd, a dull, heavy thud echoed as the ball landed forcefully in the opponent’s court.

"What the hell are you doing?! Don’t just stand there—dodge!" cursed Huayue’s number 22.

"He’s aiming for my little brother! If I don’t dodge, I’ll end up a damn eunuch!"

The stands erupted in laughter.

All eyes were on number 8. The boy lowered his lashes, smiling softly as his teammates draped an arm over his shoulder and shook him.

He exuded an air of nonchalance, noble and indifferent, his demeanor far gentler than before.

Infecting by the joyful atmosphere around her, Si Qing’s lips curled up.

Until the referee blew the whistle, urging the players to maintain order. The surrounding noise gradually subsided.

It was a best-of-five match. Huayue won the first two sets, but First High School found their rhythm in the third and fourth, tying the score.

According to the rules, the final set required a two-point lead to win. The current score was 24-25, with First High School leading.

Huayue focused on defending against number 8. After four sets, they had analyzed and adapted to his style.

It was all about brute force.

When number 8 rotated to the front row, the breathing in First High School’s stands grew noticeably quieter.

Huayue’s back row had already set up their defense, watching as number 8 jumped—

There was no expected swinging motion. Instead, upon contacting the ball from the setter, he flicked his wrist.

The ball floated lightly into the unguarded area of the opponent’s court.

A clear whistle cut through the brief silence.

It was followed by the erupting cheers from the stands and a heart-wrenching cry from the back:

"Qi Fang is awesome!"

Half the arena was chanting his name.

The boy pointed to his ear with his left hand. The bright magnesium light danced on the tips of his hair. His eyes and brows were filled with bright, dazzling smiles.

With the uninhibited and passionate spirit of youth, he openly and earnestly listened to the cheers rising for him.

His name, mixed with the overlapping sounds, poured into Si Qing’s ears again and again.

Everything around her emphasized one thing: the brightest person in the crowd was Qi Fang.

chapters.title: The One and Only Summer
chapters.content:
Si Qing snapped back to her senses, and her originally calm heart suddenly stirred with a ripple.

The flashbulbs were a bit glaring. Her gaze unconsciously followed that figure surrounded by the crowd, watching him walk away into the unlit area until he disappeared.

Her trembling heartbeat gradually steadied along with the fading cheers.

After the competition, the spectators followed the team back to the bus. On the way, Si Qing realized her watch was missing.

She had checked the time before the competition started, so it must have fallen in the gymnasium.

After explaining the situation to the teacher in charge, the teacher handed her his phone before allowing her to go back.

Fortunately, she found it between the back of a chair and the steps before the janitor finished cleaning the venue.

As soon as she left the venue, she received a call from the teacher in charge, saying that the bus for the spectating students had already left. He told her to go to the bleachers by the sports field to find the athletes' coach and return with their bus.

The sky seemed to have overturned a pot of dye, and the highly saturated orange spilled across the ground.

Si Qing stood on her tiptoes and glanced toward the sports field. The coaches of the two teams were chatting about something.

The bleachers were packed with people, and among the sea of Hua Yue's pure white school uniforms, a few dark figures stood out.

She withdrew her gaze, her fingertips brushing the broken watch lug, and stepped onto the line dividing the deep gray ground from the orange.

This watch was quite old. The bar used to attach the strap had broken several times. When she took it for repairs, the master joked that she should just buy a new one, as the cost of repeatedly fixing the watch was more than the watch itself.

Si Qing only smiled and said that the watch was a gift from her family, and no matter the price, it was the thought that counted.

Because it was the first and last gift her father had given her.

Si Qing's parents separated when she was 11 years old.

It seemed calm and uneventful, with no signs at all. But on several sleepless nights, Si Qing had heard the hysterical arguments between her parents more than once.

She nervously clutched the corner of her blanket, hiding under the covers and secretly crying.

Si Qing was more mature than her peers.

At the age of five or six, she already knew that her mother had a difficult life in this family.

Her father was a tailor at a clothing shop in the town. When she was young, Si Qing always liked to follow him around.

While drawing on the red bricks at the entrance with the tailor's chalk, she occasionally overheard the aunts from the neighboring barbershop chatting.

Their topics always revolved around the few people they knew within a few miles. Whenever they mentioned Si Qing's mother, they would sigh indignantly.

"Zhao Yi, a top student from a big city, capable of earning money and beautiful, how did she end up with such a terrible mother-in-law? Living off her, using her, and still giving her a hard time. What is she trying to prove with her air of superiority?"

Her grandmother seemed to have never approved of her mother, nor Si Qing. Criticisms were always on her lips, blaming her mother for working late and not coming home, preventing her from holding her grandchild.

In their village, the older generation still held the same old-fashioned ideas from decades ago, believing that girls were unlikely to achieve great things.

Even though her mother worked at the best bank in the city and was highly capable, her grandmother had never looked at her with respect.

Children didn't understand the adult world. They only knew that both their mother and father were gentle people, and her mother had never complained about her father or grandmother.

Until one day, Si Qing went with her grandmother to the early morning market in the west of the city and accidentally got lost.

With people coming and going before her eyes, she panicked, her heart pounding, but she didn't dare to approach strangers for help.

Fearful of encountering a bad person who might kidnap her and sell her to the mountains, knowing she was a child without adult supervision.

Fortunately, she was recognized by an aunt from the same village at a fruit stand. Only then did she feel relieved and burst into tears.

Later, Si Qing helped her aunt sell fruits all the way, and they returned together after packing up the stall in the evening.

She didn't want to trouble her aunt further. As soon as they reached the alley, she jumped off the electric tricycle, thanked her, and ran home.

Just as she was about to knock on the door, she was suddenly stopped by a sharp, familiar yet strange female voice from the other side of the door.

"I'm calling the police!"

"Qin Zhao Yi! I am your mother! How can you talk to me like this?!"

"Did you call the police when your daughter was lost?! Don't you know how chaotic it is out there?! A child of eight, lost so far from home, how can you sit here so calmly?!"

"Don't blame me for everything! Did I ask your daughter to run around and play?!"

"You...!"

Her mother's voice stopped abruptly, followed by a dull thud of something hitting the floor.

Si Qing's hand, suspended in mid-air, trembled in fear. Her knees weakened, and she stumbled into the pond next to her. Fortunately, an elderly couple passing by pulled her out in time, though she had swallowed a lot of water.

Probably from the shock, she had a fever on and off for four days, dreaming that her parents had separated.

Every time she woke up in a daze, she would hold onto her parents and cry for a long time, sobbing incoherently, promising not to wander off and play again, begging her mother not to blame her grandmother, not to separate from her father.

After that day, her parents acted the same as before in front of her, calm and peaceful.

But in the nights when she couldn't see, the arguments grew longer and more frequent.

Finally, on an ordinary day, Si Qing followed her mother and left the home where the four of them had lived together for nine years.

It was also on that day that she discovered a gift her father had secretly placed in her school bag, with a note tied to the box.

["My Qingqing is about to grow another year older. Happy 11th birthday in advance, baby.

My girl has been sensible, kind, and beautiful since she was little. Everyone who has met you praises you, and it brings your dad so much pride!

I've spent ten birthdays with you, and this is the first time I've given you a gift. It's quite embarrassing to say, but your dad isn't capable enough to give you a worry-free childhood.

But Qingqing, don't be held back by your parents' separation. Whether we are by your side or not, we love you just the same.

Follow your mother to see a broader world and become an excellent person like her.

And remember, when eating cake, give the biggest and sweetest piece to your mother.

—Your dad who loves you forever"]

Looking at it now, the price of this watch might not even compare to an out-of-season watermelon.

But it could tangibly remind her that she once had a home of her own.

Suddenly, her wandering thoughts were reined in by a faint, crisp sound in her ear, like the crunch of sugar being bitten in the mouth.

A faint orange scent wafted over in the wind, mixed with a subtle sweetness.

A somewhat familiar smell.

In her peripheral vision, a dark figure appeared in the first row of the bleachers.

She tilted her head slightly, and her eyes fell on a hand hanging over the edge of the railing.

The fine, slender knuckles were slightly prominent, and the faint blue veins on the back of the hand were visible. The fingertips tapped the railing casually.

After a moment, the boy leaned forward, resting his chin lazily in the crook of his arm, "It's you again."

The idle and carefree air about him was indeed striking.

Si Qing nodded gently, an inexplicable shyness coming over her. She softly replied, "Senior, hello. It's me again."

The corner of Qi Fang's eye twitched slightly, as if something in her words had tickled his funny bone. He let out a low chuckle, "Didn't you go back with the school bus?"

"Not yet. I left something behind and came back to find it." She paused, "Oh, Teacher Zhu told me to go with your bus."

"Mhm."

The boy absentmindedly glanced at the object in her hand, "Did your watch break?"

She said no, "Just the strap broke."

"Oh."

"Mhm."

And then the conversation ended.

Si Qing thought the topic was over. She clutched her watch and looked back at the sports field, standing awkwardly in place.

Her mind was filled with: This is so awkward. Should I say something?

She couldn't very well ask him how his brain worked to always get first place in exams.

She'd be taken for a lunatic.

Behind her, a few clear metallic clinks rang out. The boy's long hand slowly reached over, palm facing up.

"Can I take a look? The watch."

Si Qing turned back and was surprised to find a screw on the railing, about the size of the screws used for glasses nose pads.

On his other hand, his little finger hooked a portable screwdriver pendant.

She hesitated for a moment before handing the watch over.

Then, inexplicably, the boy started fixing it as if it were the most natural thing in the world.

The situation was developing more bizarrely than any dream she'd had while asleep.

Moreover, Qi Fang's bag actually had such things, like Doraemon.

Si Qing didn't dare to stare at him. She turned her face away, pretending to look at the sports field, while secretly watching him from the corner of her eye.

Qi Fang's hands were steady. He carefully collected the removed parts in his palm, replaced them with new ones, and the whole process was as smooth as flowing water, a pleasure to watch.

Before long, there was movement on the sports field.

"Fang Fang, stop loafing around there! Come take a photo!"

Fang Fang?

Si Qing glanced at the boy who was focused on fixing the watch.

He didn't move or seem to have any intention of responding.

The boy in the distance called out a few more times.

Perhaps seeing no response, he ran over.

When he saw Si Qing, he raised his eyebrows in surprise, "Hey, it's you again, little one. We seem to have quite the connection."

Si Qing nodded slightly in greeting.

The boy looked at Qi Fang again, crossing his arms and leaning against the railing, "Oh, helping others, are we?"

"Just passing time."

The boy gave a dry laugh, "Sure, whatever you say."

After a while, Qi Fang hooked the watch strap in front of Si Qing, "Done. Try it on."

The golden glow of the sunset cast a bright arc on the edge of the silver watch face.

Si Qing took the watch with both hands.

After fastening the clasp, she looked up again, "Tha—"

Before she could finish, a silhouette suddenly intruded into the blinding orange sunlight, boldly taking away most of the light.

The boy swung over the railing with one hand holding his bag, his bangs lifting as he landed. The pupils at the edge of his eyes reflected the melted glow of the setting sun. He was full of spirit, distinctly and deeply imprinted in Si Qing's eyes.

He landed steadily, zipped his sports jacket all the way up, and said indifferently, "You're welcome."

It wasn't until the two of them walked away that Si Qing belatedly raised her hand to her burning cheek.

She stared blankly at the figure standing in the center of the crowd in the distance. The pounding of her heart in her ears refused to subside for a long time.

In that moment just now.

The boy, carrying the orange-gold summer wind, had stirred a wave in her heart that she had never experienced before.

From then on, he became the one and only summer in her withered spring.

---

chapters.title: Troublemaker
chapters.content:
Si Qing returned to the dormitory and first went into the bathroom to take a shower.

The laundry room was a bit far, and she didn't want to make another trip, so she simply draped her wet hair over the back of the chair to dry.

Her roommate was on her way back, so she turned on the air conditioning in advance to cool the room.

Then she nestled into the chair, arms wrapped around her legs, and found the new chat box. She clicked on his profile.

Qi Fang's WeChat name summed up the common wish of people all over the world in four simple words.

— Sitting and Waiting for Money.

Kind of cute.

She pressed her cheek against her knee, her soft eyes curving into small crescents.

Qi Fang's WeChat avatar was a photo of his family's cat and dog—a Beagle wearing a fried egg apron and a cow cat in a rose-patterned shirt.

Their fur was smooth and glossy, and they wore adorable little clothes. It was clear they were pets raised with love.

But the relationship between the two pets was visibly not very loving.

In the picture, the Beagle had its foot on a sweeping robot, its mouth holding the cow cat's ear, while the cow cat retaliated with a resentful punch straight to the Beagle's face.

In the bottom left corner were torn paper scraps, an overturned can of cat food, and scattered dog food.

It was a very storytelling photo. She couldn't imagine what mindset had led to taking it.

There was a group called the Beagle Victim Alliance, and Qi Fang was probably in it.

Si Qing exited back to the chat interface, her fingertip pressing against the screen, absentmindedly swiping a couple of times.

After much deliberation, she was still afraid of bothering him and gave up the idea of messaging him.

After finishing her nighttime routine and about to get into bed, Tan Lexi pushed open the door with a late-night snack.

"Qing Bao! Snail rice noodles! Come eat, come eat!"

The girl held a takeout bag in one hand, shaking it so the bag rustled.

Si Qing, who had just stepped onto the stool, quickly stepped back down.

She could brush her teeth again, but a bowl of spicy snail rice noodles at midnight was something she truly couldn't resist.

"Zhu Zhu and Cen Cen?"

Si Qing broke apart a pair of disposable chopsticks, rubbed off the burrs, and pushed the extra-spicy portion along with her own to Tan Lexi's seat.

"They're behind me. I came back first to get the takeout."

Tan Lexi opened the window on the balcony and the exhaust fan in the bathroom, then sat down. Instead of eating the noodles right away, she first leaned toward Si Qing, sniffing delicately with her nose.

"Qing Bao, I smell something unusual."

Si Qing tilted her head, "I didn't change my shampoo?"

Tan Lexi poked Si Qing's soft cheek. Si Qing had just taken a shower, and her skin, moistened by the steam, was fair and translucent, turning a light pink at the slightest touch.

"Don't play dumb with me."

"Spill it. What happened today? You were supposed to come back at 8:30, so why the sudden change?"

Coincidentally, Zhu Xing and Cen Weiying Ying chose that moment to push open the door.

The private interrogation turned into a joint trial.

Si Qing honestly put down her chopsticks, placed her hands on her knees, and sat up straight like a primary school student under the teacher's watchful eye.

The three girls stared at her solemnly.

Cen Weiying Ying had just graduated from high school and recently broken up. She had chased after Tan Lexi's ex-boyfriend, who could match all 16 MBTI personality types in terms of being a scumbag.

Zhu Xing was even more hardcore. She had been in a ambiguous relationship with the boy next door for four years. Even after she got into Kyoto University and he got into Kyoto University for his master's, they still hadn't broken through that final barrier.

Among the four girls in the dormitory, only Si Qing had no experience with relationships and was the youngest.

This girl was quiet when she first met people, but once she got familiar, she was like a fluffy little lamb, soft all over, including her earlobes.

They were just afraid some fox spirit would know how to wear her down.

The period after freshmen enrollment was the peak season for scumbags to establish their personas, aiming to deceive the young girls with stirring hearts.

Especially in their business school, it was practically a training camp for playboys.

Those with a bit of family background or good looks were either scumbags or players.

Among the notable freshmen, almost all of them had become regulars at the club near the North Gate.

Most of them wanted to have fun before their families made arrangements for them. After plucking the fresh flowers, they stopped pretending, almost without exception.
