Cen Weiying Ying: "Good grades don't filter out scumbags. Kyoto University has plenty of playboys."

Zhu Xing: "Especially near the North Gate, it's practically a den of playboys. Did someone see you and your friend were pretty and insist on dragging you to a second venue?"

Could "handsome" be used to describe Qi Fang?

This thought popped into Si Qing's mind, and the corner of her mouth twitched subtly. Then Zhu Xing's "Hmm?" pulled it back into a straight line.

The snail rice noodles on the table were still steaming. Tan Lexi lifted her chin, "Eat while you talk. It'll get cold soon."

Si Qing obediently bent her eyes and gave a concise summary of what had happened.

Worried about damaging Tang Youmin's image, she made some slight adjustments and didn't mention the relationship or names.

The girls had boundaries and knew Si Qing hadn't encountered any real trouble, so they dropped the subject.

Though they were genuinely curious about the upperclassman who had taken Si Qing out to eat today—how decent, mature, and reliable he must be to earn Si Qing's good person card.

The cicadas' chirping from the gaps in the leaves rustled into the eaves. The girls had all finished their tasks and were sitting in their respective seats, chatting about the club recruitment the next day.

Kyoto University's club recruitment was divided into two batches.

Tomorrow's batch was for student organizations. After the military training, there would be a "Hundred Clubs Battle" for characteristic clubs, featuring roadshows, related activities, and mini-games. Students could collect stamps to exchange for gifts.

Both types of clubs offered practical course credits, but student organizations were more beneficial for evaluations and awards, so they had a higher priority and were relatively harder to join. Some preparation was required in advance.

Si Qing had originally planned to join the Publicity Department with Shen Shangyue, which was under Qi Fang's supervision.

Unfortunately, she perfectly avoided all the requirements for the Publicity Department.

No video editing experience, no social media account operation experience, and her photography skills were hard to evaluate.

These days, things had become so competitive that you couldn't even get credits without a special skill.

Luckily, she had experience in planning school celebrations from high school, so she was somewhat experienced in planning cultural and sports activities. In the end, she applied for the Organization Department.

---

A pig-like squeal escaped from Room 102 of the boys' dormitory.

Li Qingyu was sprawled on the desk, laughing so hard he had lost all sense of reality.

Qi Fang expressionlessly glanced at Li Qingyu's phone on the desk.

Top 4 Hot Post on the Forum: [Qi Fang to Perform Girl Group Dance].

His face showed no emotion, but he let out a "tsk."

Li Qingyu: "Damn, they're roasting you hard."

Those familiar with Qi Fang knew that no emotion was the biggest emotion.

Lu Yeti, having aired out his white coat, walked over and took a look, then laughed, "Does he know about this himself?"

"He replied to the message himself. Do you think he knows or not?"

Li Qingyu, not one to miss out on the fun, opened the image in the post.

It was a screenshot of the Business School Freshmen Group chat.

8:56 PM.

"Is our Business School debuting?"

"Swipe my campus card! All of you, send me off to debut!"

"Then I want to see Senior Qi Fang standing in the center position performing a girl group dance!"

Immediately following that message was an "OK" emoji.

Sent by: 23-Business- Qi Fang.

Qi Fang rarely checked the group chat. Since Ke Mingyuan added him to the group, he had only entered it twice.

Once to change his nickname.

The other time was today, when he let a certain little girl see the "notifications."

Li Qingyu curled his lips downward and magnified the name "Qi Fang" in the screenshot to its largest size.

"Bro, take a look. Who sent this 'OK'? I can't see clearly."

Qi Fang lifted his eyelids, as calm as a breeze, and dropped, "Not me."

Lu Yeti snorted, "Then who the hell is it?"

"Mhm." Qi Fang pressed his tongue against his dimple. "There's a troublemaker."

chapters.title: Big Bad Wolf
chapters.content:
The next morning was rare in its lack of events. Only Si Qing had an interview, and the girls in the dorm were catching up on sleep, not crawling out of bed until nearly eleven.

Zhu Xing and Cen Weiying Ying had no intention of joining any student organizations—the former was just lazy, while the latter was a suffering novelist, already immersed in her art, oblivious to the world around her.

Tan Lexi, as the class monitor, automatically joined the Student Affairs Office, following the tradition of previous years.

When Si Qing finished washing up and came out, Tan Lexi was still sitting on her bed with a head of messy short hair, looking dazed.

After a while, she peacefully closed her eyes again, buried her head in the blanket, and curled up into a ball.

"Still sleeping, Your Highness?"

Si Qing poked her and placed the warm water she had just poured into the small basket on her bedside table. "Get up and drink some water to reduce the swelling. Don’t you have a meeting at the Student Affairs Office this afternoon?"

"Okay..." Tan Lexi slowly opened her hand and held up five fingers.

Meaning, five more minutes.

Zhu Xing walked over and patted the edge of her blanket. "If you don’t get up now, I’ll take action."

Hearing the dormitory bully’s voice, Tan Lexi suddenly opened her eyes, straightened her back, and obediently climbed out of bed.

By the time she finished washing up and came out, Si Qing was on the balcony collecting laundry.

Sunlight spilled onto the white tiles of the windowsill, casting a soft halo on the girl’s ink-black hair.

She was so beautiful it was dizzying.

For no reason, Tan Lexi thought of the senior Si Qing had mentioned last night—the one who took her out to dinner.

What kind of humble gentleman could remain composed in the face of such a stunning little fairy?

And besides, who knew if he was really a gentleman at all.

For no reason, she had a hunch.

—That senior was faking it.

Most likely, he was a big bad wolf, hiding his ambition beneath a harmless exterior, watching with predatory eyes.

---

A light rain fell in the early morning. The wind carried a hint of moisture, and the golden light filtering through the leaves was softened, no longer blinding even without an umbrella.

Just before one o’clock, Shen Shangyue arrived at Si Qing’s dormitory building to return her dry-cleaned coat. The two of them went to the central cafeteria for lunch, bought fruit tea, and then headed to the print shop together.

Unfortunately, it was the break between the first afternoon classes for the upperclassmen, and the print shop near the Fourth Dormitory was packed.

Si Qing peeked through the door and decisively took a detour to the one across from the West District dormitories.

The West District print shop was located above a Yimei Supermarket, with a narrow, long stone staircase leading up to it. Shen Shangyue was wearing high heels, making it difficult to climb. Si Qing told her to wait in the shade downstairs while she went upstairs to print the interview materials.

As soon as she pushed the door open, a blast of cold air from the air conditioning hit her, and she immediately noticed a pair of outstretched long legs.

White sneakers, loose dark gray casual pants.

Tang Youmin was sitting on a tall stool, chin resting on his hand. Apart from him, the only other person in the print shop was a middle-aged man quietly eating stir-fried noodles.

Hearing the noise at the door, Tang Youmin glanced sideways. "Send me the files you want printed. I’ll do it for you while I’m at it."

Si Qing sat down on the chair next to him and forwarded the documents. She added, "These are interview materials for me and Xiaoyu. Two copies each."

After saying that, she subtly watched his reaction from the corner of her eye.

Tang Youmin’s fingers lazily scrolled the mouse wheel. "Got it."

Si Qing didn’t miss the slight pause in his fingertips when he heard a certain name.

Xiaoyu was a nickname only those close to Shen Shangyue would know.

Clearly, Tang Youmin knew it.

This suggested that in Shen Shangyue’s mind, Tang Youmin was probably someone she considered close.

Last night, Si Qing had noticed that his attitude toward Shen Shangyue was off.

Awkward, yet visibly concerned, always trying to strike up a conversation with her.

Like a peacock forcing itself not to display its feathers, but failing miserably.

As they left the print shop, Si Qing turned back to look at Tang Youmin, intending to ask if he wanted to join them for the interview at Building Three.

Unexpectedly, she found him lowering his gaze, staring at something downstairs with a bland expression.

Si Qing followed his line of sight but, due to the difference in height, she only saw a lush cluster of leaves.

Through the swaying foliage, she vaguely glimpsed two figures.

The one in the peach-colored long dress standing against the wall was Shen Shangyue. The person facing her was mostly obscured by the tree’s shadow, but from the silhouette, it was a man.

Before she could look away, Tang Youmin stuffed a transparent file folder into her arms.

A moment later, he patted Si Qing’s shoulder and pointed toward the dormitory building across the street. "Help me deliver something to Qi Fang at Building 14."

Certainly, seeing Qi Fang was a good thing, but she didn’t want to leave Shen Shangyue alone.

"You go yourself." Si Qing tucked the folder under her arm and nudged him. "Xiaoyu is waiting for me."

"I’m going to Building Three too." Tang Youmin turned and gently pushed her toward the stairs on the other side. "I’ll stop by Yimei to buy two bottles of mineral water on the way."

"..."

At this point, even if Si Qing was slow, she should have caught on.

Tang Youmin was usually the type to grumble while doing everything for you—a genuinely considerate person.

Apart from the occasional need for her to foot the bill in the past, he had never troubled her or asked her to do anything for him.

This was unusual. It felt like he was deliberately sending her away.

Si Qing could more or less guess that he had seen something downstairs just now.

But since Tang Youmin wasn’t saying, she wouldn’t pry. She let it slide.

Then she turned and sent Shen Shangyue a WeChat message: *"Xiaoyu, Tang Youmin just asked me to help him deliver something. He’s also going to Building Three. If you’re heading the same way, you can go together first. No need to wait for me."*

Si Qing checked the time, bought the water, and then went to wait at the corner of Building 14’s courtyard.

The wind rustled the leaves, and dappled sunlight danced across the pure white low wall, split by its edges into fragments of mercury at her feet.

Qi Fang stepped down the stairs, his peripheral vision catching a glimpse of light blue under the tree.

His steps faltered, and his gaze shifted over.

Si Qing was wearing a side-slit denim skirt today, her long legs slender and proportionate, neither too thin nor too plump. Her short cropped vest in the same color scheme perfectly accentuated her waistline, and her long hair was casually pinned back, neat and efficient.

Si Qing was staring at the dancing light on the ground, lost in thought, when a pair of fox-like eyes suddenly entered her line of sight.

Qi Fang placed his hands on his knees, bent down, and tilted his head to look at her. "Good afternoon."

Only at this angle could he fully see those eyes—upturned at the corners, naturally carrying a hint of flirtatious charm.

"Good afternoon." Si Qing deliberately ignored the way her heart raced at his presence and handed him the folder. "Tang Youmin asked me to give this to you."

The light, fragmented by the gaps in the leaves, sparkled like tiny diamonds across the girl’s delicate features.

With her slightly upturned eyeliner and shimmering gaze, there was a soft, restrained allure beneath her rounded eyes.

Qi Fang straightened up, taking both the folder and the bag from her wrist into his hand.

His slightly curled fingertips brushed against her wrist bone. Si Qing subtly lowered her gaze to glance at the contact.

His palm was tinged with a faint pink, the lines clear and continuous, the tendons at the base of his palm well-defined, forming a sensual dip.

There was a thin, long callus on the side of his thumb pad—likely from playing the piano.

"Let’s go."

Si Qing snapped out of her daze and followed him.

As they passed the street dance club’s recruitment poster, she suddenly remembered last night.

Half-asleep, she had heard Tan Lexi and Cen Weiying Ying exclaim in surprise at something, and then she heard Qi Fang’s name.

Even though her senses were dulled by sleep, she had forced herself to listen to the gist.

Apparently, Qi Fang had agreed to dance or something.

Unfortunately, by morning, she couldn’t recall the details.

She looked up at him through the shade of the trees. "Senior, do you know how to dance?"

"..."

He had intentionally kept it to himself, but he hadn’t expected this girl to be a little wooden block who poked at his sore spots on purpose.

Qi Fang pulled at his lips ambiguously. "Thanks to you."

His dark eyes fixed on her, seemingly carrying some unresolved grievance.

Si Qing: "?"

Soon after, her phone buzzed. A screenshot appeared in her chat with Qi Fang.

She recognized the conversation inside.

—At that time, Tang Youmin had come up behind her, startling her so much she almost dropped her phone. She had fumbled with it before handing it back to Qi Fang, the screen already off.

So, had she accidentally pressed "OK" and sent it?

This move deserved an 8.6 out of 10.

Because she had contributed 1.4.

Si Qing’s lashes trembled slightly, and she loosened her tightly pressed lips, the pale pink quickly regaining its color.

His gaze swept over the girl’s slightly glossy lips—plump and moist.

He lingered for only a moment before casually looking away.

Si Qing resignedly lifted her face. "Senior, should I compensate you..." with some money?

Before she could finish, Qi Fang cut in, his voice clear. "Money can’t make me feel better."

---

chapters.title: Lookout
chapters.content:
If money couldn’t make him feel better, then there must be another way.

"Then," her voice was soft, her chin slightly raised as she looked at him, "what can make you feel better?"

Dappled sunlight danced on the bridge of his nose, the high arc of his nosebone casting a curve of light. His fox-like eyes, hidden beneath the shadow of his brows, lowered as he looked at her.

But his gaze wasn’t focused. His pupils were dark and depthless, impossible to read.

After a long moment, she finally heard Qi Fang speak again.

"Time is more valuable."

Si Qing’s doe eyes widened slightly, but she didn’t rush to respond.

Time was abstract. If she agreed to give it to him, he would have control.

She bit her lip. "You have to set a time limit first."

What if he took advantage and demanded she serve him for a lifetime? How would that be any different from taking her life?

"Do you really think I’d take advantage of you?"

Si Qing stared at him wordlessly, her thoughts written all over her face.

"..." Qi Fang curled his fingers slightly.

If he asked for too much time, he might scare her off.

Who was really comforting whom here?

"Half a day," he said. "Deal?"

Si Qing clasped her hands behind her back, thought for a moment, then nodded. "If it makes you feel better."

"Then consider it a debt," Qi Fang gave her nose a slight, almost imperceptible lift. "I’ll come collect later."

Until now, Si Qing had never imagined that such a coquettish little expression would suit Qi Fang.

As they spoke, the two entered Building Three through the side door. Qi Fang went to the property office to get the multimedia room key, while Si Qing headed to the fourth floor first.

The Student Union had seven departments under it. The Publicity Department had many restrictions, and the Organizational Department had a high workload. Together, the two departments had fewer than 80 people, and their interviews were held in the small tiered classroom 412. The other departments each occupied a separate classroom.

On her way, Si Qing received a message from Shen Shangyue, telling her to come in through the back door when she arrived, as she had secured a prime spot in the last row.

"Qingqing, over here." Shen Shangyue raised her hand, waving in her direction, and even reserved a folding chair for her. "Last row by the window, the king’s hometown."

"The protagonist’s exclusive seat from a novel, taken by you."

Si Qing adjusted her skirt and sat down, casually asking, "Did Tang Youmin give you the interview materials?"

At that, Shen Shangyue let out a long sigh and slumped onto the table. "He did. I really owe it to you for running into him today."

Si Qing tilted her head. "What happened?"

"I was waiting for you downstairs when I ran into some creep. From the way he talked, he was probably from another school. He must’ve seen that the West District was quiet and that I was standing alone, so he came over and started harassing me with his nonsense, like he was chanting a script. He even cornered me against the wall so I couldn’t leave." She tapped her temple. "He’s probably not right in the head. Luckily, Tang Youmin sent you away, so you didn’t have to go through that too."

Si Qing recalled that Cen Weiying Ying had mentioned something similar a while back—some people specifically came to campus during lunch breaks or before the first afternoon class, knowing there would be fewer people around, making it easier to target girls.

"He didn’t touch you, did he?"

The girl’s eyes shimmered, making Shen Shangyue’s heart soften. "Relax, we’re on campus. He wouldn’t dare. Do you really think I wouldn’t scream ‘catch the mistress’ if he tried? The West District dorms would have a crowd of students rushing out to watch the show in seconds."

"But you can’t always rely on good Samaritans passing by. You should keep some tricks up your sleeve for self-defense." She poked Si Qing’s cheek. "Alright, enough of this depressing talk. Let’s focus on the interview materials. After the interview, let’s go eat copper pot hot pot at the old restaurant in Nanxiang. I’ve heard it’s famous."

Si Qing smiled and agreed.

Soon, the chatter around them died down.

Si Qing looked up toward the front rows and saw a tall figure at the classroom door.

Qi Fang’s ring finger loosely hooked the small ring at the end of the file folder’s spine as he stepped onto the podium. His posture was straight, his movements always carrying an effortless elegance.

The stand-collar design of his new Chinese-style silk shirt gave him a stable and refined air. The left shoulder extended to the placket, embroidered with a subtle white gold bamboo pattern in the same color scheme. The hem was neatly tucked into his black dress pants.

Even when sitting casually, he exuded no laziness. Occasionally, he turned his head to chat with the department heads beside him, looking quite familiar with them.

The vice president projected the pre-shuffled list onto the multimedia screen, and the interview officially began.

The two departments proceeded simultaneously in their respective areas.

The president of the Organizational Department was a clean-cut boy in black-rimmed glasses named Chen Chengyan.

The vice president was an adorable girl with twin low ponytails, a round face, and curly hair—Dai Wan.

Compared to the two from the Publicity Department, their presence was almost angelically kind.

Si Qing checked the order and stepped down to the waiting area ahead of time.

The waiting area buzzed with quiet conversation.

Qi Fang pressed the tip of a white gold pen against his finger, absentmindedly clicking the cap on and off.

Suddenly, his peripheral vision caught something, and his movements subtly slowed, then lightened. His dark eyes flicked to the side for a moment before returning.

"I’ll be damned, does our school actually have girls this stunning?"

"That’s Si Qing from the Business School. She was all over the forums on registration day. I even showed her picture to my friends from other schools—they were green with envy."

"Does she have a boyfriend?"

"No, the source is reliable. My friend in Business Management has her WeChat."

"So, what do you think my chances are if I pursue her?"

"..."

The guy opened his front camera and touched his chin. "I’m an 8/10, right? I can’t be that bad."

"..."

"Dude, don’t just sit there in silence. You’re killing me."

"Shut up, the president’s looking at us."

chapters.title: Winter Cherry Blossoms
chapters.content:
After the interview, Si Qing went upstairs to find a self-study room to wait for Shen Shangyue.

About half an hour later, Shen Shangyue sent a message.

**Small Fish Moon:** "Bao, where are you?"

**Small Fish Moon:** "It's finally over, my butt is kinda numb from sitting uwu"

**Small Fish Moon:** "I was the last one in the Propaganda Department to finish  ^-^ (This isn't a ^, it's the middle finger I'm giving to the world)"

Si Qing sent a hugging emoji, and the two agreed to meet at the entrance of the third teaching building.

---

The copper pot steamed gently, bubbles rolling as the rich aroma of meat burst forth.

The two girls stuffed large mouthfuls into their mouths, cheeks puffed out as they chewed contentedly.

"This meal is one of the few comforts I've had lately," Shen Shangyue whimpered. "I haven't even told you how unlucky I've been these past few days."

Apart from today's harassment by a pervert, her string of misfortunes included, but was not limited to:

- On the second day of school, her takeout was stolen.- On the third day, she spent an entire afternoon in meetings, thinking she could finally go back to her dorm to rest, only to find her bed collapsed when she opened the door.- On the fourth day, after finally getting reassigned to a dorm, it turned out to be a mixed-gender building—floors one to three were male dorms, and four to seven were female. Unfortunately, she was on the seventh floor, in a single room with no roommate.- On the fifth day, which was yesterday, after exhausting herself moving luggage until after 6 PM, right at dinnertime, she couldn't get food at the cafeteria, so she went to the snack street outside. It was stuffy and hot, and she was sweating profusely. Thinking she could cool off by taking a detour through the small forest by the river back to school, she ended up falling into the river. She did cool off, but almost lost her life. She was finally rescued by an old man, only to be taken away by the police who thought she was attempting suicide.

Si Qing poured Shen Shangyue a glass of lemon water and handed it to her.

The girl's deer-like eyes sparkled with a smile, her voice gentle. "Blessings and misfortunes are intertwined. Maybe your good luck has already arrived."

Shen Shangyue pursed her lips, taking a moment to mentally prepare herself.

She didn’t want to hide her relationship with Tang Youmin from Si Qing, but she didn’t know how to bring it up.

Moreover, Si Qing probably already had an idea. She was a considerate girl—if they didn’t say anything, she wouldn’t ask.

"Qingqing, have you already guessed?"

"A little, maybe?" Si Qing understood her meaning and continued, "But this is your business. Not telling me won’t affect our relationship, okay?"

Last night, Qi Fang had even come up with the excuse of a dorm check just to take her away, probably because Tang Youmin and Shen Shangyue needed a moment alone.

"But if you don’t want to keep it bottled up, you can share it with me, you know... I’m pretty good at keeping secrets."

When they were kids, classmates would share secrets with Si Qing, and even after the person themselves had forgotten, she still never told a soul.

Shen Shangyue’s eyes curved into a smile as she poked at the meat in her bowl, her voice so soft it was nearly drowned out by the sizzling pot.

Her father was always busy with business abroad, and the number of days they saw each other in a year could be counted on one hand. Her mother was a famous lawyer, so strict she bordered on rigid.

From childhood to high school graduation, her daily life and diet were strictly managed by her mother as if following an instruction manual. In short, she had grown up under her mother’s overprotection.

From elementary to high school, her weekends were packed with extracurricular classes. Dating was not allowed, and she had to be picked up and dropped off from school every day.

Shen Shangyue had long accepted a future she could see clearly from the very beginning.

The few variables in her life appeared one winter evening during her first year of junior high.

It had snowed on and off for several days, the snow piling up past her ankles.

The teachers organized them to shovel snow in front of the school building.

Back then, any excuse to skip class and do free labor was a happy one.

At that time, she and a friend ran to a small crape myrtle tree on campus.

The branches were adorned with silver-white snow, making it look like a cherry blossom tree in full bloom from afar.

Her friend pushed her under the tree, and while the teacher wasn’t looking, secretly took out her phone, saying she wanted to take the best photo of her life.

Unfortunately, the snow had frozen solid, and no matter how hard the two girls shook the branches, nothing came down.

Later, two boys passed by. One of them ran over and told her to stand under the tree.

The next second, the entire tree’s glistening white snow scattered, silver threads floating through the air.

Not like a blizzard, but like a shower of flowers.

The two girls jumped excitedly, carefully cupping the falling snowflakes in their hands.

At one point, as she turned her head, she saw a pair of bright, soft eyes.

Long, dense lashes were dusted with a few petals of silver snow, making them sparkle.

Seeming to notice her gaze, the boy turned his face slightly toward her.

She knew this boy. Because of his poor English grades, he couldn’t get into Class 1, which was full of top students, so he was content to coast in Class 2 as a physics genius.

But the real reason Tang Youmin was famous in school had little to do with academics.

He was good-looking, with a great personality, popular among both boys and girls. Consequently, he had a lot of admirers.

She had been in Class 3 in her first year of junior high. Even then, more than half the girls in her class had a crush on him.

In the first semester of her third year, after the placement exams, she dropped from Class 1 back to Class 2.

Classes 1 and 2 didn’t have the concept of deskmates; everyone had their own single desk.

After returning to Class 2, because Shen Shangyue had grown quite a bit taller, the teacher placed her in the second-to-last row, right behind Tang Youmin.

The opportunity to get closer came after a weekly test. Tang Youmin was sick and absent, so she collected the class notes and homework papers, slipping them into his desk hole.

Tang Youmin was loyal. After that, every morning, he would bring her breakfast.

She was too embarrassed to tell him she had already eaten at home, so every day, she obediently ate two breakfasts.

Shen Shangyue wasn’t the type to take advantage of others without giving back. Whenever she had time, she would tutor him in English and occasionally in history and politics.

The more she repaid his kindness, the more her friends teased her, saying she would end up giving herself to him.

She laughed it off, saying Tang Youmin didn’t have those kinds of feelings for her, and she wasn’t thinking about dating either.

But Shen Shangyue knew her own dishonesty.

Everyone liked kind and sincere people, and she had known for a long time that she was no exception.

Shen Shangyue had used up most of her luck in life just to meet Tang Youmin. Naturally, she couldn’t bear the cost of a failed confession, so she chose to avoid the risk and never took that step.

Overthinking everything, she barely even had the courage to test the waters.

She hated her own twisted nature. How could Tang Youmin possibly like her bland and boring self?

That Christmas in her third year of junior high happened to fall on a school holiday. The last two periods were consecutive self-study sessions.

Their homeroom teacher, who was also their English teacher, had found an English movie and asked the class monitor to organize everyone to watch it.

The lights were turned off.

Halfway through the second self-study period, the teacher left early. The students below started moving their chairs around, pairing up to watch the movie.

Shen Shangyue didn’t move. She leaned back in her chair, shifting her upper body.

The boldest test she dared to make was letting her hair fall onto the corner of Tang Youmin’s desk.

It was as if, in that small way, she had entered his world a little.

After a moment, her hair was gently tugged. Tang Youmin was leaning on his desk, his fingertips seemingly twirling the ends of her hair in circles.

Shen Shangyue’s heart nearly leapt into her throat. She turned back and told him to focus on the movie and stop playing with her hair.

She was utterly frustrated with her own hypocrisy, as if she were sick.

As she sulked alone, the boy behind her lightly patted her shoulder.

"You’re angry. I can’t concentrate."

"Do you want something sweet? I’ll go buy some after this." He paused, then asked, "Or do you want hot pot?"

"Oh, my aunt was going to bring you food today." He leaned in closer. "Then, how about matcha Basque cheesecake? You can have it as a snack during evening self-study. It’s not too high in calories."

...

"Are you really not going to talk to me?"

Shen Shangyue’s heart was a whirlwind of emotions. She steeled herself, turning half her body toward him, resting her elbow on his desk. "Tang Youmin, aren’t you afraid I’ll misunderstand?"

His gaze flickered with the movie’s light, shifting between brightness and darkness. "Misunderstand what?"

Shen Shangyue forced a smile, her lips curling up. "Misunderstand that you have a secret crush on me?"

She belatedly realized how reckless she had been and didn’t know how to take it back. All she could do was let the awkwardness linger.

After a long silence.

"I do have a crush on you." He laughed, poking her hand resting on his desk with his fingertip. "I’m openly in love with you, idiot."

The feeling at that moment was indescribable.

An unbearable wave of joy surged into her heart. The secret she had carefully hidden for so long spilled out through her eyes.

Even now, recalling it, the bittersweet ache at the tip of her heart lingered.

She and Tang Youmin were very careful, and apart from a certain sharp-eyed person named Qi Fang from Class 1, almost no one knew about their relationship.

On the day she received her admission notice to No. 1 High School, Shen Shangyue confessed to her mother about dating, saying that the boy was a good person and she wanted to introduce him to her.

Her mother didn’t react much at the time, just said, "Next time."

About three or four days later, her father returned from abroad, and the family went on a trip to Shencheng.

As soon as they got off the plane, Shen Shangyue wanted to tell Tang Youmin she was safe, only to realize her phone was missing.

She reported it lost, but it wasn’t found at the airport.

The next morning, when she went to the service center with her mother to replace her SIM card, she was told that her original number had already been deactivated.

It wasn’t until she discovered that her WeChat and QQ accounts had also been canceled that she looked at her mother in disbelief.

When she was told that they would be settling in Shencheng and never returning, Shen Shangyue felt a sudden suffocation.

Her mother said that if she hadn’t acted first and dated that boy for over half a year before telling her, she wouldn’t have gone to such extremes.

She wouldn’t be getting her a new phone either. She had already spoken to the teachers at the new school—if there was anything, they would notify her directly.

Shen Shangyue began to feel that life had no hope during the time she was confined to the new home by her mother.

Part of it was because she hadn’t been able to give Tang Youmin a proper explanation.

But more than that, the thought of living under her mother’s control forever made her wonder how much longer she could endure.

She couldn’t sleep night after night, losing over twenty pounds in a week.

At the start of her first year of high school, she collapsed at school. The doctor said it was a small hemorrhage in the frontal lobe causing pathological depression. Her father rushed back from abroad, applied for a leave of absence from school, and she was hospitalized for observation.

To her, it was just moving from one cage to another.

Shen Shangyue lay in bed, staring out the window, wondering how she had become like this.

She missed her friends from the mountain city, and she missed Tang Youmin terribly.

Her father turned down a lot of work to stay in the country. Her mother changed, often crying in places where Shen Shangyue couldn’t see.

Because of her illness, she lost a lot of emotional perception. In simple terms, she became so indifferent that she bordered on coldness.

Later, under medication, she slowly improved and no longer resisted going out.

While traveling in Xinjiang, her mother asked if she wanted to return to the mountain city. Shen Shangyue nodded and said okay.

The day she returned to the mountain city was a Friday in April, and the cherry blossom trees at the school gate were in full bloom.

That afternoon, she and her mother went to a café across from No. 1 High School, found a window seat, and sat there quietly, watching the school she was supposed to attend.

Her mother sat across from her, tears streaming down her face in emotional collapse, until Shen Shangyue let go of her grievances and finally received the long-overdue apology.

Under the sky, there were probably no children who truly blamed parents who loved them. But love itself was unsolvable—healing and depression coexisted.

The sunset glow spread outside the window, and the dismissal bell rang.

First-year high school students at No. 1 High didn’t have evening self-study. She and Tang Youmin had agreed that once they were in high school, they would try all the good food around the school, then walk home to digest.

The school gate was bustling, with students coming out in twos and threes.

Shen Shangyue stared intently, afraid that the person she was looking for would be swallowed by the crowd and she wouldn’t find him.

Before long, Tang Youmin and Qi Fang walked out side by side, chatting about something. He laughed and nudged Qi Fang’s shoulder, who dodged.

He hadn’t changed much, maybe a little taller.

A little further on, a girl pushing a bicycle was bumped by a boy on a bike who laughed as he passed, causing her to stumble forward a few steps.

Tang Youmin casually grabbed her backpack, and Qi Fang steadied the bicycle handlebars, preventing the bike from falling and hitting someone.

Shen Shangyue’s eyes curved into a smile.

"Mom, the boy I like is over there, the one on the left with slightly shorter hair."

She reached her fingertip toward him, only to be stopped by the glass, suddenly coming back to her senses.

She was already far away from him.

"I told you he was a good person. I wasn’t lying to you."

That day, her mother cried for a long time. Shen Shangyue also realized that she probably couldn’t truly reconcile with her mother, but she couldn’t bring herself to truly resent her either.

When she returned to Shencheng to start a new life, her personality opened up a lot.

It was as if the part of her that Tang Youmin had changed stayed with her in his place.

And then there was last night, at the police station.

Tang Youmin called her name with a displeased look, like a hedgehog on guard.

At that moment, her mind went blank, her emotions indescribable, her entire heart elated because he still remembered her.

So much so that when he saw the scratch on her arm, she couldn’t help but test him a little, asking if he was worried about her.

He said, how could that be.

Tang Youmin didn’t lie. He was always straightforward.

If he said no, then it was no.

Si Qing listened intently, her eyes glistening. Under the pretense of lowering her head to eat, she pulled out a tissue to wipe her eye, muttering to herself, "The soup splashed into my eye."

Shen Shangyue propped her chin in her hand, watching her, not exposing the act. Instead, she switched to the serving chopsticks to add more food to Si Qing’s bowl.

"Small Fish, aren’t you going to tell Tang Youmin any of this?" Si Qing sniffled, then began making excuses for her own secret tears. "So spicy."

"Let’s look forward, it’s been so long. Apart from you, I don’t have any other connection to him. It’s best if we don’t see each other in the future."

She spread one hand open. "Besides, I don’t really know what to say to him now. After we separated last night, we haven’t spoken again. This afternoon was the same—the awkwardness was so thick I could’ve ascended to heaven on the spot."

Si Qing bit her chopsticks. "Maybe he’s just pretending to be deep."

Shen Shangyue laughed. "No way, he’s such a gentle person. He usually doesn’t let people feel awkward."

Si Qing tilted her head, a question mark slowly rising above it.

Gentle? Who?

He would nag her for half a day if she fried an egg and a drop of oil splattered. Gentle?

"How come we’re only talking about me?" Shen Shangyue blinked rapidly, forcing a change of subject. "I also want to ask you—is Qi Fang pursuing you?"

Si Qing let out an "ah," "No."

On the contrary, it was she who was trying to catch the moon.

"Phones are so personal. He just handed his over to you. At most, if it were me, I’d only let someone look at it, not actually give it away."

Si Qing understood. "Because my phone was out of battery. And even if I wanted to snatch his phone, I couldn’t outrun him. Suppose, in the off chance that I did disappear, the police station is right there. He could just call the police to catch me, so he probably trusts me."

After listening to her serious analysis, the folds of Shen Shangyue’s cerebral cortex seemed to be gently smoothed by a spring breeze, bringing an unprecedented sense of relaxation.

It was as if she were strolling through an Australian forest, exchanging morning greetings with koalas, getting knocked out by a kangaroo’s elbow, and peacefully photosynthesizing on the grass after the rain.

She talked about romantic entanglements, while this girl’s mind was full of free-style boxing.

Qi Fang, you’re so lucky.

Such a rare, beautiful iron tree that blooms once in a thousand years—you better cherish her.

chapters.title: Barrel of a Gun
chapters.content:
That evening, Si Qing returned to the dorm. Ke Mingyuan had organized an online class meeting to elect class officers.

The Student Affairs Office’s first regular meeting, originally scheduled for that day, had been postponed to the next day because some classes hadn’t elected their monitors yet. Tan Lexi, lucky as could be, had eaten lunch and then gone back to bed for a nap.

Freshman military training would start the day after next. The mobilization meeting was scheduled for the next afternoon. As a representative of the School of Management, Si Qing would give a speech alongside representatives from the School of Economics and the School of Finance.

The next morning, Si Qing arrived early at the North Gymnasium’s Business School representative lounge to rehearse.

Hearing the sound at the door, the young man sitting upright on the single-seater sofa turned slightly and greeted Si Qing, “Hello, I’m Wen Zheng, from the School of Finance.”

Si Qing gave a slight nod and handed him the water she had brought. “Hello, I’m Si Qing, from the School of Management.”

At the sound, the young man lounging lazily in the middle of the three-seater sofa sat up straight, glanced back, and introduced himself half-heartedly, “Bai He.”

Si Qing’s eyes widened slightly, and she gave a small nod.

Si Qing had a close friend in Mountain City named Lian Zi, who was in the same grade as her and studied aerospace engineering at Jingda’s School of Engineering. Bai He was her boyfriend.

The School of Engineering was at Jingda’s new campus, nearly 40 kilometers away from the Yan Yuan main campus where Si Qing was.

At the beginning of the semester, Si Qing had video-called Lian Zi. Halfway through their conversation, Lian Zi pulled out a few tissues and handed them to someone beside her. Si Qing casually asked what was wrong.

Lian Zi laughed and said it was nothing, just that someone was secretly crying.

A man’s voice cut in, nasally and a bit cold, “I’m not crying.”

Si Qing had heard that her friend’s boyfriend was clingy. It was said that when he found out he wasn’t on the same campus as Lian Zi, he had been depressed for nearly half a month.

Knowing this, Si Qing didn’t dare ask more, afraid of adding to her friend’s trouble of comforting her boyfriend. So she kept quiet.

Si Qing sat down on the single-seater sofa across from Wen Zheng. When the instructor arrived, they exchanged a few words.

Wen Zheng looked at the three bottles of water Si Qing had brought, and the three bottles Bai He had brought.

No one had told him these two representatives were so considerate!

It made him look like he didn’t understand basic social etiquette.

“Should I… go buy three more bottles of water?”

Bai He: “Are you that thirsty?”

Wen Zheng: “...”

---

The mobilization meeting ended promptly at 3 PM. The girls in Si Qing’s dorm had taken a nap after returning, then got up at mealtime to go find food.

Tan Lexi still had the Student Affairs Office’s first regular meeting to attend that evening, so she grabbed an ear of corn and left.

After eating, the group returned to the dorm together, washed up, and lay back on their beds to rest.

At the thought of the hard days ahead starting tomorrow, the girls all looked gloomy.

Jingda’s military training included morning drills—assembly at 6:30 AM, morning exercises from 6:50 to 7:20, breakfast around 7:30, and training at 8 AM.

“Feels like I’m back in junior high military training. Back then, I was still a little bundle of energy,” Zhu Xing sighed, lying peacefully on her bed.

Si Qing: “I checked next week’s weather forecast. Seven straight days of clear skies, 39 degrees.”

Cen Weiying: “I’m already planning how to faint. Hehe.”

The three of them sighed deeply.

The carbon dioxide levels were about to go off the charts when Tan Lexi walked in with her corn, letting out a primal roar.

Cen Weiying flipped over, poking her head out from the bed. “Seven Seven hungry?”

Tan Lexi forced a bitter smile. “Seven Seven is shattered.”

Zhu Xing sat up abruptly. “How did a meeting break you like this?”

Si Qing got off her bed and poured her a glass of water.

Tan Lexi slumped into a chair, her heart heavy. “I dealt 10,000 damage to my direct supervisor’s health.”

Zhu Xing and Cen Weiying also got off their beds, pulled up chairs, and surrounded her. “Tell us everything.”

“The meeting was in a classroom on the seventh floor of Building Seven—that self-study building. You know the one, right? Building Seven is a bit run-down, only has two elevators.”

“With over a hundred people fighting for two elevators, I somehow got squeezed in. I thought I was lucky at first, but then I opened my eyes and—fuck! I was face-to-face with a hot guy, packed in so tight I couldn’t even turn around.”

“The guy looked like a tough one. His hair color was so eye-catching that skipping class would’ve been impossible. He even had an ear cuff. And the worst part? From the moment I got in, he kept making this *tsk tsk tsk* sound and even glared at me!”

Zhu Xing summarized: “Got it. The hot guy is your Student Affairs Office director. Then what? Did you say anything?”

Tan Lexi: “How could I dare? I didn’t even know what I did to upset him.”

“Later, with about ten minutes left before the meeting started, and the director and department heads still not there, I went to the bathroom.”

The bathroom on the seventh floor of Building Seven was at the end of a long, narrow corridor.

As Tan Lexi walked out, the lighting was dim, and she could only make out two tall silhouettes walking toward her against the light.

One of the guys laughed. “So, that student’s corn in the elevator was burning your *hook eight* the whole time, and you just endured it all the way to the seventh floor?”

“A role model for us all, Director Lu.”

Their conversation reached Tan Lexi’s ears.

A strong sense of déjà vu surged through her nerves, twisting and coiling until it exploded in her mind.

The next second, the three figures passed each other in the light, and two pairs of eyes met in mutual horror.

...

“Oh, so that hot guy glared at you because your corn was burning his *hook—”

Before she could finish, Zhu Xing’s slow reflexes suddenly caught up, and she nearly dropped her mug. “*Hook… hook… where?!*”

Tan Lexi covered her eyes. “…*hook hook da*.”

---

The next morning, the alarm went off. Si Qing, eyes still closed, crawled out of her blankets, knelt on the bed for a moment, then got up to wake her roommates one by one.

Footsteps echoed in the hallway. It was the first day of military training, and there was still a bit of novelty—no one was yawning nonstop from exhaustion.

Si Qing, Zhu Xing, and Tan Lexi were all at the West Campus field, while Cen Weiying was at the South Campus.

Jingda’s military training instructors were senior students who had been trained by the Student Work Department.

Last year they endured rain, this year they tore up umbrellas, and now they were ready to drop hailstones.

When standing at attention got tiring, they switched to squatting. When squatting got tiring, they maintained the goose-step posture.

The head instructor for the Business School was a baby-faced guy. Si Qing had seen him at the registration desk on check-in day.

During breaks, he would come inspect, crouch beside the instructors, and ask if the freshmen could hold on.

Complaints filled the air. “Senior, are you treating us like Transformers? So heartless.”

Li Qingyu smiled. “What are you talking about? We didn’t have it this good back in our day.”

Zhu Xing, in the back row, chugged some water. “I saw the little fan hanging from his waist. Do we have that kind of treatment?”

“You do, Zhu Zhu, you do.” Si Qing pulled a cooling patch from her bag and *slapped* it onto Zhu Xing’s forehead.

The cool minty freshness, carried by the moisture, seeped into her skin. Zhu Xing came back to life, her eyes lighting up. “Baby, you’re a Doraemon.”

Si Qing took off her hat to fan herself. Her bangs, pressed up, sprang back. She reached up and smoothed them down.

At the entrance of the West Campus field, a few male students in camouflage uniforms each carried a large box, lined up and walking toward them.

“Special supply for Business School teaching assistants. Remember to say nice things to Senior Qi Fang when you see him.” Li Qingyu turned his head, glanced, and lifted his chin. “Alright, take a break.”

The class monitor set the box down and called people over to get popsicles.

“Whoa, Dream Dragon? Haagen-Dazs? Sophia?”

“I’d be grateful for even a small Popsicle or a old-school ice pop. Never thought I’d get to eat *Ice Cream Assassin* during military training.”

Li Qingyu sat on the bleachers and casually grabbed a chocolate one.

As soon as he unwrapped it, someone pressed his wrist and pulled it aside. When he took it back, a small bite was missing.

“...”

He flicked the tip of his tongue against his molars, side-eyed the person beside him, and handed the popsicle over. “Here, take it. I’ll unwrap another.”

“It’ll melt and get sticky.” Qi Fang didn’t take it, instead tilting his head to take another bite.

“This is getting a little flirty.” Li Qingyu twitched the corner of his mouth.

The sunlight was blinding. Qi Fang narrowed his eyes, his gaze drifting elsewhere, ignoring him.

---

chapters.title: Unread
chapters.content:
Li Qingyu followed his wandering gaze.

The field was dotted with tiny green figures swaying back and forth, making his eyes dizzy.

“Your dorm has air conditioning, but you won’t use it. You come here to suffer instead?”

Qi Fang propped his elbows on his knees, his dark eyes lazily indifferent. “Came to see you.”

Li Qingyu: ?

Then look at me, please?

Where are you even looking?

At the back of the formation, Zhu Xing, holding a small tub of Sophia ice cream, sat back down next to Si Qing. She shared some with the girls in the front row, even thoughtfully feeding a bite into Si Qing’s mouth.

Rum raisin flavor.

Qi Fang’s gaze swept over the girl’s slightly puffed cheeks, the soft contours moving with each chew.

Like Shimizu—

Newo’s little sister.

The break ended. Li Qingyu blew the whistle on time and arranged for the freshmen to go to the auditorium for a national defense knowledge lecture.

Lined up in two rows, Si Qing stood at the end of the girls’ line, right at the border between shade and sunlight.

Actually, she had noticed Qi Fang’s arrival long ago.

Light pink T-shirt, loose washed jeans, sitting on the bleachers chatting with the head instructor, exuding a refreshing vitality.

Amid the sea of green, he was like a delicate flower growing among the leaves (?)

Qi Fang’s miraculous wardrobe at work.

Si Qing took the opportunity of adjusting the distance between her arms to turn her head toward the bleachers, pretending to casually glance over.

The head instructor stood there with a whistle in his mouth, striking a pose with one hand on the railing.

Qi Fang wasn’t there.

Si Qing took small steps backward, her gaze still lingering. Before she could pull it back, the grapefruit and orange fragrance in the air reached her nose first.

Mixed with a faint sweetness of orange candy.

Her senses sharpened instantly.

Qi Fang was here.

“Caught a good student daydreaming.”

The moment she turned and saw him, joy flooded her rational mind, her clear, moist doe eyes shimmering.

She suddenly came to her senses and calmed down, softly asking, “Here to inspect?”

Qi Fang stood against the light, his handsome profile outlined in a soft golden glow, his dark eyes lazily lowering.

He didn’t rush to answer. Instead, he subtly slipped a bottle of mosquito repellent into the outer pocket of Si Qing’s small crossbody bag.

The small bottle filled her bag completely, leaving no room for anything else.

The military training jacket had fake pockets. His gaze fell on the wide belt tied over the girl’s jacket.

His long fingers lifted the belt, tucking something inside.

Feeling something at her side, Si Qing’s shoulder trembled, half her body nearly freezing. “You—”

Flustered, she lifted her eyes to glare at him, voice barely above a whisper, “Qi Fang.”

Qi Fang finished tucking the item away, then slowly returned his gaze to her, innocent and composed, as if he didn’t find his previous actions the least bit suggestive. “Not inspecting. Just passing through.”

Si Qing blinked, suddenly feeling like a warrior drawing her sword, only to find no enemy in sight.

She clasped her hands behind her back, her fingertips brushing against the two cylindrical objects tucked into her waist. She pulled them out and held them in her palm.

Qi Fang took a step back, hands in his pockets. “Gotta go. Still have class.”

He turned and left without giving her time to react, his strides longer than usual, as if he were running late.

Si Qing lowered her head and glanced at the two orange-wrapped hard candies in her palm.

She had grown up in Shenzhen. Back home, there was a type of filled fruit candy called “Mai Bao.”

Orange and lemon flavors came mixed in the same pack. Every time you opened one, it was like opening a mystery box—a high-stakes gamble exclusive to Guangdong kids.

This kind of candy was almost impossible to find in other provinces and cities.

After moving to Mountain City, Si Qing would occasionally order some online and recommend them to her friends there.

Qi Fang also loved orange flavor.

She had always thought he would like this candy from her hometown.

And indeed, he did.

A smile curved her eyes as she put the candies back into her bag—only to discover the mosquito repellent in the outer pocket.

Had Qi Fang put it there just now?

The moment this realization settled, her heart felt as if it had been drenched by a sudden summer downpour—tingling, the sensation spreading down her spine, an uncontrollable joy.

She couldn’t help but wonder: Had Qi Fang come to the field just to deliver these?

A little voice in her mind paced back and forth, cautioning her.

Si Qing, stay calm. Don’t assume too much.

But when she finally calmed down, the answer was even more certain.

Unless Qi Fang had a sudden whim, carried an unopened bottle of mosquito repellent out the door, found it cumbersome halfway, wanted to throw it away, passed by the field, and decided to use her bag as a trash can.

...

Was this normal behavior?

He must have come just to deliver these things, right?

Si Qing tilted her head, a soft curve forming at the corner of her lips and cheeks.

Not far away, the girl at the end of Finance Class 2’s line stared at where Qi Fang had been standing, her pupils trembling.

The scene replayed in her mind like a silent film, the sound of a telegraph crackling in her ears.

Her brain captured the key frame, and she suddenly perked up.

Just now, Qi Fang… had he—

hugged Si Qing’s… waist?!

...

About five minutes earlier.

The two Finance classes were in a corner of the field. The head instructor was explaining the next arrangements, and everyone was perking up to listen.

The class instructor had asked her to help fetch water cups from under the bleachers. When she returned to the formation, she accidentally noticed an extra guy in civilian clothes at the very back, talking to the girl in front of him.

Even with her nearsightedness, she could tell the girl was Si Qing.

Tall and fair, stunning even when blurred.

As for that guy—

He stood in the sunlight, glowing, so tall that he made Si Qing, a tall beauty, seem petite.

And his outfit was on fire. Across all of Jingda, there weren’t many with such impeccable taste in clothes.

She squinted hard.

“!?”

...

Alright, she accepted this couple in 0 seconds.

They were perfect for each other!

It was just that this overwhelming underground romance vibe—

If she exposed them before they went public, wouldn’t Qi Fang’s death glare turn her into minced meat?

She’d keep it to herself. Keep it to herself.

---

On the third day of military training at noon, Si Qing received an email from the Organization Department.

The first meeting was scheduled for 8:30 PM that evening, right after the freshmen’s evening training and avoiding the time when upperclassmen had night classes.

The first three days of evening training were uneventful—just sitting in a circle with the instructors, learning military songs.

When there was downtime, people were pushed to perform talents.

Many guys secretly competed for future dating privileges over the next four years.

Turning roses into romantic gestures, accidentally flashing abs while dancing—it was all in a day’s work.

Some even pulled out a yo-yo to show off, or mimicked Kamen Rider’s transformation poses.

Though those got more cheers from the guys.

At 7:40, training ended. Si Qing returned to her dorm, changed clothes, and rushed to the meeting.

The first meeting of the Organization Department wasn’t particularly formal. Chen Chengyan and Dai Wan had bought snacks and drinks, arranging the tables and chairs in a circle to help members bond.

Following the usual schedule, a “Academic Career Planning Competition” would be held before the end of freshman military training.

The second half required a few interlude games for scoring, preferably ones that could kill time while engaging the audience.

Dai Wan suggested looking into variety shows for ideas. Everyone brainstormed together, striving to make the first event a success.

Finally, following procedure, they assigned roles for the event. Si Qing was put in charge of the award ceremony.

The upside? She didn’t have to speak.

The downside? She was the only one.

Dai Wan made the decision. “Everyone dress neatly that day. The male and female hosts and the person in charge of awards wear formal attire; everyone else wears business casual. Send me your sizes in advance so I can rent clothes for you.”

Chen Chengyan weakly protested, “Where are we supposed to get the money, Sister Dai?”

Dai Wan: “Getting approval from Qi Fang for funds isn’t something a deputy like me should worry about.”

“I see why you insisted on making me the director.”

Dai Wan blinked innocently.

Chen Chengyan laughed helplessly. “Alright, I’ll handle it.”

The two department heads bantered back and forth, amusing the members below.

The meeting ended at 9:30 PM. Si Qing returned to her dorm and took a shower immediately.

Hearing the bathroom door lock, Tan Lexi poked her head in. “Qing Bao, your phone’s been ringing nonstop. Check if it’s something urgent, don’t miss it.”

At that, Si Qing hurried over.

The soft towel was still draped over her head, droplets falling from the ends of her hair onto the desk.

Her phone screen showed 23 unread messages.

All from Qi Fang.

chapters.title: Xiao Qi
chapters.content:
Blood roared in her eardrums.

Si Qing moistened her lips, not having time to think much before opening the chat box.

Qi Fang had sent a picture.

In the image, a small cat lay on its back on the grass, basking in the moonlight, its belly covered by a large, cold, white, and good-looking hand. The slender, finely boned knuckles sank into the fluffy fur.

[坐以待币]: "cat"

Next came photos of flowers, grass, streetlights, and the moon.

Each photo was followed by a noun.

Like Baidu Baike.

He was still taking pictures.

Si Qing sensed something was wrong. "What's wrong with you?"

The message was sent, and the chat box repeatedly showed "The other party is typing..." but no message came through.

She stared at the bottom of the chat box, her fingertips unconsciously swiping up twice.

Then she exited WeChat, disconnected and reconnected to the network, waited a while, and reopened the chat box.

After a moment, she finally received a voice message.

She switched to receiver mode and held it to her ear.

"I can't find the way."

Six words, spoken in six seconds, slow to an unusual degree.

Had he been drinking?

Si Qing had no time to dwell on the strange tightness in her chest caused by the cuteness. She grabbed a thin shirt from the wardrobe and draped it over herself.

The cat in Qi Fang's photo was Xiao Qi, belonging to the boss of the Fourth Dormitory's print shop. Si Qing had a rough idea of where he was.

[山青]: "Stay right there, don't move around"

She told her roommate, then rushed out without even changing out of her sleepwear.

Droplets of water traced crystalline arcs along her dark hair, and the cotton sleepdress was darkened in patches by the moisture. As she ran, the night wind rushed in through the neckline, chilling her.

Si Qing tightened her outer garment and hurried straight to the Fourth Dormitory.

The wind howled past her ears, and the deep blue shadows of the trees retreated in clusters.

The moment her peripheral vision caught the small dark shape beside the lamplight, her heartbeat reacted before her mind could.

Qi Fang was crouched by the roadside, draped in a deep blue shadow cast by the camphor tree, tilting his head as he petted the cat.

Soft and lonely.

Fragile to the point that one dared not reach out to touch him.

"Qi Fang." Si Qing called him, her breath slightly trembling from the earlier rush.

He reacted half a beat late, slowly lifting his face. His dark eyes still held the unique, lingering tenderness from playing with the cat.

Si Qing tucked her skirt neatly and crouched beside him. "Do you want to go back now, or stay a little longer?"

"Not ready to go back yet."

He buried half his face in the crook of his arm. "Will you stay with me?"

Si Qing's breath hitched for a moment.

This man's unconscious coquetry was really hard to bear.

"I'll stay with you."

He didn't respond further, only the curve of his fox-like eyes deepened with pure joy.

Si Qing followed his gaze to the chubby cat lazily lying on the grass.

She had seen this cat a few times before when passing by with her roommate.

It always slept soundly; even when someone played a prank by placing a small pebble on it, it wouldn't wake up. It was affectionate and had a good temper.

There were many free-roaming cats on campus, most without names, referred to by nicknames among the students.

Classified by size and breed: Big and Small Orange, Big and Small Tabby, Big and Small Calico, etc.

There was only one Cheese—small in size. The print shop owner was from Liaoning Province and had named it Qi Zi. The students found it unpleasant, so they privately called it Xiao Qi.

Si Qing's fingertips scratched under the cat's chin, and the little one's tail tip brushed against her wrist. Its round belly flipped over, inviting a rub.

"So well-behaved, Xiao Qi."

She spoke softly, her clear, cool voice almost dissolving into the evening breeze.

Hearing a few indistinct words, Qi Fang's fingers, suspended in mid-air, stiffened. His gaze shifted openly to the side.

The girl's bangs were lifted by the wind to both sides, and the halo of the streetlight rested on her eyebrows.

The shadow cast by her eyelashes trembled lightly, like a butterfly perched on a misty lake surface. With the slightest flicker of her eyes, it could easily arouse his curiosity.

Si Qing's fingers, which had been petting the cat, froze, yet she pretended not to notice his gaze.

"Xiao Qi?" His lips moved, barely managing to bite out those two words. "Me?"

Si Qing's deer-like eyes widened, quickly realizing. She tapped the cat's little head. "It's her, Xiao Qi, the Qi from cheese."

Qi Fang rarely took a moment to react.

After a while, as if thinking of something.

"Sometimes Fang, sometimes Xiao Qi."

The dimples at the corners of his mouth deepened. "Si Qing, are you teasing me?"

"..."

A half-minute of silence followed, behind which was Si Qing's rapidly beating heart.

"I am not."

Si Qing lowered her eyelashes, focusing on petting the cat, no longer looking at him.

After a moment of silence, Qi Fang's phone rang.

The screen displayed the name Tang Youmin.

Qi Fang didn't even glance at it; he picked up the phone by the edge and handed it directly to Si Qing.

She knew he wasn't thinking clearly now. It was possible he'd fall asleep mid-call.

Si Qing took the phone, pressed the answer button, and stood up to stretch a bit.

Tang Youmin: "Just signed the contract. Why did you call so many times?"

"Qi Fang drank too much."

There was a silence on the other end.

After a long while, he spoke, "Who is this?"

Tang Youmin's "Who is this?" shattered four years of plastic uncle-nephew relationship with one punch.

"Si Qing."

As soon as she spoke, she clearly heard Tang Youmin exhale deeply, followed by a string of flowery language.

"I thought he got drunk and let someone sleep with him! Scared me to—"

Before he could finish, he changed the subject, "Wait, were you two drinking together?"

"..."

People who hung out with Qi Fang really had special thought processes.

Si Qing was speechless. After briefly explaining the situation, she told him to hurry back to campus to pick up Qi Fang from the Fourth Dormitory.

In case Qi Fang really passed out, she wouldn't be able to carry him back to the dorm by herself.

Si Qing hung up the phone and looked back.

Under the lamplight, a tabby cat had suddenly appeared, its pupils narrowed to slits, staring intently at Xiao Qi.

Qi Fang's palm had a few red scratches extending to the back of his hand.

Yet, he still heedlessly petted the agitated Xiao Qi, as if he was used to being scratched by cats.

Xiao Qi was used to freedom in this small plaza; rolling around in the grass was a common sight.

Si Qing was worried about Qi Fang's wounds getting infected, no longer concerned with personal boundaries.

The girl's slender hand clasped his wrist, pulling it towards her.

"Let's go sit over there."

Si Qing nodded towards the stone bench not far away, her voice carrying a stiffness she herself hadn't noticed.

Those usually deft fox-like eyes rarely showed a moment of bewilderment.

Qi Fang lowered his gaze slightly, said nothing, and staggered to his feet, letting Si Qing arrange him.

"No more playing with the cat. Stay here and wait for me. I'll be right back."

After saying that, she was afraid he wouldn't listen.

Qi Fang was at most eight years old right now.

Only a mix of coaxing and threats would work.

Si Qing pressed him down on the stone bench, her dark eyebrows slightly furrowed. "Be good or I'll spank you..."

He sat in the light, his pupils surprisingly bright.

The earlier bewilderment seemed to shatter into a pool of stars, spreading across his eyes.

Si Qing's self-image was overturned by his pitiful glance.

Her voice uncontrollably softened as she wrinkled her nose at him, finishing the sentence: "Be good."

"I know." The boy's long lashes trembled slightly, his voice a bit hoarse.

"I will be good."

---

chapters.title: Spoiled
chapters.content:
The 24-hour convenience store across from the central cafeteria had medical authorization. There was no povidone-iodine, but medical alcohol and disinfectant cotton swabs were available.

Si Qing slightly regretted not opening the campus running app to check in.

The amount of exercise she'd done in one night was equivalent to a day of military training.

She returned with a large bag of supplies.

Qi Fang had really listened to her; he sat there without moving.

The lamplight, like melted amber, flowed down from his soft, fluffy black hair to his shoulders.

Just seeing him sitting there alone made Si Qing's heart tighten.

On one hand, she felt sorry for him; on the other, she couldn't find the source of this feeling.

She really wanted to hug him.

But she couldn't now.

Si Qing approached, summoning her courage to poke his shoulder. "I'm back."

Qi Fang looked up towards the light, his dark eyes almost unable to focus. "Sleepy."

He definitely didn't know how beautiful he looked right now.

Si Qing's breathing shallow, she sat down beside him and patted her own shoulder.

Before she could speak, the boy lightly leaned against her.

The cheek resting on her shoulder was soft, and the hair brushing against her neck was slightly stiff.

They were too close; if he was still awake, he might hear the rhythm of her heartbeat and pulse.

Si Qing took out a few disinfectant wipes, avoiding the wounds, and carefully wiped his hands, palm, and knuckles several times.

Qi Fang was probably asleep.

She secretly extended her hand, comparing it with his in the air.

From the palm to the fingertips, Qi Fang's hand was a joint and a half larger than hers.

Suddenly, the boy straightened his back slightly and nuzzled into her neck.

Si Qing's hand, suspended in mid-air, panicked and clenched into a fist.

He turned his palm over, his scorching fingertips exploring her forearm. The back of his hand, with faint blue veins, lightly brushed over her wrist before loosely holding it, still.

"Cool."

Si Qing's mind buzzed with static, her nails almost embedding into her palm, yet her voice remained calm.

"Are you cold?"

His hand was clearly very hot.

"Here," his fingertip brushed over her pulse, "comfortable."

Si Qing was amazed to decipher the meaning from his incoherent words.

He was hot, found her body cool, and holding it felt comfortable.

"..."

Her throat tightened, as if holding a piece of half-dissolved orange candy—sweet to the point of bitterness, yet she couldn't bear to swallow it. So she let him hold it.

With her other hand, she took a cotton swab, dipped it in alcohol, and gently dabbed the red swelling on the side of his palm.

Seeing that Qi Fang didn't react, she applied a bit more pressure, wiping along the traces where the blood had spread.

"Are you taking revenge on me?"

He suddenly spoke, startling Si Qing into a shake of her hand. "Huh?"

Qi Fang pulled his hand back. "You're hurting me."

She could tell he was genuinely in pain, and the coquettish tone at the end of his words was real.

What to do? She really wanted to laugh.

"I'm sorry, I'll be gentler." She coaxed him.

"I don't want it anymore." The boy's clear, magnetic voice carried a hint of a nasal tone. "It hurts."

Si Qing, with practiced ease, pressed his hand down. "Last time, bear with it."

...

After finishing, Si Qing packed everything back into the container and opened a bottle of mineral water to hand to him.

Qi Fang obediently took a sip, then muttered, "You said it was the last time. Liar."

The spoiled little thing was throwing a small tantrum. No longer leaning on her shoulder, he took off his suit jacket and threw it onto her lap, then lowered his head to sleep.

When Tang Youmin arrived, he immediately saw the two people under the light, one dark, one light.

Iron tree was iron tree. Others would be happy to find a good opportunity for drunken ambiguity.

These two were impressive; sitting there like a game of chess, with the Han River boundary between them.

"Let's go, we're leaving." He walked over, shaking Qi Fang's shoulder to wake him up.

To be honest, he really couldn't carry Qi Fang.

It wasn't that he was weak.

Even though Qi Fang looked like he had no meat on his bones, his 193 cm height wasn't for nothing.

The last time this happened, it took all three of their dorm mates taking turns to barely get him home.

Not to mention, today Li Qingyu wasn't in the dorm, and Lu Yeti was still in the lab.

Qi Fang lazily lifted his eyelids. "Oh."

Si Qing tilted her head to look at him; he seemed a bit better now.

She folded the suit jacket over her arm and casually asked, "Does he often do this?"

"Not often," Tang Youmin draped Qi Fang's arm over his shoulder, "probably business dinners."

Qi Fang, that guy, looked like a spendthrift who didn't care about anything.

He always said he wanted to squander his father's money, but in reality, he was stubborn.

In the capital, there were few businesses that couldn't be secured by invoking his father's name.

But Qi Fang refused to do so.

He had his own ambitions and drive.

"Take Si Qing back first." Qi Fang suddenly spoke, nudging Tang Youmin's shoe with his own. "I'll wait here for you."

Tang Youmin: "You've got to be kidding me."

The plastic uncle and nephew had reached a subtle tacit understanding on this matter.

Kyoto University didn't have a strict curfew. Si Qing had informed the dormitory auntie before going out that she might return late, so there was no urgency.

The three of them slowly made their way to the West District.

The night dew, soaked in moonlight, turned into a cool mist floating on the camphor leaves, shaken off by the oncoming wind in rustling clusters.

The fabric behind her, dampened by the moisture from her hair, spread from a point into a patch, making her a bit cold.

Tang Youmin told Si Qing to put on Qi Fang's jacket.

She said her hair wasn't completely dry and would get his jacket wet, so she wouldn't wear it.

"Wear it." The man, who had been dazedly following along, blurted out a word.

After speaking, he pulled Tang Youmin to a stop and personally lifted the collar to drape it over her shoulders.

Qi Fang's jacket was very large on her.

Si Qing shrugged her shoulders, her accelerated heartbeat and uneven breathing all enveloped in his unique scent.

The boy's dark eyes intently stared at the slightly open jacket, frowning in dissatisfaction.

Not until he grabbed the lapels and completely wrapped her up like a silkworm pupa did the corners of his eyes curve.

Only when Si Qing's face turned red from his tightening did Tang Youmin reach out to pull him away.

"What are you doing, drunk?"

"Don't bother me."

Tang Youmin: ?

He was still throwing a tantrum.

A person who, when drunk, only knew how to harass cats, had now, for the first time, started bullying a young girl.

He squinted, examining for a moment, then inexplicably took out his phone, opened the camera, and started recording Qi Fang as they walked.

Si Qing: "What are you doing?"

Tang Youmin: "You don't know, Qi Fang is very talkative when he's half-asleep."

Si Qing's eyes widened in disbelief as she stared at him.

"Has anyone ever told you two that your thought processes are bizarre?"

Suddenly, it was as if they had jumped into outer space.

"Try it and you'll see. He agrees to anything when he's like this. Really."

chapters.title: Brother
chapters.content:
Tang Youmin shook him, "Give me money."

"How much?"

Tang Youmin shrugged at Si Qing, "See, you agreed."

"..." Wasn't this taking advantage of a crisis?

Tang Youmin held up three fingers, "Thirty million."

This was no longer taking advantage of a crisis.

This was burning, killing, and looting.

Qi Fang, dazed, nodded slowly, half a beat behind, "Call me dad."

"..." Even when drunk, he couldn't forget this damn rule.

Tang Youmin scoffed, teasing him, "Then won't Si Qing have to call you grandfather if she wants your help in the future?"

Si Qing was speechless. She glared at Tang Youmin, then turned back to Qi Fang.

The boy's eyes were blank, no longer responding.

Just as they reached the dormitory building, Tang Youmin took Qi Fang's coat, told Si Qing to wait outside for a while, and after settling Qi Fang, he would take her back to her dormitory.

The evening wind cut the shadows of the trees into fragments, crawling in a mottled pattern up the pure white low wall stained with the color of night.

Si Qing combed her almost dry hair to one side of her neck with her fingers, threading them through, slowly untangling it.

The spot on her wrist where he had held her seemed to still retain the sensation.

Dry, scorching, unreasonably lingering.

Suddenly, her peripheral vision caught a tall figure running towards her.

Si Qing thought it was Tang Youmin. Her deer-like eyes turned, and her gaze froze the moment she saw who it was.

"How did you run out?" She took two steps forward, asking him, "Where is Tang Youmin?"

"I hadn't finished talking."

He stopped in front of her, still a bit unsteady.

"Tang Youmin was wrong."

His eyes were covered with a layer of mist that wouldn't dissipate, blurred beyond belief.

"You should call me brother."

There was a rare seriousness in his expression. Si Qing was briefly stunned.

Seeing that she wasn't reacting, Qi Fang crouched down, staring at her, "Say something."

Si Qing came back to her senses, nodded, and looked at the fringe covering his eyes, curling her fingers.

"Okay." She said.

He was the one drunk, but it seemed to give her courage.

The girl's fair, rosy fingertips lifted, tucking away that strand of fringe.

Perhaps the ends of his hair brushed his lashes, he let out a low "mm" sound, his eyes slightly squinting.

The bright moonlight veiled the boy's brows and eyes like a thin gauze. His fox-like eyes were slightly curved, and the faint reddish tint at the corners of his eyes was strikingly beautiful.

Si Qing suddenly pulled her hand back, struggling to look away. Her eyelashes dropped, trembling slightly.

This was bad.

He was unbearably cute.

The next second, the boy's scorching warmth covered her cheek.

Her heart, like a butterfly suddenly awakened, fluttered wildly in her chest, almost breaking free from the cage of her ribs.

She held her breath, her cheek enclosed by his palm, her words a bit slurred, "What are you doing?"

Qi Fang held her face, lifting it up.

"Why touch me, but not look at me?"

Si Qing's lips parted, her voice so soft it was almost inaudible.

Qi Fang didn't hear what she said. He cupped her face, lifting her up a bit.

His gaze fixed on her lips, reading them.

The girl's lip color, pale under the night, glowed faintly in the moonlight, like petals dusted with dew, luminous and plump.

What was she saying?

He didn't know.

His Adam's apple rolled unconsciously, his mind still blank.

Suddenly, as if struck by a thought, he abruptly let go of her, took a step back, and squatted down on the spot.

By the time Tang Youmin finished washing his hands in the bathroom and came out, the ancestor who should have been sitting on the chair was gone.

He was so anxious his head hurt. He searched inside and out, even under the flower pots on the balcony, but still couldn't find a trace.

Worried that Si Qing might be cold waiting outside, he decided to take a new coat out to her first.

Rushing out the door, he took a look.

Under the tree, one person was standing bent over, and another was squatting beside them.

He didn't know why Qi Fang was giving Si Qing a hard time tonight.

Tang Youmin was just born to worry.

With these two ancestors, it was his fate.

He threw the coat to Si Qing, then pulled Qi Fang up from the ground and dragged him back.

Back in the dormitory, he was surprised to find that his good brother looked like he had known her for a long time.

His ears and neck were red.

He touched them, no fever, probably just the alcohol kicking in. He must be feeling uncomfortable now.

He quickly made a cup of warm honey water and placed it nearby, locked the dormitory door, and rushed out to take the other ancestor back.

---

The next morning, Si Qing rarely woke up last.

The girls in her dormitory had gone to bed early last night and didn't know what time she had returned. This morning, they let her sleep in a bit longer.

On the fourth day of military training, the tension wasn't as high as the previous days, and the energy wasn't as strong as the first day.

At 6:50, people hadn't all arrived yet, and a few boys' dormitories had even skipped the morning training.

The head instructor was furious. He stopped the morning training and personally went to the dormitories to get the students.

A group of people sat on the plastic grass covered with morning dew, waiting for the cafeteria to open.

After the morning training, Zhu Xing linked arms with Si Qing out of the field and met Shen Shangyue at the entrance. The three of them walked together towards the West Second Cafeteria.

Shen Shangyue took a bite of her bun and suddenly laughed.

Si Qing: "What's up?"

"It's just that the ground on our field is wet, right?"

Shen Shangyue lowered her head, her shoulders trembling slightly, "When I think of everyone on the field standing up, their butts are all cold, yet they pretend like nothing's wrong, I just want to laugh."

Zhu Xing, upon hearing this, felt like she had found a kindred spirit in the abstract race, "There are two thousand people on the entire field, so there are four thousand cold butt cheeks."

This remark was like a perfectly executed tap dance on Shen Shangyue's funny bone.

The two girls laughed until they were pounding the table.

Si Qing helplessly smiled, "As soon as you talk about this kind of thing, you go all out, forgetting everything else."

There were still over forty minutes until the training session. The three of them decided to linger in the cafeteria until 7:50.
