The cafeteria was almost empty, presumably everyone had the same idea.

Shen Shangyue ordered three more three-freshness buns and, by the way, got two cups of century egg and lean meat porridge for Si Qing and Zhu Xing.

Before long, the chatter around them gradually lowered.

This situation often occurred where Qi Fang appeared.

Si Qing instinctively turned her head, but unexpectedly met the gaze of a certain grumpy face.

She had forgotten that the one back home was also quite noticeable.

Tang Youmin's eyes curved at the ends. He had been worried about not finding a place to wait for his meal, but now he had a spot.

With a long stride, he headed straight for them.

Shen Shangyue was sitting right in front of the entrance and had noticed Tang Youmin as soon as he arrived.

Now, seeing him walk over, she had a vague bad feeling.

They were at a four-person table. Si Qing and Zhu Xing occupied one side, and she sat across from Si Qing.

Where Tang Youmin would sit was obvious.

Thus, she subtly shifted to the middle of the bench.

Tang Youmin saw through her little action's subtext.

It was nothing more than telling him not to come near.

Why? Did she own the cafeteria?

"Classmate, scoot over a bit."

Seeing that Shen Shangyue was pretending not to hear, Si Qing also pretended not to hear.

A voice that didn't belong to any of the girls at the table abruptly joined in. Zhu Xing looked up from her phone, startled.

So handsome!

This person stared at Shen Shangyue and called her again.

Zhu Xing thought she hadn't heard, so she poked her, "Little Fish, someone's looking for you."

Shen Shangyue's heart sank.

She looked up, pretending she had just heard, "Oh, you're talking to me?"

Tang Youmin gritted his teeth, looking down at her, "I said, move over a bit."

This guy was like a stick of dynamite in his stomach.

The cafeteria was still filled with empty noise.

Si Qing didn't dare to speak, lowering her head and pretending to be a quail.

Tang Youmin tapped the table in front of Si Qing with his finger, harshly, "Who did you learn this from, pretending to be deaf and blind when you see someone?"

As soon as he finished speaking, the presence of someone who wasn't even there skyrocketed.

"..."

Pretending to be deaf and blind, wasn't that Qi Fang?

Tang Youmin recalled last night and changed the subject.

"Si Qing, is there something going on between you and Qi Fang?"

---

chapters.title: Provoking
chapters.content:
After sending Si Qing back last night, when he returned to the dormitory, Qi Fang had gone to the bathroom.

The door wasn't even locked.

Drunk showering could easily cause metabolic imbalance. Worried he might pass out in there, Tang Youmin pushed the door open and went in.

Who knew the guy hadn't even taken off his clothes, standing unsteadily under the showerhead.

The water temperature wasn't very high either, probably cold when it hit his body.

He called out to him several times with no response, scaring Tang Youmin into punching him to wake him up.

After waking him, he wrapped a towel around him and took him home.

He had never seen him like this before.

Tang Youmin felt something was off.

Si Qing showed no reaction on the surface, calmly asking, "No, what's wrong?"

In reality, her hand holding the porridge cup was clenched tight.

"Impossible."

Tang Youmin narrowed his eyes at her, after a long while, "If you didn't provoke him, would he keep chasing you to kill?"

Using his clothes to strangle her wasn't enough; he even ran out of the dormitory to the school.

Presumably, before he arrived, Qi Fang had bullied her outside again. Si Qing, in a moment of urgency, had punched him in self-defense, knocking him to the ground.

This was the most plausible cause and effect he could imagine for the two of them.

A question mark slowly rose above Shen Shangyue's head.

Was it really chasing to kill, not chasing after?

Beside her, Zhu Xing was still upgrading her CPU.

Si Qing noticed she was spacing out, poked her, and then extended her palm towards Tang Youmin, simply introducing, "He's my uncle, Tang Youmin, seems to be from the School of Information."

She paused, then added, "Qi Fang is a senior from the same high school. We didn't have much interaction before, just got to know each other recently."

Zhu Xing shook with laughter, "‘Seems to be’ from the School of Information? Did you and your uncle just meet too?"

Si Qing: "A little more familiar than with Qi Fang."

Tang Youmin: "Raising a pig would be faster than getting familiar with you."

Si Qing recalled last night's phone call. Revenge was late but it came, "And you are?"

Tang Youmin: "..."

Zhu Xing laughed, leaning on Si Qing's shoulder.

As the quietest person at the table, Shen Shangyue didn't want the atmosphere to be awkward. After much hesitation, she still picked up Si Qing's words.

"Then it's my turn to introduce myself?"

Tang Youmin's gaze faltered, his Adam's apple moving unconsciously.

Then, as if nothing had happened, he pressed open his phone, his fingers swiping back and forth between various apps. Not finding one to his liking, he turned off the screen and put the phone back on the table.

Soon, his sharp ears caught Shen Shangyue's soft utterance of the word "former." His shoulders stiffened.

Former... what?

Former boyfriend?

How could she be so composed?

His eardrums buzzed, and in the haze, he heard her voice again.

"The person I was closest to a few years ago." Shen Shangyue hugged her water bottle, biting the straw and taking a sip, her tone light. "Later, I made him angry. We didn't speak for several years, and it was only recently that we met again."

Si Qing lowered her head, sipping her porridge. Hearing this, her eyes stung with acid.

Tang Youmin's fingertips moved, and under the table, his knee inadvertently touched hers.

Shen Shangyue's shoulder trembled slightly, subtly moving away.

Tang Youmin lowered his eyes, turning his face away, and stood up, "I have an early class, I'll go first."

These two seemed unaware that they couldn't hide anything.

The sense of alienation was so strong that even Zhu Xing noticed it.

Seeing that it was almost time, the three of them also packed up and strolled towards the field.

The morning's training passed with formation drills and basic first aid lessons.

At noon, Si Qing opened Qi Fang's chat box, her fingers habitually scrolling up.

The latest message was still her green bubble.

She held her phone, her fingertips rubbing the phone case, and typed a few words.

"Are you feeling better?"

After sending the message, she stared at it for a while.

Seeing no response from the other side, she turned on silent mode and climbed onto her bed for a nap.

In the afternoon, during the break, her phone had a new notification.

Sent at 15:41, about half an hour ago.

Zuoyidaibi: "I'm awake."

Si Qing asked him: "Are you uncomfortable?"

After a few minutes, he sent a "Yes."

Qi Fang woke up with a bruise on his upper arm and a few scratches on his hand.

He didn't know if it was from bumping into something last night or if someone had hit him.

He scrolled up, saw the previous messages, and his brow furrowed even more.

"..."

Zuoyidaibi: "Did I look for you last night?"

Si Qing, with her arm bent around her calf, puffed out her cheeks.

He provoked her and then forgot all about it.

Shanqing: "You called Tang Youmin, he didn't answer, so you messaged me."

Zuoyidaibi: "Then you came?"

Shanqing: "If I didn't go, you would have slept outside with the cat."

Qi Fang buried half his face in the pillow, his dimples deepening.

Zuoyidaibi: "Was I good?"

Si Qing inexplicably detected the teasing in his words.

She scrolled up to look at the message she had sent him last night. With his deliberate mention, she suddenly felt like everything had taken on a different flavor.

[Be good and stay put]

How could she say that?!

It made it seem like they were very familiar.

Her eardrums felt like they were filled with a steam engine, swelling with steam, then suddenly deflating.

She hardened her head and replied, "Alright."

Qi Fang probably knew what he was like when drunk.

It was nothing more than playing with the cat, blacking out, and then going straight to sleep.

He didn't remember, so he must have fallen asleep before Si Qing arrived.

Shanqing: "You were scratched by the cat last night. You need to get a vaccine within 24 hours."

He lowered his eyes to the small, scabbed scratches on the side of his palm, "No need, I just got one last month when I was scratched."

Si Qing buried her chin into the crook of her arm, just thinking about his chubby cat at home when she received a video from him.

The room had its curtains drawn, so the light was a bit dim.

The pure white, soft blanket was slightly wrinkled under the chubby milk cat. The cat wore a light blue shirt, its eyes round.

Its small paws, like lychee flesh, opened and closed as it kneaded the blanket.

The man's cold, fair, and slender fingers rubbed under the cat's chin.

"Tomato, greet your sister."

His voice was low and smooth, tender and affectionate.

The cat meowed softly.

The video ended there.

Si Qing shrugged, her eyes curving into small crescents.

She replayed it several times before finally shifting her attention from the adorable creature to the fact that Qi Fang wasn't at school.

It was already 4:30, and the last class ended at 5:15.

Shanqing: "You don't have class today?"

Zuoyidaibi: "I took a leave."

Shanqing: "Oh."

Qi Fang's fingertips traced circles around the cat's ear tips, his dark eyes quietly fixed on his phone.

No new messages came in for a long time.

The effects of the hangover hadn't worn off, and his head still ached.

He pressed the screen off, hugged Tomato to his chest, and rubbed his nose against the fur on its head.

After about ten minutes, a light glowed in the darkness.

Shanqing: "Are you coming back to school today?"

chapters.title: Come See Her
chapters.content:
-

There was no evening training tonight, a phased rest period, and each class was free to engage in activities.

The two class assistants from the Finance Department had already arranged a welcome team-building event at the West Campus sports field at seven o'clock in the evening.

While eating dinner with the other girls in the dorm, Zhu Xing brought up what happened that morning, and the two girls who didn't know about it had their eyes light up.

"Qing Bao, your family has such good genes!" Tan Lexi slurped a mouthful of fried rice noodles, "Your uncle is so handsome!"

Cen Weiying Ying held her phone, opened the memo app, and started typing away.

She was a novelist, and it was necessary for her to record inspirations daily.

"Based on my ten years of experience writing romance novels, your uncle and that beautiful sister are probably in a torturous love story."

Upon hearing this, Tan Lexi opened the tarot app on her phone, drew three cards for the two of them, and launched into a vivid interpretation.

"It'll work, I calculated it."

After saying that, she looked meaningfully at Si Qing and pushed her phone over, "Qing Bao, pick three cards."

Si Qing blinked, "Do I have a role in their torturous love story?"

"What?" Tan Lexi laughed at her joke, "Let me calculate yours."

Si Qing went with the flow and tapped three times, "Can you calculate my academic performance?"

The three girls exchanged a glance.

Tan Lexi: "Academic performance and wealth can be achieved through hard work, but romance depends on fate, doesn't it?"

Zhu Xing: "Encountering a bad romance can be disastrous, it might even block your academic and financial luck, so it's better to avoid it early."

Cen Weiying Ying: "Qiqing, take a look, I can't wait."

Si Qing didn't actually believe in metaphysics.

When she was a child, she went hiking with her parents and met a master at the foot of the mountain who drew a divination for her.

He said she would be a happy child, with a harmonious family and a smooth life.

Later, her parents still separated.

Tan Lexi looked at the cards, pointed with her small hand, and started rapping.

"There's a lot of romance... but that's normal."

She rubbed her chin and, following Qi Fang's lead, made up some nonsense, "Recently, there might be a man around you who is about 190 cm tall, um... he should be a handsome guy, wealthy, with good grades. He has distinct facial features, like a mole or dimples. His personality... uh, might be a bit introverted? Ah, maybe he'll be easier to talk to once you get to know him. In short, if such a person really exists, you can try to seize the opportunity."

"Oh! With these conditions, he's practically husband material."

Zhu Xing and Cen Weiying Ying could barely contain themselves.

The three of them had experience in love, so they were more sensitive in this regard than Si Qing.

What does an adult man want when he sends a WeChat message to a girl after drinking?

Even Voldemort didn't send a WeChat message to Lin Daiyu after drinking.

Si Qing didn't know if tarot could really predict such specific personal traits, but she effortlessly matched this person with Qi Fang.

As for seizing the opportunity, she was already trying.

It's just that the WeChat message she sent in the afternoon hadn't been replied to by Qi Fang yet.

-

A little later, Si Qing and Zhu Xing changed their clothes, scanned two shared bikes, and went to the West Campus sports field.

In the evening, there were many mosquitoes, and since they would be sitting on the grass, Si Qing wore a pair of jeans, a fitted off-shoulder long-sleeved top, and her half-dry hair draped over the back of her head.

Many classes were having team-building activities, sitting in circles, and a few class assistants had borrowed speakers and set up microphones in the center.

Class 1 of Finance was on the right side of the entrance, and several girls had already reserved a spot for them. When they saw Si Qing and Zhu Xing, they raised their arms and waved, "Here, here!"

Ke Mingyuan and the class monitor each carried four large bags of snacks and walked over swaying.

"Later, someone will come to join our team-building, everyone don't be restrained, just have fun." Ke Mingyuan handed the snack bags to the class monitor and the life committee member to distribute.

"Come on! The more, the merrier!"

After a few days of military training, everyone was more or less familiar with each other. Once the atmosphere heated up, someone suggested playing the bomb game.

The phone randomly timed, and each person in turn asked a question or made a request to the next person. When the phone rang for someone, they had to perform the classic party game.

— The source of all evil, the grand adventure.

After a few rounds, it was over without it being Si Qing's turn.

The boy next to her was asked to perform the grand adventure.

He had to record a video, run to the South Campus sports field, give a bottle of Pulse to the teaching assistant of the Medical School, and shout "Lu Yeti, I won't marry anyone but you," until Lu Yeti felt inexplicably confused.

"Senior Ke, who is this prank for?"

"Senior Lu is the victim of this flying disaster, hahahahaha."

Everyone around was laughing.

Si Qing was a bit distracted, repeatedly opening a certain chat interface, swiping a couple of times, and then exiting.

Then she regretted it.

She shouldn't have been so impulsive in the afternoon, asking him if he was coming back to school.

Was her intention too obvious and noticed?

She had seen the perspective of someone being secretly admired.

Knowing that she couldn't reciprocate the other party's expectations, and out of consideration, not wanting to cause too much direct harm, she would, like an ostrich, bury her head in the sand.

Would Qi Fang do the same?

Two little people were arguing in her mind.

The little white gently patted her forehead, "With over 8 billion people in the world, the probability of mutual love is negligible. How could this luck possibly fall on you?"

The little black pulled out a wolf tooth club and pounded the little white until it was bouncy, "Why did he, after drinking, not flatter Tang Youmin's face but come out to provoke you?"

Si Qing thought for a while and felt that the wolf tooth club was indeed useful.

Qi Fang was someone who couldn't stand being nagged. As soon as she thought of him, her phone, which had been dead all afternoon, came back to life with a vibration.

Qi Fang: "Coming."

Si Qing didn't react immediately, "What's coming?"

A faint, cool fragrance in the air signaled his presence.

The surrounding sounds suddenly lowered, then faded away one by one, as everyone stared in surprise at the person who naturally took a seat next to Si Qing.

Amid everyone's gaze, Qi Fang casually spoke, "I'm late, do you mind if I join the fun?"

Everyone at the Capital University knew that during these days of military training, the freshmen in the Business School had it easier than any other department.

The other departments were almost green with envy.

Once people entered university, they would gradually regress into monkeys as their high school knowledge faded.

The thing they looked forward to most every day was receiving the bananas fed by the zookeeper.

Qi Fang was that zookeeper.

Naturally, everyone liked and welcomed him.

The warm evening breeze mixed with laughter and the roar of blood rushed into Si Qing's ears, chaotically knocking on her thoughts.

Chatting with him through the phone didn't seem like a big deal.

But seeing Qi Fang in person, the memory of last night came rushing back to haunt her.

Including the nasal tone of his groan, distinctly etched into her eardrums.

...So annoying, only useless things were remembered.

Qi Fang leaned back slightly, his hand propping up the grass, and subtly turned his head towards the girl next to him.

From the time he arrived until this round of the game started, Si Qing hadn't moved an inch.

Her waist was straight, sitting cross-legged, her eyelashes lowered, occasionally trembling when the wind blew, and even her blinking frequency was low.

She was clearly lost in thought.

It was just Beijing's evening rush hour. Because of one message from her, he had driven for nearly an hour to return to school.

She was really something.

"Si Qing." He said softly.

No response.

"..."

Qi Fang, who had one leg bent, swung it casually.

Then—it collapsed.

The moment his thigh touched her knee, the girl's thin shoulders flinched.

The deer-like eyes, glistening slightly, looked over as he had expected.

Si Qing was startled by his sudden movement, forcibly pulled out of her daze, and her eyes inevitably welled up with a physiological moisture, rippling layer by layer with her shifting gaze.

The cold and sharp fox eyes softened slightly as they caught something.

chapters.title: Cat Ears
chapters.content:
Si Qing had a pair of very spirited eyes.

Being stared at by those moist, onyx-like eyes, one would inexplicably feel as if they had bullied her at some point.

But the truth was the opposite.

She was the one who bullied others.

"You called me over, and now you're ignoring me." His gaze shifted away from the moisture, not looking at her.

As if he couldn't stand that she thought he wouldn't cry.

Si Qing snapped out of her daze, her vision clearing up after a moment.

Actually, when she asked Qi Fang if he was coming back to school in the afternoon, she was wondering whether to deliver the hangover medicine and porridge to his home or have takeout delivered to his dorm.

Because Qi Fang said he felt unwell after waking up, and she was afraid he might not eat if he was uncomfortable.

That would upset his stomach, and he might get sick without realizing it.

But Qi Fang seemed to have misunderstood her intention.

If she explained now that she didn't mean to ask him to come back, he would probably get angry and scold her for being heartless.

After a moment of thought, Si Qing curved her eyes slightly and took out mosquito repellent from her bag.

The boy from the neighboring class who was singing "The Tibetan Plateau" strained his voice with a loud "ah."

Si Qing found the right moment when everyone was cheering and handed him the item, softly saying, "Qi Fang."

Qi Fang indeed didn't hear her.

She raised her voice slightly and called him a few times symbolically.

Finally, she reached out her fingertip and gently poked his forearm.

The surrounding laughter and noise hit a small lull, and those emotionless black eyes looked over.

Si Qing pursed her lips, her deer eyes innocently staring at him, speaking first, "Aren't you going to acknowledge me anymore?"

She knew Qi Fang was being petty and needed coaxing.

But if she started coaxing him right away, he would take advantage of her.

Qi Fang was the best at acting spoiled; she had to be even better at it than him.

"Hmm?"

"Maybe it was too loud over there, you didn't hear me speaking, did you?"

After saying that, she paused for a breath, secretly observing.

The boy's eyebrows slightly lifted, and the fake double folds created by his eyebrow arches softened a bit, as if he couldn't believe what he had heard.

Before he could react, she blinked and continued, "Can we call it even?"

Qi Fang finally figured out what she meant.

First, she pitifully stared at him, put a label on him, then gave him a way out, pulling the conditions to an equal level.

Tsk.

She had him wrapped around her finger.

Qi Fang lifted his eyelashes, his beautiful fox eyes glancing over with a sidelong look, "Sure I have no temper?"

Si Qing: "..." Where did he have no temper?

You had the most temper.

Under his sinister gaze, Si Qing felt inexplicably guilty, biting the soft flesh inside her cheek, and quietly shifted her gaze to a place where he wasn't.

Qi Fang was almost amused by her, his gaze falling on the girl's soft cheek, grinding his teeth.

He wanted to pinch her.

But he was afraid of hurting her; this little delicate thing might cry if he pinched her.

Annoying.

"This time I'll let you off," he narrowed his eyes, with a clear warning in his gaze, "Next time you ignore me, I'll beat you up."

"And I won't coax you even if you cry." He added in a harsh tone.

Si Qing turned her head to look at him, the corners of her eyes and eyebrows tinged with a bright and gentle smile, "There won't be a next time."

The girl's tone was soft and gentle, her words flowing smoothly, with a hint of subtle coquettishness that was neither flattering nor overly sweet.

Previously, Tang Youmin had mentioned in passing that Si Qing's hometown was probably Shencheng, a southern girl with her own accent.

Qi Fang really liked her voice.

"Here." Si Qing opened the cap of the mosquito repellent spray and placed it near his hand, "Spray some, or you'll get bitten later."

He lowered his eyelashes, "Oh."

Before the new round of the game started, the unlucky guy who had been sent to the South Campus sports field to gross out Lu Yeti returned triumphantly.

The boy ran back joyfully, only to find his world collapsing.

His hard-earned prime spot next to Si Qing!

Who was so dishonorable as to raid his home while he was at his most vulnerable?

He stormed over, saw who it was, and then meekly left, going to sit with his meal buddy.

The game went on for a few rounds, and all the mean tricks had been played, so they switched to exploring the three gardens.

"Let's agree first, no using people's names as answers," Ke Mingyuan clapped his hands, "Capital University campus landmarks."

There were too many things to mention, and after two rounds, the remaining options were not many.

All that was left in Si Qing's mind was the heart-shaped dragon fruit steak from the Western restaurant under the Management School building.

"Dragon fruit steak." Qi Fang lazily spoke up.

"..." Si Qing choked, her deer eyes lifting slowly and turning towards him.

Qi Fang watched as the girl's cheek curve puffed up in a pout, and one of his eyebrow tips lifted.

Si Qing regretted for the first time sitting next to Qi Fang.

"I plead guilty." She helplessly shrugged, "I really can't think of anything else."

The girl sitting next to Ke Mingyuan stood up with her phone, "Come on, come on, the girls' grand adventure is drawn here."

Before the team-building started, Ke Mingyuan had declared that the grand adventure for girls should not be too excessive, and any physical contact with the opposite sex should be avoided entirely, so he had specifically asked the life committee member to prepare a few easy-to-complete tasks for emergencies.

"Rabbit ears, dog ears, cat ears hand gestures, three consecutive shots, share to the group."

"I'll take the photo, I'll take the photo!" Zhu Xing was the first to raise her hand, opening the camera, "I'll guard my treasure's beauty!"

Another girl ran over with a flashlight, "Then I'll handle the lighting!"

Zhu Xing found the right angle, chatted with Si Qing to make her laugh, and pressed the shutter at the most natural moment.

Si Qing had a cold and detached appearance, but her clear, moist deer eyes neutralized some of the coldness brought by the sharp angular lines, and when she smiled at the camera, her eyebrows and eyes came alive with brightness.

"Beautiful." Zhu Xing clicked her tongue, admiring her own masterpiece while cueing the next action, "Now it's time for the cat ears."

The cat ears pose required both hands to make a "yeah" gesture, flipped upside down and placed on top of the head.

Si Qing's off-shoulder top today was short, and raising her hands would inevitably pull the hem up.

The previous two poses had already been a bit extreme.

She put down her arms and pulled at the hem of her top with her hands behind her back.

The man who had been sitting next to Si Qing watching the show inexplicably stood up and walked to her diagonal rear, kneeling on one knee.

After playing together all evening, the classmates were no longer surprised by this.

After all, throughout the evening, Qi Fang had been sitting with his posture leaning towards Si Qing as if he wasn't afraid of a curved spine. When Si Qing handed him things, she also seemed to habitually place them near his hand.

Their body language was enough to show they knew each other.

Perhaps they were quite familiar.

Feeling the boy's slightly higher body temperature wrapping around her, Si Qing's hand, which was pressed against her lower back, stiffened. She lifted her chin and looked back, "What's wrong?"

The girl's butterfly bone pressed against his upper abdomen as her upper body turned slightly.

Qi Fang's posture didn't change, "Need a hand?"

Si Qing didn't realize what he meant by "need a hand" and instinctively thought he was going to help her pull down her hem.

He had a previous record.

Last time on the sports field, he casually tucked candy into her waist.

Anticipating a blush, she stopped in time and didn't think further, instead tightly covering her waist.

The next second, two soft and heavy sounds collided.

"Not allowed..."

"Help you make cat ears."

chapters.title: Group Photo
chapters.content:
Si Qing froze like a stalled machine, her blood boiling as it rushed to her cheeks.

She snapped her gaze back, her voice muffled, "Oh."

Qi Fang lowered his eyes, his fingertips brushing against Si Qing's soft hair. He looked up and asked Zhu Xing, "Like this?"

"Ah," Zhu Xing snapped out of her daze, finally pulling her smile—almost as bright as the moon—back into place. "Just stay in this pose, don't move."

She suppressed her smile, observing the height difference between the two, adjusting the frame ratio, and included Qi Fang in the shot.

In the photo, the girl had graceful shoulders and neck, with a few strands of black hair hanging by her neck. Her small, porcelain-white face was stunning, and her hands were clasped in front of her as she sat obediently in the front.

The boy had sharp, refined features. Below his high nose bridge, his beautiful lips curved in a slight arc. The aggressiveness from his top-tier bone structure was almost softened by the faint affection in his eyes.

The blurred lights in the background, the warm tones, and the whale-blue sky after dusk complemented them perfectly.

Two faces that could be considered works of art.

Great. No words were needed.

After confirming with Si Qing that no edits were needed, Zhu Xing sent the photo to the group chat.

Ke Mingyuan added, "This is an internal photo. Don't share it outside without their permission."

"We know, we know! We wouldn't do that."

Immediately, a flood of message notifications sounded.

The entire class lowered their heads, their faces illuminated by their phone screens.

Qi Fang's gaze lazily swept around, his knee bumping into Si Qing's. "Everyone's excluding me."

Zhu Xing heard and slapped her forehead. "Oh right, right, right! Senior, I'll AirDrop it to you."

Si Qing: "!"

She had thought Qi Fang wasn't in the group and wouldn't see the photo, so he wouldn't bring it up.

But she hadn't considered that everyone was looking at the group chat, and he was the only one left out. He would throw a little tantrum.

Regardless of his intentions for wanting the photo, Si Qing had one thought in her mind now.

Every girl wants to be a little more perfect in front of the person she likes.

So, at the very least, shouldn't she edit the photo a bit before sending it to Qi Fang?

She blinked at Zhu Xing, but unfortunately, her cute little sister was looking down at her phone, not receiving her distress signal. Instead, she delivered a devastating blow.

"Senior, do you want a solo photo of Qingbao too?"

Qi Fang leaned back lazily, indifferent. "Sure."

"OK, sent it to you."

Si Qing's fingertips dug into her knuckles, crumbling silently.

Noise and light overwhelmed the moonlight as the team-building event reached its second half. Si Qing received a notice about an emergency meeting from the Organization Department.

"Where's the meeting?" Qi Fang asked her.

Si Qing replied in the group chat, then turned to him, "Building Seven."

"Oh." He stood up with one hand on his knee, interlaced his fingers, and stretched his arms in front of him. "Coincidentally, I'll go there too."

Si Qing suddenly had the illusion that stars had been falling on her head lately.

In just a few days, she had seen Qi Fang more often than in the past three years combined.

It was as if the empty candy jar she had carefully held onto had suddenly been filled with a few star candies by him.

Si Qing glanced up and saw Qi Fang talking to Ke Mingyuan.

She silently sped up her packing, picked up her bag, stood up, and walked over. She briefly explained the situation to Ke Mingyuan, said goodbye to everyone, and left first.

Qi Fang had his hands in his pockets, lazily following half a step behind her.

Si Qing looked down at the group messages, her peripheral vision catching the shadow of the man on the ground. As the light slanted, their shadows briefly touched, overlapped, and then separated.

As if driven by something, her fingertips swiped, turning on silent mode, then opening the camera interface and manually turning off the flash.

She slowed her pace, as if cautiously probing something. The pounding and tightening in her chest became clear.

Until she successfully captured the moment when their two shadows touched, and she pressed the shutter.

Then, as if granted amnesty, she sighed in relief, turned off her phone, and turned around.

The surrounding music was noisy. Qi Fang noticed she wanted to speak and bent down to listen.

He was afraid this little rascal would catch him not listening to her again.

"Qi Fang, have you eaten?"

"No."

"Was the cafeteria already out of food when you arrived?"

"There was, I'm not hungry." He countered, "What's wrong? Haven't you eaten?"

Si Qing said she hadn't.

In reality, she had eaten, but if she told Qi Fang the truth, there wouldn't be a good reason to take him to eat.

"There's a dessert shop near Building Seven. My roommate said the crepes on the second floor are very good."

She was afraid he wouldn't eat, so after thinking for a moment, she added, "It's sweet."

She knew Qi Fang liked sweets.

Before, near Shancheng No. 1 Middle School, a pop-up dessert shop had opened. Her best friend, Lian Zi, was an absolute fan of green grapes and had dragged her there on the first day of business.

That day, Si Qing had unexpectedly seen Qi Fang through the window.

He was wearing a black bomber jacket zipped all the way up, holding a pink bear bag from the dessert shop.

Tang Youmin was waiting for him on the side of the road with dinner, curiously looking at the bag's contents, taking something out, and curiously taking a bite.

In the end, he got a light slap on the arm.

Tang Youmin wasn't convinced and elbowed him back, only to get kicked in the end.

It was then that Si Qing realized that Qi Fang knew her somewhat unfamiliar uncle.

Not far away, Zhu Xing was eating sunflower seeds, watching the scene with a few other girls, completely engrossed.

The incandescent light from the top of the fence splashed onto the girl's hair, lifted by the evening breeze, and the boy's raised hem of his jacket.

The girl tilted her chin up, saying something to the boy. The boy's broad back slightly hunched as he leaned in to listen, his half-shoulder width passing the girl's waist's curve.

"Does anyone think their height difference is really attractive?" one of the girls beside her sighed, opening the last photo in the group chat.

The boy had almost completely enveloped the girl sitting in front of him with just over half of his body.

Si Qing was tall and slender, but not excessively thin. She had a slim waist, long legs, and was softly plump where she needed to be.

As her roommate, Zhu Xing knew how well she ate every day.

Qi Fang had broad shoulders and a narrow waist, a rare male physique that still showed a noticeable height difference when standing next to Si Qing.

"And their faces are so authoritative."

Halfway through her sentence, one of the girls suddenly remembered something and interrupted, "Hey, isn't Qingqing from Shancheng No. 1 Middle School?"

"Didn't someone say before that Qi Fang was also from that school?"

"That's why I thought they seemed to know each other!"

"Speaking of which, Tang Youmin from the School of Information is also from that school, right?"

"Wasn't that fairy-like girl from the School of Engineering at the new campus popular a while ago also from there?"

"..."

"Wait, is that school just full of good-looking people?"

---

chapters.title: Fragrance
chapters.content:
There was still about half an hour before the meeting, so the two decided to dine in.

Previously, when they had eaten together, Si Qing had felt that Qi Fang seemed to have a low appetite.

Today, she found out that he was incredibly picky.

He ate strawberries but not strawberry jam. He got tired of cream after just a little, and he didn't eat the crepe skin.

After picking and choosing, he only ate a few strawberries and the top layer of caramel.

On the other hand, she, guilt-ridden, devoured an entire matcha bretzel crepe.

Between the Fifth Cafeteria and Building Seven, there was a small artificial forest. Si Qing spotted two couples sitting in the pavilion from afar.

A few days ago, after training, she and her roommate had passed by here. Si Qing had wondered if the couples would end up chatting with the ones next to them by accident.

Tan Lexi had said that couples had their own barriers; once they cuddled, they would be completely absorbed.

The moonlight, like clear varnish, filtered through the sparse foliage and spilled down, creating irregular patterns on the wooden path.

Two sets of footsteps, staggered, stepped onto the wooden planks. Suddenly, Qi Fang seemed to think of something and called out to her.

"Si Qing."

She looked up in response, "What's wrong?"

"What does 'not allowed' mean?" he suddenly asked, out of the blue.

But Si Qing instantly knew what he was referring to.

—Just now on the field, when taking photos, he had offered to help her, and she, in a moment of absurdity, thought he was going to help adjust her clothes. She had instinctively said, "Not allowed."

Her deer-like eyes curved slightly as she seamlessly added the second half of the sentence, "Not allowed, it would tire you out."

Si Qing felt she had made great progress; now she could lie to Qi Fang without batting an eye.

A pair of bright, smiling fox-like eyes, which she couldn't see the end of, lowered to stare at her, capturing a moment of panic, and the corners of his eyebrows lifted pleasantly.

"Liar."

Si Qing: "..."

She didn't know what to say.

Qi Fang leisurely glanced at her, his fingers itching every time he saw the curve of her cheeks.

He had wanted to pinch them for a long time.

He knew it was bullying to treat a little girl like this.

But.

He wasn't exactly a good person.

Moreover, had Si Qing ever been easy on him?

Qi Fang wasn't this patient with anyone else.

So, what was wrong with pinching her?

He wouldn't hold back.

"Tell the truth."

His arm loosely wrapped around the girl's shoulders, and from the other side, he poked her cheek.

His fingertips sank into the softness, warm and smooth, like touching silk-wrapped cotton. It slightly gave way, then was gently pushed back by a resilient force, slowly rebounding.

Fun.

Before Si Qing could speak, he poked her a couple more times.

Si Qing stood frozen, her breathing light.

Their shadows, outlined by the moonlight, seemed intimate.

But in reality, they were far from that.

In Qi Fang's eyes, she only saw a hint of curiosity, not affection.

Yet he still teased her consciously.

The girl's long, fine lashes trembled. "Don't do that."

The cicadas' long drones and the rustling leaves mixed, spreading into this quiet corner.

"So, the 'not allowed' you said was this?"

He raised an eyebrow. "Not allowed to bully you?"

Si Qing choked.

"Si Qing, tell me, how have I been bad to you?"

He had never bullied her before.

How could Si Qing be so afraid of him?

And that "not allowed."

Qi Fang had never been told "not allowed" by anyone except when he burned the school's wires in high school and was called in by the principal.

It annoyed him.

He bit his fang lightly against his tongue. "Did I call you a little white-eyed wolf for nothing?"

Si Qing, pinned by his arm, couldn't speak and muffled an "mm."

Ah, ah, ah, ah!

She couldn't break free!

Si Qing had no choice. She raised her hand to hold his wrist, and with the other hand, she gripped his index finger, prying it open. "Qi Fang."

The girl's voice was soft, without any intention of acting cute, but the nasal tone carried a genuine coquettishness that hit his eardrums.

Her entire hand, even when gripping, was still shorter than his index finger.

Such a small thing, yet she held him so tightly.

Qi Fang loosened his grip and asked in a deep voice, "Does it hurt?"

Si Qing pulled his hand away from her face. A faint pink mark was visibly spreading on her cheek.

Qi Fang's gaze darkened as he looked at it.

Si Qing took out her phone, the screen black, and checked the two small red marks on her cheek under the moonlight. She raised her hand and patted them.

She knew Qi Fang hadn't used much force.

This little mark would fade away with a bit of wind soon.

"It doesn't hurt," she said.

The air was filled with the warm, slightly damp fragrance of grass and trees, occasionally mixed with the crisp scent of pomelo leaves, belatedly wrapping around her nose.

Si Qing's hand, pressed against the back of her phone, was covered with a thin layer of moisture. She slightly tilted her wrist.

The corner of the screen reflected her eyes, and behind her was the boy's broad shoulders and the small section of cold, white collarbone peeking out from under his shirt collar.

"..."

She suddenly came to her senses and took a big step forward.

She tried her best to ignore the tension that swept over her, pulling on her backpack strap as she walked forward. "I'm leaving first, I'm almost late."

The few strands of black hair hooked on his chest slowly fell, the moving air carrying a fragrant scent.

A woody, minty fragrance mixed with a faint shampoo scent.

Si Qing took two steps away, then turned back to say goodbye.

With every meeting with him, she wanted a proper beginning and end.

"Watch the road." he said.

chapters.title: Accompanying Her
chapters.content:
The Seventh Teaching Building was a self-study building. It wasn’t until they reached the sixth floor that Si Qing finally slowed her pace. When the shadow behind her drew near, she looked up. "Are you also attending the Organization Department's regular meeting?"

"Ran so fast earlier like a rabbit, and now you finally ask me."

"Why didn’t you say anything?" she asked. "If I knew you were coming, I would’ve waited for you earlier."

Qi Fang walked up beside her, lowering his voice to mimic hers. "Why didn’t you ask?"

"I thought you were coming to the Seventh Teaching Building to study."

Qi Fang gave a low chuckle. "Idiot."

Si Qing’s eyes widened slightly. "Why are you cursing at me?"

"Just because." He slowly withdrew his gaze, stuffed his hands into his pockets, and lengthened his stride, leaving her behind.

"..." So unreasonable.

The two of them entered the classroom through the back door one after another. Qi Fang took a seat right by the back entrance. Si Qing followed him in, ignoring the large empty spaces in the front rows. She gently pulled out a chair separated by one empty seat from him and sat down.

From the corner of his eye, he caught sight of the well-behaved little girl sitting beside him. Qi Fang crossed his long legs, leaning his upper body slightly toward her. "Am I disturbing your meeting?"

Si Qing took off her bag and placed it on the desk, turning her head as she replied, "No, you’re not."

"Oh." The boy leaned forward onto the desk, burying his chin in the crook of his arm.

After a moment of silence, his pale, upturned fingertips tapped the desk beside him. "Then sit here."

"Come over and help me block for a bit. I want to sleep." He stretched out his legs, the tip of his shoe nudging hers.

Occasionally, Si Qing would think that this man was a combination of a kitten and a fox.

Flirting and teasing seemed as natural to him as breathing.

And yet, he himself seemed completely unaware of it.

"You can sleep if you want to. Why do you need someone to block for you?" Si Qing grumbled, but still moved her things to the desk next to him, got up, and shifted over.

A faint woody fragrance from the girl’s hair drifted lightly into the air as she moved.

Qi Fang’s gaze followed the strands of her hair that fell onto the desk, absentmindedly speaking, "I’m a good student."

If this had been back when Si Qing first entered high school, she would have believed him without a doubt.

Later, someone pointed out those new buildings on Mountain One’s campus to her. Only then did she learn that they were all donated by Qi Fang’s father after he caused some major trouble.

She heard that during a physics experiment, he did something that fried the school’s electrical circuit, resulting in a half-day holiday for the entire school.

Students from those years at Mountain One could still recite lines from his written self-reflections.

This man, even when standing under the national flag reciting his self-criticism, carried himself with such spirit that it seemed like he was being commended. Holding the microphone, he would solemnly spout nonsense, turning his self-criticism into a post-mortem analysis, with not a hint of remorse, which amused the principal to no end.

His exploits were numerous and included, but were not limited to, keeping cats and hedgehogs in his desk, messing with the multimedia display to an irreparable extent—even the information technology teacher couldn’t fix it. Eventually, they gave up and he restored it himself. And so on.

He didn’t smoke, didn’t drink, didn’t fight. He was purely a source of trouble for his father.

As Tang Youmin put it, Mountain City No. 1 High School had its own Bichon Frise.

But the principal, teachers, and students all liked him.

So much so that when he later transferred, the entire school, regardless of age or gender, felt a pang of reluctance to see him go.

Si Qing blinked. "You’re quite famous."

Qi Fang could tell the little girl was teasing him about his notorious high school antics. He curled his lips and gave a soft snort. "You don’t remember any of the good things I’ve done, but you remember every little bad thing, huh?"

"I don’t think they were bad things."

Just then, Chen Chengyan entered through the front door, stepped onto the podium, and tapped the standing microphone. "Let’s begin the meeting, everyone, please quiet down."

Qi Fang hadn’t heard her response. He turned his head, shifted positions, and rested his head on his arm, closing his eyes. "Wake me up when it’s over."

"Okay."

Si Qing said they weren’t bad things because back in high school, the only times she could see Qi Fang extra were when he was called to the office or asked to give a speech or self-criticism at the flag-raising ceremony.

Although Mountain One had east and west campuses, they were separated only by a library.

The teacher’s office building, the main sports field, and the gymnasium were all shared.

Si Qing’s homeroom teacher was the head of the first-year grade, and all the grade leaders and directors shared the same office.

So, apart from the weekly flag-raising ceremony and the annual sports meet, the place where she was most likely to run into Qi Fang was the director’s office.

Provided, of course, that Qi Fang had caused trouble and her homeroom teacher happened to need her.

This did require a bit of luck.

Unfortunately, Si Qing wasn’t particularly lucky.

Fortunately, Qi Fang was a troublemaker.

So, despite the low probability, she still managed to encounter him.

At that time, Qi Fang had been called to the office for not wearing his school jacket and was left to enjoy the air conditioning. The teachers were called away to a meeting, but before leaving, they gave him a set of math papers—apparently for the next weekly test for the first years—and asked him to work out the answers.

Later, only Si Qing, the class academic representative, and Qi Fang remained in the office.

Qi Fang hadn’t brought a pen and came over to ask for one.

During free activity time in PE class, Si Qing had been silently memorizing Chinese texts and happened to have a pen in her pocket. She casually pulled it out and handed it to him.

After that, there was no further interaction.

Organizing the newspapers took about 20 minutes. When Si Qing looked back at him, Qi Fang had already finished.

He was lazily leaning against the windowsill, gazing at the scenery below, drawing something on the back of the test paper.

A small pile of candy wrappers was stacked beside his hand.

To finish so much candy in 20 minutes—she didn’t know whether to praise his teeth or his health.

Seeing how absorbed he was in his drawing, Si Qing gave up on the idea of asking for her pen back.

Arm in arm with the academic representative, she passed behind him, "casually" glancing at his artwork.

In four words: shocking and appalling.

It was to the extent that no carbon-based life form could appreciate it. Si Qing couldn’t bring herself to love the house and the crow in it.

This man wrote a hand of sharp and stylish running script, but his drawing skills were unexpectedly impressive.

After leaving the office, the academic representative leaned in to whisper to her, careful not to let the great artist inside hear.

"Qingqing, do you think the senior drew a stick with a lump of... shi on it?"

"It’s a tree, probably." Si Qing quickly interjected.

The other girl gasped in a hushed voice, "Ah, you can see that too?!"

"Maybe?" she smiled.

In truth, Si Qing hadn’t been able to tell what he was drawing.

She was just looking at the tree, while he was looking at her.

---

The main topic of tonight’s meeting was to discuss the process for the Academic Career Planning Competition. Dai Wan and Chen Chengyan had designed several interactive activities, which were then comprehensively revised based on the suggestions of those present. Finally, the two hosts were instructed to rehearse privately to avoid any mishaps during the official competition.

As the meeting ended, Dai Wan and Chen Chengyan carried their tablets, discussing the plan as they walked. The other students dispersed in small groups.

A few girls passed by the back row and, noticing the boy asleep next to Si Qing, deliberately lowered their voices to greet her.

"Si Qing, aren’t you leaving?"

Si Qing smiled. "In a bit. I just need to pack up."

"Oh, okay," one of the girls glanced at the boy slumped beside her and whispered, "Did your boyfriend come to keep you company at the meeting?"

chapters.title: Favor
chapters.content:
Si Qing’s eyes widened abruptly. Almost instantly, she reacted. "He’s not my boyfriend."

The second half of her sentence, "He didn’t come to keep me company at the meeting either," was still on her lips when she saw the girls smiling and flashing an "OK" sign. "Oh, sorry about that."

Earlier, when Si Qing and Qi Fang had entered through the back door, the students in the front were deep in conversation. The freshmen hadn’t seen much of Qi Fang in person, so no one would have guessed that the person asleep here was Qi Fang.

But it was clear that this boy was top-tier in every aspect—possibly even a great-looking guy.

His attire was stylish and refined, exuding an air of elegance with every strand of hair.

Moreover, for someone of Si Qing’s caliber—a beautiful and intelligent woman—ordinary people wouldn’t catch her eye.

The fact that she allowed this boy to sit beside her and keep her company likely meant there was something between them.

The girls waved at her with hushed giggles, "Then we’ll leave first. Bye-bye."

Their voices gradually faded away, leaving only the two of them in the large classroom.

Si Qing withdrew her gaze and reached out to poke Qi Fang’s shoulder blade. "Wake up."

To her surprise, he propped himself up almost instantly, his eyes still drowsy.

Si Qing’s heart skipped a beat as she pulled her hand back. "You weren’t asleep?"

"Just woke up." His voice carried a faint nasal tone and a slight hoarseness.

"Oh." Si Qing didn’t ask further. She lightly brought up the topic the girls had mentioned. "Are you leaving then?"

The boy’s sharp fox-like eyes showed no emotion as he slightly lowered his lids, staring into the distance. "My legs are numb. I’ll wait a bit."

Si Qing nodded absentmindedly, her thoughts consumed by whether he had overheard the girls’ words. She began to pack her things into her bag one by one.

Suddenly, she heard a soft chuckle.

She came back to her senses. "What’s wrong?"

"You might as well pack me into your bag too."

Si Qing’s fingertips paused. She looked down at the two phones in her bag.

"..."

She felt so stupid she could cry.

A wave of helplessness, like searching for poison only to find it was dog urine, washed over her.

She closed her eyes in despair and took out Qi Fang’s phone to hand it back to him.

He rested his chin on his hand, watching her. "So natural."

Her habit of blushing whenever he teased her really needed to change.

"Next time, I won’t be so natural."

...

When Si Qing returned to her dormitory, it was already 10:30 PM. She greeted her roommates and then slipped into the bathroom for a quick shower.

Her palm glided over the mirror, which had been fogged by the steam, leaving a clear streak.

In the mirror, her fair cheeks had a faint blush. She reached out to poke and pinch them.

It felt like Qi Fang’s fingertips were still there.

He seemed unexpectedly slow in this regard, lacking any awareness of boundaries between genders.

Ruffling her hair, holding her wrist, cupping her face—these seemed to him like mere physical contact, nothing special, just things he did on a whim.

But Si Qing hadn’t noticed him doing the same with other girls.

Indeed, he was an unpredictable wind, free and unrestrained, coming and going as he pleased.

If he was happy, he would linger at your fingertips a little longer.

But if one day he decided to leave, no one could stop him.

Yet the tree, its heart filled with wind, could only cherish the fluttering, waiting day after day for the wind to favor it once more.

It wasn’t fair.

So today, she had mustered her courage, reached out, and touched her wind and moon.

The damp mist in the bathroom seemed to seep into her entire noisy heart. Something suddenly became clear.

—She seemed to finally be able to, just a little, yearn for the moon.

---

Men’s Dormitory 102.

Ke Mingyuan had brought over a video of Lu Yeti being proposed to tonight for everyone to enjoy. Li Qingyu was laughing so hard he was nearly in tears.

Lu Yeti was swamped with work. After returning from the sports field, he had been busy with the Student Union’s tasks. The forms submitted by the staff under his department were a mess, and he was now typing away furiously on his keyboard.

Tang Youmin came in from the balcony after finishing a cigarette just as Qi Fang emerged from the bathroom.

"You shower how many times a day?"

Earlier that morning, he had seen Shen Shangyue, and since then, Tang Youmin had been annoyed with everyone. He would curse at anyone he passed, even a stray dog.

It was just Qi Fang’s misfortune to appear at the wrong time.

"What, you’re unhappy?" Qi Fang flicked his damp hair back with his fingers, casually tossing it behind his head before slumping into a chair, his long legs sprawling out in front of him.

Tang Youmin lifted his leg and kicked him. "I’m so unhappy I could die."

"Oh, too bad." Qi Fang leaned back in his chair, unusually not kicking back.

He curled his fingertips into his palm, a smirk playing on his lips. "I’m so happy I could die."

Silence fell after his words.

Li Qingyu and Ke Mingyuan, who had been laughing, almost choked, their laughter dying abruptly.

Li Qingyu’s neck twitched as he turned his head. "Bro, do we really need to tell you guys everything?"

Normally, his brother might dress a bit flashy and talk a bit wild, but he didn’t think he’d actually share the feelings he got while... in the shower.

Tang Youmin clicked his tongue. "Are you in heat?"

Qi Fang shot him a sideways glance. "Did your aunt come to visit?"

Tang Youmin: "..."

Li Qingyu: "Neither of you should talk."

One was being lewd, the other was angry.

Tang Youmin fell silent and returned to the balcony for another cigarette.

Qi Fang could see he was frustrated. He casually ruffled his hair, picked up his phone from the desk, opened the Publicity Department group chat, and found a screenshot to send to Tang Youmin.

Tang Youmin, with his elbow propped on the windowsill, suddenly saw his phone screen light up.

The screenshot Qi Fang sent was of a short video social platform account.

Tang Youmin never browsed short videos; he didn’t even have the app on his phone.

His gaze lingered on the ID. As if possessed, he downloaded the app, but when he opened the search bar, his fingers seemed glued in place, hovering there.

It was no exaggeration to say his hands were shaking as he typed.

【Year After Year, There Are Fish】

He knew who this person was.

65 videos, mostly vlogs of scenery. Only one featured her.

Tang Youmin clicked on it.

The video was posted four years ago in April.

The screen was bathed in a warm glow, the high-saturation orange hues soaking the sky. The girl smiled brightly, making a big peace sign at the camera.

The light haloed her brows and lashes. Driven by her vibrant energy, his fingers swiped to enlarge the image.

He stared for a while. The background music looped several times before he finally let go.

chapters.title: Dogged
chapters.content:
On the seventh day of military training, the phrase "freshmen are inexplicably busy" was perfectly embodied in Si Qing and Tan Lexi.

During the day, they played the role of soldiers, and after evening training, they had to run around campus. Back in the dorm, they still had to work late on club activities.

Si Qing was fine, but Tan Lexi had been cursing for three days straight.

The high-frequency words in their dorm these days included, but were not limited to, "that Lao Liu," "damn Lao Liu," and "Brother Liu is here again."

Lao Liu was a person's name.

Rumor had it that her direct supervisor was surnamed Lu, who was sharp-tongued and passive-aggressive, and always sent her work messages while she was watching dramas—pure Lao Liu energy.

As she put it, every day was like having an affair with the WPS Office suite; as soon as night fell, she had to open it for a visit.

Crude words, but the sentiment was real—though the words were indeed crude.

Right now, she was still in the dorm, tallying data in a spreadsheet, while Si Qing casually took her and Cen Weiying's phones to check in for the campus run.

As for Zhu Xing, she faked a leg injury and sweet-talked her crush of four years into running for her for a day.

Si Qing had arranged to meet with Shen Shangyue. They ran from the Accounting College teaching building to the entrance of the Third Teaching Building, passed the West Second Cafeteria, then ran to the North Stadium, and finally back to the Accounting College teaching building. The main roads they passed along the way happened to form a heart shape.

The entire run took a little over forty minutes, burning off their energy. The two of them strolled back leisurely.

Passing by a shop, Shen Shangyue confirmed that Si Qing wasn't on her period, then dashed in to buy two ice pops.

They found a long bench outside, sat down, and enjoyed their ice pops while catching the breeze.

Shen Shangyue leaned back on the bench, letting out a long sigh. "I'm so tired these days. Almost every department has events coming up, and we have to follow and take photos. These days, I have to attend meetings with each department. I'm about to die from all the meetings."

She counted on her fingers, "There's the Hundred Societies Battle, the Model United Nations Foreign Language Drama Competition, the Debate Society's debate competition, and so on. But the most urgent is your department's event. Last time, it was Qi Fang who attended the meeting."

"Your Organization Department has quite the influence, even able to get the president to attend."

Si Qing nodded. "Yes, our department head and Qi Fang have a good relationship."

Chen Chenyu was from the Law School. Before Qi Fang transferred to the Business School, they were in adjacent classes, had the same professional course teacher, were in the same innovation and entrepreneurship group, and were part of the same student organization. So, it made sense that he was close enough to Qi Fang to get him to attend meetings.

Shen Shangyue tilted her head. "You and Qi Fang have a good relationship too."

Si Qing unconsciously swung her legs, lowering her gaze to her knees, which occasionally bumped together. She spoke softly, "I wouldn't say it's very good, but I guess we've become a little more familiar."

With more frequent encounters, she could gradually relax around him. But sometimes, she still struggled to keep up with his conversations.

A little discomfort was inevitable. After all, it was hard to be completely herself in front of someone she had liked for a long time.

Shen Shangyue looked at her with a smile, saying nothing.

Some people's kindness had to be felt by Si Qing herself to count.

An outsider's excessive reminders would only diminish the surprise she felt when discovering those feelings, and that experience was precious.

She could sense that Qi Fang felt differently about Si Qing because she had seen with her own eyes what Qi Fang used to be like.

From Shen Shangyue's perspective as an ordinary classmate with no admiration filter for him, Qi Fang was not exactly indifferent, but he didn't seem to care much about most people or things.

He was polite yet distant, with social boundaries so well-controlled they were almost perfect.

He seemed equally close and distant to everyone, but in reality, apart from the people he truly recognized—close family or friends—no one else mattered.

It was as if maintaining a relationship with him was a one-sided effort from the other party.

Yet, this person, who was so emotionally detached, had chased a girl after drinking a few days ago.

Alcohol was supposed to liberate the nature of those who suppressed themselves for a long time, wasn't it?

Qi Fang was something else.

After liberating his nature, he had completely transcended human behavior—utterly dogged.

And dogs were sincere and honest creatures. If they liked someone, they wagged their tails and followed them everywhere.

In this regard, Qi Fang was very much like the Tang Youzhen of the past.

Because she had truly experienced that straightforward and passionate liking, she could see at a glance that Qi Fang felt differently about Si Qing.

The two girls chatted away, rambling from club activities to where they would go after military training ended.

At one point, Shen Shangyue noticed the streetlight above was just right, so she pulled Si Qing into a few selfies.

As they took photos, they realized the wind felt particularly nice tonight. The two of them actually sat there willingly, feeding mosquitoes for over half an hour, happily collecting more than three hundred photos with almost identical angles and expressions before heading back to the dorm.

The Accounting College teaching building was closer to the South District. Shen Shangyue walked Si Qing back first, then continued a bit further to her own dorm.

She lived in Building 15 of the West District. Fortunately, it was a co-ed dorm building, and at this time of night, the courtyard was practically no different from the area below the girls' dorms.

Under the trees, by the walls, couples were everywhere.

Shen Shangyue walked close to the edge of the dormitory building, tilting her head to watch a particularly passionate couple locked in an embrace by the wall.

Suddenly, something sharp and angular lightly tapped the top of her head.

It wasn’t heavy, but it felt like a phone had dropped and hit her. Instinctively, she raised her hand to cover her head and looked up.

Her gaze collided with a pair of calm, expressionless phoenix eyes.

The boy looked down, the edges of his pupils reflecting the bright light from the dorm room. His forearm rested on the balcony railing, his long, slender fingers loosely holding a phone.

Tang Youzhen stood quietly there, staring at her without a word.

Shen Shangyue took a step back. "Why did you hit me? Did I disturb you?"

Tang Youzhen's gaze flickered, turning his face slightly into the shadows. "No."

They stood in silence for a while before Shen Shangyue looked up to meet his gaze again. "If there's nothing else, I'll go then?"

Tang Youzhen didn’t move or speak.

Shen Shangyue took two steps forward, standing on her toes. "Bye."

The summer wind rushed through the window, stirring her hair. The sound of cicadas was all gathered and thrown into her eardrums.

In this bustling place, only here was silent.

After a moment, the boy lowered his gaze again, glancing lightly at the girl who hadn’t moved.

The outline of his face was rendered with a faint silver edge by the warm white streetlight. His eyes were as clean and soft as ever, but his voice was cold and hard.

"Aren’t you leaving?"

Shen Shangyue raised her hand, tucking the hair blown by the wind back behind her ear. "But you didn’t say bye."

The moonlight was soft and bright, diffusing over the girl’s slightly smiling eyes. "So I guess... you don’t want me to leave."

---

chapters.title: Goodnight
chapters.content:
Tang Youzhen was a meticulous and sensitive person.

Back when they were still together, a "bye" and a hug were always a must before parting.

Shen Shangyue’s mother was strict, and her holidays were almost entirely filled with cram schools.

It was tiring, but attending classes was the only free time she had away from her mother’s watchful eye.

Between her English and physics classes, there was a three-hour gap. During that time, Tang Youzhen would bring her favorite little cake and come find her.

They would go to quiet places like the city library or a café and spend some time together.

It wasn’t exactly a date, just a change of scenery for studying.

After finishing their homework, they would read or chat for a while, and then he would take her back to the cram school.

Before parting, he would hug her at the building entrance, burying his face in her shoulder and neck, grumbling about how time passed too quickly.

Shen Shangyue would check the time and say she had to go, bidding him farewell.

He wouldn’t respond. Instead, he would bury his face deeper, pulling her up slightly by the shoulders and holding her tightly, saying he just needed one last half-minute.

So she guessed that Tang Youzhen not responding to her goodbye was because he didn’t want to part.

Or perhaps—

"Do you have something you want to say to me?"

The boy’s eyelids twitched slightly, his lips parting but no sound coming out before he tightened them again.

Shen Shangyue tilted her head. "Then I really am leaving?"

He lifted his chin slightly. "Go."

As if anticipating his words, her voice came almost simultaneously, overlapping the end of his sentence.

"Just kidding, I’m not leaving."

The girl’s light-colored eyes were filled with moonlight, shining brightly.

Seeing that he still hadn’t reacted after a long while, Shen Shangyue stood on her toes, reaching up to grab the windowsill, leaning as close as possible. "I’m not leaving."

The evening wind rustled the treetops, and a few birds flapped their wings and flew away.

The sound of fluttering feathers struck his eardrums, and Tang Youzhen suddenly came back to his senses.

"You—" He let out a syllable, his voice hoarse.

His Adam’s apple moved as he moistened his throat, then spoke again. "Don’t you have something to say to me?"

For Shen Shangyue, the barrier between them was like a thorn lodged between her ribs—every heartbeat reminded her of its presence.

But if Tang Youzhen had decided to move forward, she would convince herself to slowly digest it.

After all, it was she who owed him.

But since he asked, did that mean she still had a chance?

"If I say I do... will you listen?"

The boy’s dense, long lashes were tinged with silver by the moonlight. His phoenix eyes, glistening softly, remained fixed on the girl for a long time.

She was smiling, but Tang Youzhen felt that the eyes beneath those long lashes seemed to be dripping, as if caught in a light rain.

Even after all these years, he still couldn’t bear the sight of her looking at him with such grievance.

After a moment of silence, he compromised. "I’ll listen."

Shen Shangyue nodded, her tone light. "Then can you wait a bit? I need to go back and draft something first."

"??"

His heart was about to jump out of his chest, and that’s what she wanted to say to him?

"You need to draft a speech to talk to me?"

She pressed her lips into a smile. "You’re different from others. I get nervous."

"..." He tapped his phone case with his fingertips, his voice suddenly softening. "Oh."

"Then, see you next time?"

"Mmm."

"Goodnight?"

"Mmm."

Shen Shangyue didn’t move. "All you say is 'oh' and 'mmm'."

The boy lifted his eyelashes, pressing his index finger against her forehead and gently pushing her back. "It’s late. Go back, or you’ll be late for training tomorrow."

Shen Shangyue brushed the dust off her hands. "Alright, I’m going back then."

The girl’s high ponytail swayed with her quick steps. Tang Youzhen rested his elbows on the balcony railing, watching until she entered the neighboring dormitory building before withdrawing his gaze. He moved his lips as if murmuring to himself.

"Goodnight, little fish."

---

Si Qing returned to the dorm, and after washing up, she curled up in a chair. She and Shen Shangyue selected the best photo from the hundreds they had taken, attached it to tonight’s campus run check-in, and posted it on WeChat Moments.

Almost instantly, a like appeared.

Si Qing didn’t need to guess—it had to be her mom.

She scrolled to the top and saw [Qin, Female] and her eyes curved into a smile.

Her mom rarely missed her posts, always being the first to notice her updates.

[Qin, Female]: Is our little star working again?

Qin was a very trendy person, young at heart, and loved to play along with the younger generation. There were a few times when she went shopping with her mom and they were stopped by street photographers. Qin would confidently swing her bag and pull Si Qing along to pose for them.

Si Qing replied to her mom’s comment: Maintaining exposure, there’s a new movie coming out soon.

[Qin, Female]: Okay, big star, don’t forget to save two tickets for me and your Uncle Tang.

[Qin, Female]: Three tickets, including Xiao Wen.

[Tang Youzhen] replied to [Qin, Female]: I’m not going.

Si Qing: "..."

She suddenly wanted to delete this post.

More likes and comments gradually appeared. When the familiar profile picture of a cat and dog in a World War II battlefield appeared, she buried her face into her knees.

Qi Fang had seen her post too.

Her phone buzzed, and a new message notification popped up at the top.

坐以待币: Tired these days?

The last time she saw Qi Fang was three days ago. Dai Wan had given her the task of writing a documentary plan for the Academic Career Planning Competition. When she needed to coordinate with the Publicity Department, she could message Qi Fang.

Although such matters were usually easier to handle between the staff members, Qi Fang was kind and said it was fine to contact him.

山青: A little. I just finished the storyboard and am about to work on the plan.

坐以待币: What time is it? Look at the clock.

山青: 10:18

A sudden, soft chuckle came from the boys' dorm.

Who asked her to report the time like a machine?

Tang Youzhen turned his head. "What’s so funny all of a sudden? It’s creepy."

It seemed like a laugh, but in reality, he had no comeback.

Qi Fang ignored him, lowering his head to type: Go to sleep, you have military training tomorrow.

山青: Aren’t you in a hurry for the plan?

坐以待币: I’m not that unreasonable.

As Si Qing received the message, Tan Lexi on the bunk above suddenly sat up, pausing her drama, and yanked at her pajama collar in furious helplessness.

"I’m going to dig a tunnel and assassinate Lu Yati—"

Si Qing turned her head and saw the girl stomping down the ladder, sitting in her chair, opening her laptop to have an affair with WPS.

"Your director is looking for you again?"

Tan Lexi’s face was pale with anger as she showed her the phone.

老六: Have you checked the data?

搞点夜宵七七叭: Can it wait until tomorrow, Senior? I’m about to sleep.

老六: What time is it? Look.

搞点夜宵七七叭: Are you in a hurry for it?

老六: If it’s not urgent, then don’t do it? There’s no other work after this?

搞点夜宵七七叭: Senior, can you be reasonable?

老六: I’m from the Student Affairs Office, not a place for reasoning ^_^

Si Qing pursed her lips and silently turned off her phone.

chapters.title: Little Pig
chapters.content:
The next day, the temperature was too high. By the time it neared noon, several people had been heat-stunned, so the instructor temporarily changed the training to watching national defense propaganda films.

The entire school was gathered in the third-floor exhibition hall of the Science Hall. The Finance Department, with its small number of students, was always squeezed into a corner.

With nearly a thousand people from the whole school crammed into the same space with their small stools, the carbon dioxide they exhaled was enough to make someone dizzy.

Si Qing was tall, so she stood in the last row of the girls, right in the corner by the wall.

Dizzy from the carbon dioxide, she looked around. Within her line of sight, a sea of black heads swayed rhythmically as they moved their necks.

Her position was like a throne. Not only could she lean against the wall to sleep without risking a fall from the stool, but there was also a thick load-bearing column in front of her, which not only kept her cool but also gave her a sense of security, making it unlikely she’d be spotted by the instructor.

This was the reward for drinking four cans of milk every day during her puberty growth spurt.

She took off her cap and placed it on her lap, then leaned back and fell into a comfortable sleep.

Feeling safe from the instructor’s notice, she allowed herself to relax a little.

She never expected that someone with exceptional height could spot her slacking off through the high window by the back door.

Since it was the first day of the second week of military training, the counselor was also free, so he called Qi Fang over to the school with a phone call and handed him a few discipline assessment forms.

Originally, he hadn’t woken up properly and was annoyed to death. Carrying a folder, he came to inspect the training. Everyone he encountered along the way had a bad expression.

He didn’t expect this trip to yield an unexpected gain.

He walked over, his back to the column, and squatted down facing Si Qing.

The little girl had a rather pleasant sleeping posture.

Her head tilted against the wall, a few loose strands of hair hanging at the corner of her mouth. Her long, fine lashes had a natural curve, occasionally trembling.

Qi Fang had a slight case of OCD. It wasn’t serious, but right now, he found the stray hair on her cheek unbearable.

His fingertips moved slightly, and as if possessed, he reached out, tucked the hair away from the corner of her mouth, and smoothed it behind her ear.

Then, satisfied, he poked her cheek.

It was a bit warmer than that night, soft, and his fingertip sank in as if he wanted to pinch it.

Perhaps sensing his presence, the girl’s brows furrowed slightly.

A soft, low voice brushed past his eardrum, and it felt as if an invisible thread in his spine had been yanked, sending an electric, tingling sensation all the way to the back of his neck.

Qi Fang’s gaze darkened. He withdrew his hand and rubbed his earlobe with his bent finger.

...

Si Qing was in a deep sleep and had no sense of time.

She woke up a few times in between but quickly fell back asleep due to the dizziness from the carbon dioxide.

Her neck was uncomfortable, so she changed positions several times. Later, she didn’t know what she was resting her head on, but the height was just right.

The last time she opened her eyes, she saw a hand loosely holding a phone.

The skin was cold and pale, the knuckles long, and there was a sexy little dimple between the thumb and wrist, filled with light streaming in from the high window.

Her drowsiness completely vanished.

Qi Fang was here again?

This time, he even brought a folder, so he must have really come to inspect.

And she had just happened to fall asleep right in his line of sight.

Just as she was struggling with whether to continue pretending to sleep or to face the storm, the boy’s voice covered her ear from the side.

“Do I have to wake you up myself?”

Si Qing’s shoulders stiffened. She straightened up with a whoosh, her hands pressed tightly against her thighs, sitting as obediently as a primary school student.

After a moment, her doe eyes blinked in embarrassment. “I’m up.”

Qi Fang lightly tapped her forehead with the folder in his hand. “Good afternoon, little pig.”

Si Qing choked. She had no justification, so she could only weakly protest in a small voice, “...I’m not.”

“You are.”

She was so asleep that she couldn’t even be bothered to move. Waking up and then falling asleep again—wasn’t that just like a little pig?

Seeing her toss and turn, her neck must have been uncomfortable. She’d probably have a headache when she woke up.

Qi Fang’s heart softened, so he squatted down to let her rest her head on him.

Now, she had slept for nearly an hour, and it seemed she had slept very well.

She was sitting, and he was squatting. When his legs went numb and he changed positions, the height of his shoulder dropped slightly, and she would wake up.

There was nothing he could do, so he squatted back down.

Si Qing glanced at her watch. Her doe eyes suddenly widened. “I slept this long?”

Qi Fang lowered his head and chuckled softly. “Maybe because it was comfortable resting on me.”

Si Qing raised her hand to press her burning earlobe and tucked a few strands of hair behind her ear.

She tugged at the boy’s clothes. “You should sit here.”

Qi Fang found it amusing and raised his eyebrows slightly. “Conscience finally kicking in?”

“I didn’t know you were here. I didn’t mean to use you as a pillow,” she poked his upper arm again, urging him to sit quickly. “You should rest for a while.”

Si Qing was wearing her military training uniform, so she didn’t stand on ceremony. She hugged her knees and sat down on the floor.

“Come back and sit.”

The exhibition hall’s air conditioning was set low, and the floor was cold. Qi Fang grabbed her arm and, like lifting a chick, pressed her back onto the chair. Then he stood up and stretched.

Si Qing tilted her chin up to look at him. “Were you squatting this whole time?”

The girl’s clear, moist eyes held an indistinguishable mix of guilt and something else. In any case, she looked pitiful.

Qi Fang’s dark eyes shifted slightly, and his palm rubbed the soft top of the girl’s head. “You’ve learned to care for others.”

Si Qing slightly shrugged her shoulders, letting him ruffle her hair. She mumbled, “Don’t change the subject.”

“I just arrived.” He withdrew his hand, and his beautiful fox-like eyes hooked into a charming smile. “I saw you sleeping soundly from outside.”

Si Qing puffed out her cheeks. “So you came over?”

He neither confirmed nor denied, and his fingers flipped open the folder cover, picking up the page with the table and holding it up for her to see.

On the page with the header “Discipline Violation Record,” there were dense rows of Si Qing’s name.

Qi Fang had beautiful handwriting.

Each stroke was well-defined, with slightly elongated vertical folds, leaning towards a slender Jin style, yet not overly meticulous.

It was very much like him—unconstrained and free-spirited.

Suddenly, she realized something.

“...” That’s not right.

After a moment, her doe eyes slowly widened: “?”

Finally, she looked up at Qi Fang with almost disbelief: “!”

Was she crazy? Here she was, looking at her name filling up half a page of violations, and she was still distracted by his handwriting.

“I came to inspect,” he said with a smile, his eyes bending like a fox’s.

Si Qing’s gaze swept around. Without exaggeration, within a 10-meter... 15-meter radius, she was the only one awake.

Then she looked back at the absurd violation record.

After a day of military training, her usual points were now in debt to him by 200.

The girl’s clear black-and-white eyes were filled with disbelief. “Everyone was sleeping, and it’s all counted against me?”

She didn’t know if it was because she had just woken up, but her face looked completely dumbfounded.

“Yeah,” he said, the dimple at the corner of his mouth more pronounced than ever. “I don’t know the others.”

“Aren’t you just bullying me?”

Si Qing realized he was teasing her again. She let out a breath of relief, but her true personality couldn’t help but show a little.
