To the point where, for the first time ever, as if she had eaten the heart of a bear or a leopard, she raised her fist and gently nudged his upper arm.

Qi Fang’s eyes filled with even more amusement.

She had hit him so gently and softly that if someone saw it, they might think she was being coy rather than angry.

So cute.

“You let me sleep, and now you won’t even let me bully you a little?”

---

chapters.title: Aspiration
chapters.content:
Qi Fang was the kind of person who did everything with confident justification.

Si Qing’s breathing became shallow. “Didn’t you say you were reasonable?”

At least last night, he had been reasonable.

His pupils were dark, and his black eyes stared at the girl’s slightly flushed cheeks. “When I was being reasonable, you didn’t listen to me.”

“Ah.” Si Qing shrank her neck, guiltily averting her gaze.

As for why she felt guilty—

—Last night, Qi Fang had told her to go to bed early, and she hadn’t listened.

Tao Leqi had gotten out of bed to work, and Si Qing thought, maybe she should keep her company downstairs. After all, it was only a little past ten, and she wasn’t sleepy yet.

She was the type who, once on vacation, would finish all her homework in one go so she could play without a care afterward.

As a result, the two of them worked until they lost track of time, burning the midnight oil until nearly 1 a.m.

During the morning break, she had fallen asleep leaning against Zhu Xing.

Qi Fang’s fingers lightly traced up her chin, lifting her gaze.

“What time did you go to bed last night?”

“...” He had found out.

Si Qing’s gaze was firm. “Eleven.”

“Eleven?” He narrowed his eyes. “Wasn’t it one?”

“.........................”

If melancholy was a talent, then Si Qing was gifted right now.

“But I finished the plan,” she blinked. “From now on, I won’t stay up late. I’ll go to bed early every day.”

Qi Fang silently raised an eyebrow. Si Qing interpreted this as: Keep talking.

She curled her fingers, which were resting on her legs, and her nails scraped over her index finger’s knuckle. Hesitantly, she lifted her eyelids.

Qi Fang’s cold face was truly a bit fierce.

The sharpness from his clean-cut profile was on full display, and the fake double eyelid created by his deep-set eyes intensified as he looked up, staring at her without blinking.

The pressure was overwhelming.

She raised three fingers. “I swear.”

She pursed her lips, then added a fourth finger. “I swear on four, I definitely won’t sleep during training tomorrow.”

Qi Fang’s brow twitched slightly. He didn’t understand how her mind had jumped to this.

Staying up late could lead to low blood sugar, and with the heat, a little sun exposure could make her dizzy.

He said she shouldn’t have stayed up late, but she thought she shouldn’t have violated the rules by sleeping.

She couldn’t even be coaxed to the point.

So stupid.

Si Qing pouted, mustering her courage to stretch out her fingertip and touch his hand hanging by his side. “Qi Fang.”

The girl’s fingertips were soft, a little cool. The moment they touched the back of his hand, she quickly pulled them back.

His pale eyelids lowered. “Hmm.”

“Want to have dinner together tonight? The instructor said there’s no evening training tonight.” She curved her eyes. “If you have time, we can go out to eat. Whatever you like, my treat.”

Still a cold face.

But the dimple had just sneaked out to greet her, then disappeared again.

Did inviting him to dinner seem to work? Si Qing wondered.

But this person was a bit hard to please.

Seeing that he didn’t seem to want to respond to her immediately, Si Qing reached out and tugged at his clothes. “Did I say something?”

Qi Fang repeatedly pondered her words, “Did I say something?” The more he thought about it, the funnier it seemed.

The tip of his tongue hooked at the corner of his mouth, and he couldn’t help it. He turned his head and laughed.

“Alright, let’s go out to eat.”

---

The documentary ended at 4:30 p.m., and with less than half an hour left before the end of training, the instructor decided to let them off early.

As October approached, the days grew shorter, and the sunlight at 5 p.m. was not overly harsh.

Qi Fang had changed into a light blue denim suit. Standing lazily under the camphor tree across the street with one hand in his pocket, he was slightly lowering his head to look at his phone.

Si Qing and Zhu Xing walked out of the entrance arm in arm and spotted him immediately.

The boy was tall and straight, and the dappled light and shadows from the leaves rippled from his hair to his shoulders like water.

Si Qing tilted her head slightly, puzzled.

Qi Fang had returned to the school to submit the forms at around 3:30.

They had agreed to go out at 5:30. Si Qing needed to change clothes and freshen up, and Qi Fang could rest a bit in the meantime.

It wasn’t time yet.

After a moment of thought, Si Qing concluded that he was probably waiting for someone else.

“Qingbao, that’s Senior Qi Fang over there. Shouldn’t we go say hello?”

Si Qing nodded and agreed.

The two of them walked toward the other side of the road. Behind them, three girls jogged past, stopping not far from Qi Fang.

The girls’ hair flew in the wind, and even from their backs, it was clear they were excited.

Si Qing had seen this scene countless times before.

Back in high school, smartphones weren’t allowed, so many girls from the East Campus would sneak over to the West Campus during the break before evening self-study.

With exquisite envelopes tucked in their arms, they would try their luck at the basketball and badminton courts. If Qi Fang was there, they would secretly slip the letters into the bottom of his bag.

They didn’t disturb him, and it seemed they didn’t expect a response. They just wanted to convey their feelings.

Because the moon was the moon—no matter how much you reached out, you couldn’t touch it.

It was less about liking him and more about admiration.

Zhu Xing nudged Si Qing’s arm and covered her mouth. “Oh my, am I actually seeing Senior Qi Fang, the acting king, playing dumb?”

Si Qing silently pressed her lips together, suppressing the inexplicable tightness in her heart, and nodded.

People who secretly admired someone didn’t even have the courage to say they liked them, let alone the right to be jealous.

The girls stopped in front of Qi Fang. The one in the middle was pushed forward by her friends. “Senior, do you have a moment to listen to what she has to say?”

Qi Fang lifted his eyelids, glanced at the girl who had been pushed forward, turned off his phone, and gave a low “mm.”

The girl smoothed her bangs, lowering her head. “Hello, Senior.”

“I went to the same high school as you, um... Beijing Guanghua. Later, we were in the same competition group,” she said, her fingers tightly gripping the seam of her pants, her voice soft as she moistened her throat and continued. “Do you... do you remember me?”

“Sorry, I don’t recall.”

“Ah, it’s okay. It was a long time ago.” The girl smiled. “You probably don’t know, but I’ve always... always ad... admired you. Coming to Beijing University to see you was my goal.”

“I came to tell you that I also got into Beijing University. I was this year’s top student at our school. Although I’m not as good as you, I’ve already achieved my dream.”

“If I hadn’t met you, I probably wouldn’t have been able to keep going.”

“Even though you might find it a bit out of the blue, I still wanted to thank you.”

Qi Fang gave a slight nod. “Congratulations, you’re amazing.”

“Thank you,” she took half a step back, gave a slight bow, “Sorry to have taken up your time, goodbye, Senior. Wishing you a bright future.”

With that, she pulled her two friends and ran off.

The crowd at the entrance of the Science Hall gradually dispersed.

Zhu Xing rubbed her chin. “That girl must like Senior Qi Fang, right? Why did she say ‘admire’ instead?”

Si Qing stared in the direction the girl had left, the cool wind hitting her face. Only then did she realize her eyes were burning.

Just like her.

chapters.title: Tenderness
chapters.content:
"Eavesdropping?"

Qi Jing's pleasant voice reached her. Si Qing instinctively turned her face away from him, blinking gently to ease the stinging in her eyes.

"Oh, Senior, hello. We weren't eavesdropping." Zhu Xing looked up. "We were lining up to greet you."

"Senior, hello." Si Qing was lost in her own thoughts, completely unaware of her faint nasal tone and the slight furrow between Qi Fang's brows.

Zhu Xing glanced at the boy staring intently at her sister, and a brilliant idea flashed through her mind.

"Senior, want to have dinner with us later? Our evening training was canceled today."

Qi Fang lowered his gaze, still processing Si Qing's cold and distant "Senior, hello."

*Does she have a split personality?*

It had been less than an hour since they last saw each other. How had he gone back to being just "Senior"?

He recalled the time he took her out to eat alone. The little girl had been so restrained, as if he were trying to snatch her money. Whenever he got too close, her hands would tightly clutch her small bag, as if it held something precious.

Did he look that broke?

He didn’t understand.

He wasn’t well-versed in the psychology of little girls and didn’t realize that her ever-changing emotions were all because of him.

He assumed she was just uncomfortable at the thought of having to deal with him alone again.

With her sister around, maybe she’d give him a few more smiles.

"Then invite your roommates too. My treat."

Si Qing blinked, unsure how this had suddenly turned into a dormitory gathering.

But if Qi Fang didn’t mind, she was fine with it.

The main thing was to keep him happy.

Zhu Xing made a "no" gesture with her hand. "No need for you to treat us. We’ll Venmo you later. If you think there are too many girls, you can bring your roommates too. More people, more fun."

After settling on a meeting time, the two girls said their goodbyes to Qi Fang and prepared to leave.

They had barely taken two steps when Zhu Xing habitually reached for Si Qing’s hand—only to find empty air.

She turned back in surprise to see her ethereal sister being carried off like a kitten by the much taller boy.

"Uh, Zhu Zhu, I’ll be back soon."

Zhu Xing’s cheekbones twitched, but she just flashed an OK sign and left first.

The summer wind devoutly carried the faint scent of flowers, and the rustling leaves lingered over the quiet clearing.

The boy’s long fingers were still hooked around the back of her collar. Si Qing could even feel the warmth of his touch through the thin air at the nape of her neck.

She didn’t change her posture, tilting her chin slightly to the side. "What’s up?"

What she didn’t know was that from this angle, Qi Fang could clearly see her lashes, clumped together from the moisture.

His gaze darkened, his black eyes fixed intently on that glistening spot.

As if possessed, his palm cupped her soft cheek, his fingertip gently brushing beneath her eye to wipe away the tears.

Si Qing instinctively tried to pull away, but his palm pressed against her chin, lifting her face higher.

"Why are you crying?"

Si Qing froze. Her hand, hanging at her side, slowly clenched into a fist until her nails nearly dug into her palm.

Some emotions came out of nowhere, surging and scorching, climbing back up to her eyes.

There was no absolute empathy in the world, but she could relate to the girl’s feelings from earlier.

Si Qing, too, had persisted in coming here because of Qi Fang.

She wanted to see him but didn’t dare say she missed him. She could only say she longed for Beijing.

Because Beijing was where he was.

In the 944 days she couldn’t see him, Si Qing had never relaxed for a single moment, fearing that if she slackened even a little, she would never see Qi Fang again.

Later, when Tang Youmin also went to Beijing, she lost all access to news about Qi Fang.

For a while, she had been terrified—terrified that he might have found a girl he liked, terrified that when they met again, he would have forgotten her.

The unknown filled her with confusion.

She was left alone in the mountain city.

It was so hard to see Qi Fang again.

She had to fight her way out of a million test-takers in the mountain city to earn this chance.

The hardship in between was something she couldn’t afford to look back on.

She feared that if she did, she would never be able to take another step forward.

Her emotions unraveled like a sweater with a pulled thread—the more it was tugged, the more it came apart.

In the past, she had suppressed them for so long that she hadn’t even felt the grievance.

But once someone asked her why she was crying, her heart softened, and that taut string snapped.

Qi Fang watched as the girl’s eyes filled with tears, until they could no longer be contained, falling one by one into his palm.

Cold, yet scalding.

He had grown up believing nothing could disrupt his rhythm or rules.

Si Qing’s tears came without warning, and suddenly, he couldn’t tell whether the salty tightness in his throat was from panic or something else.

Qi Fang didn’t have time to think.

He wrapped his arm around the girl’s thin shoulders, his palm cradling the back of her head as he pulled her into his embrace, patting her back gently to soothe her.

"There, there, big brother’s got you."

He didn’t know how much time passed. Listening to the girl’s sobs turn into quiet whimpers, his Adam’s apple bobbed repeatedly before he finally found his voice again.

"How did you end up so wronged?"

His voice was so soft it seemed afraid to startle her.

Si Qing’s face was buried in his chest, her hand clutching his side tightly.

Hearing Qi Fang’s voice, she regained some awareness, but her emotions were still out of control. Afraid she wouldn’t be able to explain later, she quickly came up with an excuse.

"…Qi Fang."

"I’m here."

Her voice was muffled through his clothes. Once her sobs subsided a little, she continued, "Can you…"

"Yes."

"I haven’t finished—"

"I can do it."

Qi Fang’s palm patted the back of her head. "Take your time."

Si Qing sniffled and hummed in agreement, speaking slowly. "The military training results count toward the public required courses… I don’t want to fail."

Qi Fang’s arm around her shoulders stiffened. A single syllable squeezed out from his throat.

"Huh?"

"Did you deduct my usual points?" This was another source of her grievance. "I’m doomed."

Qi Fang felt like the folds of his cerebral cortex had all unfolded.

"I know I was wrong. I shouldn’t have fallen asleep…"

Could he even speak? He was so angry he almost laughed.

"Si Qing," Qi Fang ground his teeth, lifting her delicate, fragile neck with his hand and pulling her out of his embrace. "If you dare say that the reason you’re crying like this is because of *that*, I will actually hit you."

Si Qing, feeling guilty, bluffed, "Assaulting a minor carries a heavy sentence."

"…"

He could tell she had cried enough to joke with him now.

Unfortunately, Qi Fang wasn’t in the mood.

---

chapters.title: Mind Your Own Business
chapters.content:
A laugh of ambiguous meaning rumbled in his chest. His thumb and forefinger pinched her chin, pressing firmly against her tear-stained cheek as he rubbed it hard several times.

Si Qing let her head sway with his movements, loosening her grip on his clothes. She patted his side.

"Slow down."

"No use acting cute."

His hand around the back of her neck tightened slightly. Si Qing sensitively shrank her neck, and her gaze flickered. She unexpectedly noticed a few dark stains on his chest where the tears had soaked through.

Qi Fang also noticed the marks Si Qing had left on him. He tugged at his lips.

"Cried your heart out." He pinched her soft cheek between his fingers, lifting it up, and gritted his teeth as he praised her, "Impressive. A true artist."

"…"

She would petition to classify Qi Fang’s mouth as a controlled weapon.

Si Qing carefully examined his buttons, roughly estimating how expensive the shirt was.

Clothes from this brand had to be sent to a specialized care shop for cleaning.

Previously, Ms. Qin had been obsessed with the brand’s style and bought many of their pieces, but later, due to poor maintenance, she had ruined several of them with her carelessness.

"Take off your jacket and give it to me. I’ll have it cleaned and return it to you."

"I don’t have a habit of making girls run errands for me." Qi Fang wrapped an arm around her shoulder, turning her in the opposite direction. "Let’s go. I’ll walk you back to your dorm."

Si Qing nimbly slipped out of his embrace. "No need to walk me. It’s not far from my dorm. You go do your thing."

If she refused, he didn’t insist on escorting her.

Qi Fang pulled a neatly folded slip of paper from his pocket, pinched one corner, and smoothed it out, tapping it with his fingertip. "See this?"

Si Qing lifted her gaze, her tear-laden lashes trembling.

It was the disciplinary form filled with her name, with an unflattering stick-figure pig drawn at the bottom, its head surrounded by a few "ZZZ" snoring marks.

His drawing skills were still as… moving.

"You came here to show me this?"

"Was I supposed to keep it without showing you? What if you really failed military training and blamed me?"

"I wouldn’t blame you."

Si Qing shook her head, her doe eyes curving into a smile. She almost said, *You’re the best*, but thinking it sounded like she was being coy, she changed it at the last moment. "You’re such a good person."

He scoffed, refolding the paper and lazily placing it on top of her head.

Once it was secure, he spoke again. "Go on. See you later."

Si Qing took the small object from her head and pressed it to her chest. Only after his figure disappeared from sight did she suddenly regain her senses.

All her strength had been drained from holding back earlier. She slowly squatted in place.

The boy’s voice, so gentle it seemed to dissolve in the wind, still echoed in her ears, refusing to fade.

A fierce, icy, and sharply fragmented gust of air suddenly surged from the depths of her chest, rushing to the top of her head.

---

The dinner location was a popular barbecue restaurant on the backstreet of Jingda University.

Tan Lexi’s personal recommendation—quality guaranteed.

Dian Shangyue had also heard of this place. Normally, reservations had to be made a day in advance. Today, not only was it a last-minute decision, but Qi Fang had also secured a large table.

"Probably the power of money." Cen Weiying opened her notebook and jotted down a note.

—*[Young Master even reserves the largest table for barbecue]*

Zhu Xing blinked. "You’re writing *this* down?"

Tan Lexi: "Let her be. She’s been cramming for two days. She’s a little unhinged now."

In the end, the girls arrived first, taking one side of the sofa and leaving the opposite side for Qi Fang.

The warm, bright lighting outlined the rising wisps of smoke, and the lively chatter mixed with the smoky aroma filled the air.

Occasional clinking glasses and laughter added to the lively atmosphere.

"Rumor has it the owner opened this place because his wife loves barbecue, and he was worried about hygiene outside, so he started his own restaurant." Dian Shangyue said, "I saw on Xiaohongshu that many people say the owner is very kind and always gives discounts."

"Those who love their wives thrive." Tan Lexi looked around. "His wife must be an extraordinary person."

As soon as she finished speaking, a crisp snap of fingers came from above.

"You’re right. My wife *is* extraordinary." A young man with dark green hair propped himself up on the back of their sofa with one hand, smiling brightly. "Ladies, you’ve got taste. I’ll give you a discount."

Tan Lexi’s face lit up with delight. "That generous? Thank—"

Before she could finish, a lazy male voice behind her committed an act of banditry, casually snatching the money away.

"Free meal." Qi Fang placed a milk tea on the table and sat down on the opposite sofa. "Thanks."

The girls’ eyes nearly popped out of their sockets. They decided that if the owner came after them, they’d run first.

"Qi Fang, you—"

The bandit justified his actions. "Didn’t I say thanks?"

The owner was exasperated. "Should I kneel and kowtow three times, pull out a banner that says *Warm Welcome to Young Master Qi* to make it better?"

"You’re the one without shame, not me."

"…Fuck." The owner instantly lost all will and means to argue.

Si Qing lightly nudged Qi Fang’s shoe with her own, whispering, "You know him?"

"Friend."

Qi Fang didn’t acknowledge many as friends.

The owner sat down next to him and gave a simple introduction. "Zhou Qi’ang. Went to the same high school as him. Just kidding earlier. This meal’s on me. Don’t stand on ceremony."

Tang Youmin and Li Qingyu parked and came in, casually dividing the milk tea on the table.

The group of guys were all familiar with each other. Zhou Qi’ang looked around. "Titi’s not here? Busy again?"

Li Qingyu took a sip of his milk tea. "Yeah, after her shift at the infirmary, she goes straight to the lab."

Then, shifting gears, he turned to the girls across the table, earnestly warning them, "The doctor on duty at the infirmary has changed this week. Not as easy to fool as last week. If you want to fake a faint, just lie down on the stage. Don’t go to the infirmary for the AC. Better to be a little hot than to get a shot."

Zhu Xing stretched her neck. "What do you mean?"

Li Qingyu wiggled his fingers. "The senior on duty this week is sleep-deprived and carb-deficient. His temper? Almost as bad as your Senior Qi’s."

Zhu Xing: "Senior Qi has a great temper, right? Don’t you agree, Qingqing?"

Si Qing nodded.

Qi Fang lifted an eyelid, meeting that pair of clear, guileless eyes.

There wasn’t a hint of insincerity or sarcasm—she genuinely meant it.

But anyone in the room who knew Qi Fang would find the statement surprising.

Zhou Qi’ang bumped shoulders with him. "Not like you at all."

Qi Fang’s long lashes lowered, the light casting fine, dense shadows beneath his eyes.

"Mind your own business."

chapters.title: The Button
chapters.content:
It really didn't suit him.

Zhou Qi'ang had met Qi Fang only after Qi transferred to Beijing Guanghua. Among this group, Tang Youmin was the one who had known Qi Fang the longest.

He knew Qi Fang’s character too well.

—He had a face that made every strand of hair seem to have a girlfriend, yet he was completely oblivious to romance.

Not the kind of oblivious where he couldn’t tell when someone liked him, but rather, in his mind, romance simply didn’t exist as a concept.

Their school, Beijing Guanghua, was notorious for its wealthy students—either young masters or princesses, all raised under halos of privilege.

Kids from such backgrounds had faced little hardship, so their confidence and ambitions soared higher than the sky.

Qi Fang was the only one admitted through special recruitment, with a mysterious background—possibly none at all.

Yet, a crowd of popular young ladies still followed him.

When it came to looks, ideals and background took a backseat.

After all, he was so handsome that someone could drop dead beside him without anyone noticing.

Then, as they pursued him, they discovered his "special admission" was because he overslept during his transfer exam, only taking physics and chemistry—both perfect scores—but far below Beijing’s high school admission line. His father donated a small experimental building to Guanghua to get him in.

Rich, handsome, and brilliant—his reputation quickly spread beyond the school.

Without exaggeration, wherever he went, butterflies followed—some for his money, some for his looks.

But Qi Fang never looked back.

Among a group of arrogant elites, he was the proudest of them all.

Over time, those haughty young ladies, frustrated by his indifference, gave up on chasing him.

He was like a soundless valley—throw a stone into the sea and you’d at least see ripples, but in a valley, you’d hear nothing.

After all, who doesn’t love themselves more than anything? Without a response, who would keep wasting their time?

Unless someone was truly foolish.

No one knew that among them sat another stubborn soul, clinging to a few fleeting moments, wasting three years on Qi Fang without a single glance back.

Amid the lively chatter, Si Qing met a pair of eyes filled with a faint smile.

The boy leaned lazily against the sofa back, his lashes lifting from below, his gaze bright.

Their eyes met, then parted.

Noticing the fine strands of hair swaying at the girl’s forehead, Qi Fang glanced up at the central air conditioning vent.

Under the table, he nudged her shoe with his. "Si Qing, come here."

"Huh?" Five girls responded in unison, like a choir.

"The AC is blowing directly on you." Then he kicked Tang Youmin beside him. "You go over."

"Tsk."

So he wanted him to block the wind, huh?

The two switched places. The moment Tang Youmin sat next to Tan Lexi, the girl popped up, saying she needed to use the restroom.

When she returned, she deliberately sat on Chen Weiying’s side, perfectly squeezing out the space between Tang Youmin and Shen Shangyue.

Chen Weiying was still scribbling notes, silently marveling at how Tan Lexi was a lifesaver for her material-gathering mission.

While waiting for the food, Zhou Qi’ang left first—his wife was finishing her evening self-study, and he had to go home to cook for her.

Both were students at the University of Finance, and last year, right after turning 18, they got married in Ireland. They planned to hold the wedding after graduation, already reserving seats for their friends.

Qi Fang’s friends were all decent—polite, well-mannered, and easy to get along with. Even a group of relative strangers quickly bonded.

When the dishes were almost all served, a pretty college girl approached. She politely greeted everyone, then leaned closer to Si Qing, whispering in her ear, "Excuse me, is the person next to you your boyfriend?"

Si Qing’s heart jolted.

She shook her head, her voice calm. "No."

The girl’s eyes lit up subtly, then cautiously asked again, "Does he have a girlfriend?"

"I don’t know."

She knew he didn’t.

But if this girl wanted to get to know Qi Fang, Si Qing didn’t feel obligated to help. After all, it had nothing to do with her—she could just ask Qi Fang directly.

She was aware of her own selfishness and the inevitable pang of emotion, but there was nothing she could do about it.

"Oh, okay." The girl straightened up, then leaned past Si Qing to greet the boy inside, "Hello, handsome."

Qi Fang lounged on the sofa, playing on his phone. Li Qingyu, sitting beside him, was quick to chime in, pointing to his own ear, "Miss, he’s deaf and mute."

The girls on the opposite sofa covered their faces, whispering, "Iconic! So iconic!"

Si Qing’s expression remained indifferent. She lowered her lashes, unbuttoning her shirt cuffs with deliberate care, rolling up her sleeves one by one.

To avoid paying too much attention to the side, she had to do something else to distract herself.

"But I was sitting right behind you earlier and heard him talking," the girl smiled, her personality straightforward and bold. "How about we exchange WeChat?"

Si Qing’s peripheral vision sharply caught the boy next to her tilting his head slightly in their direction.

He had looked up.

Her fingers slipped, and after several failed attempts to undo the right cuff, she impatiently tugged the sleeve up her forearm.

Qi Fang’s gaze leisurely swept over the girl’s tightly pressed lips, then slid to her hand resting on her leg.

Probably stubbornly competing with herself, her knuckles were white from gripping too hard.

Tsk.

Quite the temper.

Let a little button bully her like that.

"Come here." He played the game one-handed, using his other hand to loosely grasp her slender wrist, pulling her arm over—

chapters.title: No Time to Look at Others
chapters.content:
Warm, dry fingertips pulled down her sleeve, his nimble fingers deftly undoing the cuff button, then pressing the fabric into a neat fold as he rolled it up for her.

Qi Fang withdrew his gaze.

Si Qing felt she had troubled him and didn’t want to delay him further. She quickly pulled her hand back, pressing her lips together. "Thank you."

"You’re welcome." He leaned back against the sofa, then remembered something. Lifting his eyelids slightly, he glanced at the girl still standing beside Si Qing, unmoving. "Sorry, I don’t use smartphones. I don’t have WeChat."

*Goddamn, he doesn’t use smartphones?*

The girl looked at the phone in his hand, where the speaker blared the "ace" sound effect from his game. Furious, she turned and left. "Not even bothering to act anymore, seriously."

The people across from them were laughing so hard they nearly choked.

Tang Youmin looked at Si Qing’s neatly rolled sleeve with interest, propping his chin up as he eyed Qi Fang. "This is good, isn’t it? As an older brother, you should take better care of people. Don’t always bully them like before."

Qi Fang glanced at him indifferently, not bothering to respond.

Shen Shangyue furrowed her brows, slowly tilting her head to look at the person beside her. "You..." Have you been to the hospital to get your eyes checked?

What kind of filter was he using to have such a severe cognitive bias?

Tang Youmin raised an eyebrow. "What’s up?"

"Nothing. It’s fine." Shen Shangyue turned her face away.

Maybe one day, your buddy will take such good care of your niece that she becomes your sister-in-law, you absolute spring fool.

With so many girls present, and training scheduled for tomorrow, no one drank or played games. They just chatted and ate, then left early.

Tan Lexi had ordered an entire plate of roasted chili peppers.

Si Qing loved spicy food, but her tolerance was low.

She used to enjoy ordering roasted chili peppers when eating barbecue, but they often turned out extremely spicy. One bite, and the pain would shoot straight to her eardrums—even two bottles of nutritional express drinks couldn’t soothe it.

Si Qing casually picked one.

*No child cries every day, no gambler loses every time.*

She took a bite, and before she even bit through the stem, she knew something was wrong.

Across from her, Tan Lexi had pulled three skewers in a row and none were spicy. Frustrated, she saw Si Qing suddenly cover her eyes and grab the untouched half of the green pepper from her own bowl.

Tan Lexi took a bite. "Wait! Qingbao, yours isn’t normal!"

A Chengdu girl who considered extra-spicy food a daily staple was defeated, gulping down her milk tea desperately.

Qi Fang turned his head at the sound, only then noticing the girl beside him had nearly finished her milk tea.

The young girl’s eyes were red-rimmed, holding the milk tea in her mouth to cool it down before swallowing discreetly.

Si Qing’s drink was Yangzhi Ganlu; every sip she took was a big gulp, her cheeks puffing out. As she chewed, the soft flesh of her cheek twitched slightly.

She was so overwhelmed by the spiciness that she couldn’t spare attention for anything else, so she didn’t notice Qi Fang had been staring at her for a while.

It wasn’t until the person beside her laughed so hard his shoulders shook that she finally sensed something and looked up.

Qi Fang leaned against the sofa back, openly staring at her with a smile.

"Stop laughing." She hadn’t recovered yet. The moment she set down her milk tea, her ears started hurting again.

The boy’s fair, handsome fingers pressed against his own milk tea, pushing it toward her. His voice carried clear teasing. "Not enough? There’s more here."

"I haven’t drunk mine." He said.

Si Qing was so dazed by the spiciness that her temples throbbed.

She couldn’t take it anymore. Taking his milk tea, she asked, "If I drink this, will you still drink it?"

The dark, lazy fox-like eyes met hers, lingering for a moment before his long lashes lowered slightly, his gaze tracing the moist sheen on her lips.

In that brief instant, he casually looked away again. "Drink it. I’m not thirsty."

"Okay, thank you." Si Qing’s mind was blank, not noticing anything amiss. She nodded, clutching his milk tea like a lifeline.

Curiosity could kill a person.

Across the table, all the girls except Shen Shangyue were dead.

Half a green pepper, one bite each—just to see how spicy it was. Now, each of them clutched their ears, feeling as if flames were about to burst through their eardrums.

Shen Shangyue handed them tissues to wipe their tears.

When she looked back, her bowl had a few peeled crayfish.

Tang Youmin, skilled with his hands, peeled another and dropped it into her bowl.

Shen Shangyue didn’t move her chopsticks, silently biting her lower lip.

She loved crayfish, but she was allergic.

Strangely, no matter the size of the crayfish, she could eat eight without issue, but the ninth would trigger a reaction.

After Tang Youmin found out, he didn’t let her eat any at all.

So now, he might have forgotten about her allergy.

He tapped the side of the bowl with his knuckle. "Good thing these are the last few."

Shen Shangyue was about to say she was allergic, but when she looked down, there were exactly eight crayfish—no more, no less.

Her eyes sparkled with unfiltered joy, as if she had found the greatest fortune.

"You remembered."

Tang Youmin removed his disposable glove. "Less talking, more eating."

Shen Shangyue mumbled an "oh," tilting her bowl so the crayfish gathered in one corner before picking up her chopsticks.

Tang Youmin watched her strange actions. After her chopsticks missed the first two times and only caught a crayfish on the third try, his eyebrow twitched.

"Have you been drinking?"

Shen Shangyue, satisfied, stuffed the crayfish into her mouth. "No."

Her eyes were clear, and she didn’t seem off in any way.

Tang Youmin averted his gaze, pulling out a wet wipe to clean his hands, and didn’t ask further.

After dinner, the girls insisted on paying. Zhou Qi’ang was saving money to buy his wife pretty clothes, so they couldn’t let him foot the bill.

It wasn’t until they reached the front desk that they saw Qi Fang was already paying.

They had only just met, so it wouldn’t be right to let him treat them, especially since it wasn’t a small amount.

The girls tried to transfer money to him, but Li Qingyu stopped them.

"Alright, ladies, no need to stand on ceremony with him. We’ve only just met."

Li Qingyu led the group out, continuing his story. "Once, I dreamed I made 5 million a year, and Qi Fang walked by and said, ‘Dreaming of only 5 million, and it’s annual salary? You wanting food or what?’ You have no idea how much I wanted to kill him then."

They laughed all the way out.

Qi Fang finished paying and walked over. "Did I say something wrong?"

Li Qingyu: "What? When have you ever been wrong?"

"You know the answer."

---

It was only a little past 6:30 when they left. The back streets of Beijing University were lively, and the girls had only recently arrived in Beijing, with little time to explore.

Si Qing enjoyed crafts, and when they passed a bead shop, she decided to go in and make something for each of the friends who had come out today.

The girls in her dorm were lively and restless, so Li Qingyu went with them to look around.

Qi Fang didn’t feel like moving, so he stayed on the small sofa in her private booth, playing games.

She was halfway through her design when her stylus suddenly paused. Turning her head, she asked, "Qi Fang, where did Xiaoyu and Tang Youmin go?"

The man lounging on the sofa didn’t even lift an eyelid. "Don’t know."

"Too focused on you. No time to look at others."

chapters.title: The Reason
chapters.content:
The bustling streets behind Kyoto University were indeed lively, but they were also a mixed bag of people.

Not long ago, there had even been an incident of a child going missing.

Shen Shangyue had something to discuss with Tang Youmin. Before parting, Tang Youmin asked Qi Fang to keep an eye on Si Qing.

Previously, when Tang Youmin had gone shopping with Si Qing and Madame Qin, he noticed that Madame Qin would always tightly hold onto both of them whenever they passed through crowded areas.

Later, when he mentioned this to his elder brother, he learned that Si Qing had almost gotten lost as a child, and Madame Qin had been deeply affected by it.

At that time, Tang Youmin thought, such a small child, left alone in an unfamiliar place—how panicked she must have been.

So he felt that Si Qing might also fear such situations to some extent.

She didn’t say it, so he didn’t ask, but he would do his best to keep an eye on her.

Although Si Qing wasn’t his brother’s biological daughter, their family truly cherished her, treating her like an ancestor to be worshipped.

This girl was truly lovable. Not only his brother, but anyone who had met her couldn’t help but speak to her in a soft, gentle tone.

Even Qi Fang, with his stubborn temper, now obeyed her without complaint.

Apart from anything else, Tang Youmin had to admit that Qi Fang was reliable most of the time.

If he was willing to protect Si Qing like a real sister, that was all for the best.

...

Si Qing probably knew why Qi Fang had been sticking so close to her just now as they passed through the busy market area.

Most likely, Tang Youmin had told him to keep an eye on her.

But Qi Fang seemed to have a natural flirtatious bone in his body. The way he spoke was always tinged with a suggestive, teasing tone.

Anything that came out of his mouth seemed to carry an ambiguous undertone.

Even if he himself didn’t mean it that way at all.

Si Qing stopped talking and lowered her head to draw again.

The bead mosaic she was making wasn’t a pre-designed pattern from the store; she had to design the pixel art herself.

The faint scratching sound of the stylus on the tablet filled the silence.

Qi Fang grew tired of playing games. He tossed his phone aside, pulled over a body pillow, and let his bored gaze wander before finally settling on the quiet girl drawing.

Her posture was always straight, her head lowered, revealing the fair, delicate nape of her neck.

“Drink some water.”

Before she knew it, Qi Fang had stood behind her, placing a cup of water within her reach. He rested his hands on the back of her chair and leaned down to look at her drawing.

“It’s pretty cute.” His fair, sensual Adam’s apple bobbed as he spoke, suddenly appearing in Si Qing’s peripheral vision.

Her dark, clear eyes widened in surprise. “Aren’t you playing games anymore?”

“It’s boring.” The boy’s long lashes lowered slightly as his dark eyes fixed on a few lazy strands of hair that clung to the side of her neck. His fingertips reached out, lifting the strands and tucking them back behind her ear, into the loose bun she had tied.

His expression was serious, as if that stray hair had been bothering him for a long time.

That strand of hair had been deliberately left out by Tan Lexi, who had told Si Qing that a little controlled mess was the key to a girl’s hairstyle having the right vibe.

Unfortunately, Qi Fang was a straight-laced Virgo with mild OCD and didn’t understand such nuances.

“Who are you drawing?” Qi Fang pulled over a chair and sat beside Si Qing, glancing at the image on the tablet.

A cute pixelated figure with a small braid by the ear, half of the hair tied up.

Si Qing blinked at him, saying nothing.

“Me?” Qi Fang’s eyebrows lifted slightly as he leaned in for a closer look. His fingertip tapped the small braid on the cartoon figure’s temple. He chuckled lightly, “But this is a girl, isn’t it?”

“It’s you.”

Earlier, at the store, Zhou Qiang had shown them the commemorative photo from Guanghua’s coming-of-age ceremony.

Qi Fang had been standing in the center of the back row, his tailored modern Chinese suit unbuttoned halfway, his medium-length hair tied back loosely at the nape of his neck. His hands were in his pockets, his chin slightly raised as he turned his head to speak to Zhou Qiang beside him.

His sharp, handsome features and the imposing presence of his striking bone structure were softened by his smile, compressed to the extreme. Even though he wasn’t looking at the camera, among the crowd of silly poses, he still stood out at a glance.

Si Qing said, “You used to have long hair.”

“Hmm?” He asked, “So why not draw me as I am now? Don’t I look good now?”

He did look good now.

But the Qi Fang from that period was a transitional phase between the recklessly vibrant boy in her memories and the refined, gentle young man before her now—a slightly rebellious phase.

The wild, untamed energy and the innate pride in his bones complemented each other, giving off a raw, roguish charm.

Si Qing’s gaze flickered. “Because I’ve never seen you like that before.”

“How have you not seen me like that?”

His fox-like eyes curved into a mischievous, unapologetic smile. “Didn’t you used to call me homeless?”

At his words, Si Qing’s heart jolted heavily.

It was the misunderstanding from Tang Youmin’s video call.

“It was a misunderstanding.”

Her usually calm, warm voice carried a rare hint of emotion. Since he remembered, she had a chance to explain. “I meant the homeless style that was trendy back then. I didn’t mean to say anything bad about you.”

“Then why are you explaining it only now?” He stretched his long legs out, crossing them behind her small legs.

“Back then, we didn’t…” She paused mid-sentence, correcting herself, “We weren’t close yet. I didn’t have your contact information. I couldn’t explain.”

Actually, she did.

Once, when Qi Fang had called Tang Youmin, Tang Youmin had been cooking, and it was Si Qing who had answered the phone.

Tang Youmin used to not save numbers, recognizing callers by their voices.

At that time, Si Qing had secretly memorized the number. It was still saved in her old phone.

“So now we’re close?”

Si Qing nodded. “I suppose so.”

“We are?”

The boy’s dark eyes were calm on the surface, but the way he looked at her was inexplicably intense, carrying a probing, almost sinister edge.

She didn’t dare speak, only shrugging slightly as she looked at him.

After a moment, she heard his voice again.

“Then can you tell me the truth? Why did you cry this afternoon?”

---

chapters.title: Learning to Be Naughty
chapters.content:
He needed to know if the little girl he had been comforting for so long had been bullied by someone else, which was why she had come to him in tears.

Si Qing knew her own limits. If she tried to come up with another excuse now, she wouldn’t be able to fool him.

He had asked this question out of genuine concern, and his care for her so far had been sincere, without any ulterior motives. Yet she harbored feelings for him that he knew nothing about.

So she absolutely couldn’t tell him everything.

She pressed her lips together. “Because I remembered some things… from my third year of high school.”

“Did someone bully you?”

“No, it was just… the pressure was a bit much.”

Si Qing’s gaze flickered. Since she had cried so much that afternoon, her eyes were now painfully sensitive. If she didn’t blink for a while, her eye sockets would burn.

Qi Fang knew how difficult it was to take the college entrance exam in the mountain city.

The girl was remarkable—she had outshone millions to rank second in the province. He didn’t need to think too hard to know how much hardship she had endured.

In her first year of high school, her baby fat had still been noticeable. Now, it was gone.

Her deer-like eyes shimmered with a watery sheen. Qi Fang lightly brushed the corner of her eye with his knuckle. “You’ve been wronged.”

“But it was worth it.”

As his knuckle pressed against her eye, her eyelids fluttered slightly, almost identical to the way his cat at home rubbed against him.

He bit the tip of his tongue with his fangs, suddenly recalling that Si Qing had mentioned she wasn’t an adult yet.

A frown formed between his brows, but he quickly suppressed it.

Qi Fang withdrew his hand. “You’re seventeen now?”

Si Qing didn’t know how his thoughts had jumped there, but after more interactions, she had gradually grown used to it.

She could even occasionally take the lead and tease him a little.

“Sixteen,” she said.

Qi Fang’s eyes narrowed slightly. “What?”

The girl’s innocent deer eyes looked up at him, deliberately staying silent as she just stared.

The atmosphere grew quiet.

Until he caught a fleeting glimpse of a smile in those sincere, bright eyes. Qi Fang ground his teeth, both amused and exasperated.

“You’ve learned to be naughty.”

Si Qing neither agreed nor disagreed, her eyes curving into a smile. “I’ll be eighteen soon. I’ll be an adult by the end of the year.”

Her attention returned to the tablet. Qi Fang, hugging the body pillow, sat back on the sofa, lost in thought. After a moment, he softly hummed in acknowledgment.

---

Shen Shangyue brought Tang Youmin to a small park nearby, where they found a bench to sit on.

This area was near residential buildings, and it was just after dinner, so people were out for a stroll. The wind rustled past their ears, the willow branches swayed gently, and the water rippled under the moonlight, creating a pleasant atmosphere.

Shen Shangyue closed her eyes and leaned back on the bench, letting the wind blow over her. Tang Youmin sat beside her, plucking a willow leaf and idly folding and unfolding it between his fingers.

She had called him here but said nothing. Tang Youmin waited patiently, and the two sat in silence for a long time.

Finally.

“Tang Youmin.”

“Hmm.”

The girl’s voice, mixed with the rustling of the willow branches, sounded a bit muffled. “You’ve grown a lot taller. I haven’t grown much since junior high.”

“Because you don’t eat properly,” he said.

Shen Shangyue was an extremely picky eater. Among girls her age, she was quite thin. Back then, he had tried every way to feed her, even learning to cook and bringing her breakfast, just to help her gain a little weight.

A few days ago, at the police station, he had seen her arms—they were even thinner than before, almost nothing but bone.

She tilted her head back against the bench. “Someone spoiled my appetite.”

Tang Youmin averted his gaze. “Would you not eat at all without me?”

“I wouldn’t starve, but I wouldn’t eat well either. I’d just get by.” Shen Shangyue slowly opened her eyes, her bright peach-blossom eyes shimmering with a smile dampened by the moonlight.

Tang Youmin always felt there was more she wanted to say, but she stopped there, just smiling at him.

“Your body is your own. If you get sick, do you think I can feel the pain for you?”

“That won’t work. I couldn’t bear it.”

She tilted her head closer to him, studying his face carefully.

“I don’t want to just get by anymore.” She called him, “A Min.”

Tang Youmin’s gaze flickered.

After a long silence, he found his voice. “That’s your business. You don’t need to ask me.”

“What I mean is,” her eyes brimmed with a watery shimmer, “I want to pursue you, to win you back. Can you give me a chance?”

Tang Youmin felt almost half of his body go numb.

His emotions were a tangled mess, his mind unexpectedly chaotic.

Why did she say she wanted to win him back, yet never explained why she had let him go in the first place?

She came and went as she pleased—what did she take him for?

“Shouldn’t I first hear the reason we broke up?”

Shen Shangyue’s smile froze for a moment.

She didn’t want Tang Youmin to know that their breakup had been because of her family.

He was sensitive and considerate; he would definitely blame himself for not being good enough to earn her parents’ approval.

But during that age when love was both forbidden and budding, he had already done everything right.

He had respected her, cherished her completely. The most intimate they had ever been was hugging and playful affection.

Because of his first-place finish in the provincial physics competition in the second half of his third year of junior high, Tang Youmin had been directly admitted to the top high school.

He could have stopped coming to school entirely, but he still came every day just to bring her breakfast and keep her company for dinner.

And he had taken care of all the trivial matters for her, allowing her to focus solely on her studies.

Because he had encountered the rarest and most precious thing in life at such a young age, the years she had spent without him had left Shen Shangyue with nothing but compromise.

But she couldn’t say any of this.

Including the fact that she had been sick—she didn’t want him to know.

Tang Youmin would be heartbroken.

But Shen Shangyue didn’t realize that Tang Youmin could always tell when her smiles were genuine and when they were masking other emotions.

He remembered every little habit of hers, even the ones she herself wasn’t aware of.

Like now, her thumb was repeatedly scraping against the second joint of her index finger.

Tang Youmin knew—she was anxious.

—She didn’t want to talk.

He wouldn’t force her.

If he was spineless, then so be it. It was better than making her cry.

“Forget it.”

Shen Shangyue lightly tapped her lip against the inside of her teeth. “Then can I still pursue you?”

Tang Youmin didn’t answer, his eyelashes lowering to hide the warmth in his eyes.

She zoned out, hesitating for a long time, not even bothering to fix her hair as the wind from the river blew it into disarray.

It wasn’t until his warm fingertips gathered her scattered hair, brushing past the thin skin behind her ear, that a flicker of surprised light finally flashed in her clear peach-blossom eyes.

“What do you like about me now?” His fingers combed through Shen Shangyue’s soft, long hair all the way to the ends.

“I want to hear it. Then I’ll consider whether to let you pursue me.”

chapters.title: Not Happy
chapters.content:
Chén Shàngyuè didn’t quite understand the question.

"Liking someone is just a feeling. When I see you, my heart still races. I want to see you every day, eat lots of delicious food with you, and take walks together. That’s how it is."

Táng Yǒumín pinched the ends of her hair between his fingers.

Feelings were intangible—you couldn’t see or touch them. What if one day, her so-called "feeling" disappeared, and she left him again? What would he do then?

Táng Yǒumín’s real issue was that he didn’t know how to keep her. He couldn’t keep getting hurt over and over—just taking losses would be the death of him.

He said, "That’s not very concrete."

Chén Shàngyuè knew he was feeling insecure.

Even if she swore on her life, Táng Yǒumín might not believe her.

So she had to play along, smooth out his ruffled feathers first.

She curved her eyes, "You’re so handsome, and so tall."

"Will I be handsome and tall forever? What if I’m not, will you stop liking me?"

She thought for a moment, "You cook *really* well."

Cooking skills couldn’t just vanish overnight. And even if one day his cooking wasn’t good, she could pretend it was.

"Am I just supposed to chase you so you can be my nanny?"

"…No." Chén Shàngyuè let out a soft breath, "You’re well-liked, and you’re smart."

"So you like me for my friends and my brain?"

"…"

For the next half hour, Chén Shàngyuè listed every single one of his strengths, inside and out.

But he seemed determined to nitpick, finding fault with everything.

Chén Shàngyuè’s eyelid twitched. "Táng Yǒumín, do you just want me to keep complimenting you?"

Táng Yǒumín propped his elbow on the chair back. "You’re already annoyed, and we haven’t even started dating yet."

"No, I’m not—" After rambling nonstop for over half an hour, she was running out of energy. "Fine, I like you because you’re rich. Money, Young Master Táng, I need money."

"There are plenty of people richer than me. Why me?"

Chén Shàngyuè was genuinely annoyed. "What does it matter if others are rich? Do they give me money? It’s not like any of them sent me 50 on Crazy Thursday."

This was infuriating. She already hated rich people, and now she hated them even more.

Soon, she heard Táng Yǒumín let out a low laugh.

Then, the boy held his phone by the edges with his fingers and handed her a green QR code.

"Add me on WeChat. I’ll give you money—whatever amount you want."

Chén Shàngyuè’s brain suddenly froze.

He wouldn’t listen when she was nice to him, but the second she got mad, he smiled and offered to give her money.

This man was more unpredictable than AI.

What the hell was wrong with him?

Dazed, Chén Shàngyuè added him on WeChat. Then he asked for her bank card and Alipay account numbers.

Ten minutes later, the money arrived in her bank account.

One, ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand… *Dad.*

500… *thousand?*

Táng Yǒumín, when you had a fever as a kid, didn’t your mom carry you to the hospital?

The weight of the money almost made her drop her phone. "No, I was just joking! Don’t give me money!"

Táng Yǒumín had finally convinced himself—this time, he *would* keep her.

He’d trust her one more time.

But the very next second, she changed her tune, telling him she’d been joking.

"Chén Shàngyuè."

His voice carried an unyielding chill, and her spine tingled. She lifted her gaze slowly, cautiously. "Y-Yes? What is it?"

Táng Yǒumín’s phoenix eyes drooped as he looked at her. The girl’s lips were pressed into a tight line, her shoulders slightly hunched—she was clearly scared.

He had never been harsh with her before. This was the first time he realized just how little she could tolerate from him.

And yet, even without him doing much, she already looked like she was about to cry.

"You. Be good. Don’t make me angry."

His voice was low, soft, yet carried the weight of someone in control.

The deep, magnetic voice settled over her, and Chén Shàngyuè’s eyes suddenly burned. "Okay."

His warm palm pressed down on her head, rubbing gently. "Be sincere. I’m hard to win over."

A sudden, intense tremor shot through her chest and into her eyes, welling up a misty haze.

For a moment, it felt like she was back in junior high, that Christmas.

The boy had smiled brightly, his fingers intertwining with hers as he asked her directly, passionately, "Chén Shàngyuè, can I pursue you?"

Back then, Chén Shàngyuè had been a risk-averse coward, and Táng Yǒumín had always existed outside her carefully constructed rules.

Like a cautious little snail poking its antenna out of its hard shell for the first time, the girl had shyly pulled her hand away, turned her back, and muttered:

—"Then you have to be sincere. I’m hard to win over."

Now, years later, she wanted to walk his path again.

The mist in her eyes blurred the world around her into patches of light. Chén Shàngyuè lowered her head, her bangs pressing against the shoulder of the man beside her—broader and more solid than it had been five years ago.

Every change in him was a reminder of the five years they’d missed.

She missed him so much.

"Àomin, hug me."

"Hug you before we’re even dating?"

"Hug me."

"Chén Shàngyuè, you’re getting spoiled."

"Àomin."

"…"

A gentle breeze passed by, and Táng Yǒumín noticed the small damp spot on his shoulder. His jaw tightened abruptly.

Had he made her cry?

Should he comfort her? Or not?

…

Was she doing this on purpose? Tricking him into showing weakness?

If he gave in now, would she take advantage?

…

Scheming woman.

He wouldn’t comfort her.

Táng Yǒumín wrestled with himself, trying to rationalize.

Before he knew it, his body had already honestly pulled her into his lap, cradling her securely against him.

"…"

His Adam’s apple bobbed. After a long silence, he squeezed out a few words.

"Don’t cry. Here’s your hug."

---

After shopping for a long time, the girls returned triumphantly to the bead store to meet up with Sī Qīng.

Lǐ Qīngyù’s eyes were spinning from accompanying the girls on their shopping spree.

The girls had boundless energy, unlike people who had just survived military training.

Meanwhile, he had been eating, playing, and carrying bags for them, and the lively atmosphere had nearly given him heatstroke.

Just when he had finally found a store with air conditioning, his butt had barely touched the chair before the girls were already done paying.

The two roommates he’d come with—one had disappeared, and the other was lazy, leaving him to suffer alone.

He thought about calling Lù Yětí to help share the burden, but that guy wasn’t answering his phone.

Probably asleep in the lab again.

"Qīngbǎo Qīngbǎo Qīngbǎo!" Tán Lèqī burst into the private room, holding up a roasted cold noodle in both hands. "We’re! Baaaack!"

The two girls behind her hovered their hands in the air, ready to catch her if she fell.

Sī Qīng turned her attention to the door and blinked. "Why is Qīqī so excited?"

Zhù Xīng massaged her temples. "We passed a stall selling butter beer earlier. Qīqī said she’d never had alcohol before and wanted to try some."

Cén Wéiyíng shrugged. "And then this happened."

Tán Lèqī patted her chest and, in a perfect Liaoning accent, said, "No problem, this little bit isn’t even enough to feed a fish." The girls burst into laughter.

Lǐ Qīngyù was restless and couldn’t sit still. He wandered over to ask Sī Qīng how her work was coming along.

Sī Qīng looked up. "Just the chains left to string. Qī Fàng has finished the rest."

Lǐ Qīngyù raised an eyebrow and glanced at the person curled up asleep on the sofa with a cushion.

"Got it. I’ll do the rest." He pulled over a stool and sat down.

Sī Qīng said it wasn’t necessary. "I can do it."

Lǐ Qīngyù took a few strings of beads from her and carefully threaded them through the holes. "Don’t be polite. You’ve already made us gifts. It’s only right that I help out a little."

The girls gathered around to watch, eyes sparkling. "Qīngbǎo, did you draw all of these yourself?"

Sī Qīng nodded. "From memory. They might not look exactly like the real people."

"So cute!" Zhù Xīng pointed at the one with a white headband. "Is this me?"

Cén Wéiyíng: "My glasses are so adorable!"

"The short-haired one is me! The long, curly-haired one is Xiǎoyú!" Tán Lèqī blinked rapidly. "It really does look like us! Qīngbǎo, you’re a genius!"

Each person’s features were captured perfectly.

The girls were too enthusiastic, and Sī Qīng smiled awkwardly, rubbing her lips together. "You’re exaggerating."

Lǐ Qīngyù finished stringing a chain and pressed the clasp firmly. "Don’t be modest, little sister."

The moment the words left his mouth, the person who had been motionless on the sofa had a subtle frown.

"Tsk."

chapters.title: Territorial
chapters.content:
The room suddenly fell silent, and everyone turned to look.

The boy’s dark, deep eyes were heavy with exhaustion. His pale eyelids were pressed into folds by his sharp brow bones, one deeper than the other.

The temperature in the air seemed to drop by half.

The girls all held their breath, trying to make themselves as invisible as possible, afraid that one wrong move would earn them a glare sharp enough to cut them down.

Only Lǐ Qīngyù remained completely at ease. "Did we wake you?"

His roommates knew that even when he seemed grumpy, he was actually just spacing out—he didn’t have much of a temper when waking up.

Qī Fàng stared at him with an unreadable expression for a moment before shifting his cold, dark gaze to the girl beside him.

After a long silence, he let out a slow breath and raised a hand to cover his eyes.

When he lowered his hand, most of the irritation had faded, replaced by a hint of a smile—not much, but far gentler than before.

Sī Qīng finally dared to speak to him. "You’re awake?"

Qī Fàng tossed the cushion aside. "Sī Qīng, come here."

His voice was lower than usual, with a faint nasal tone that made her ears tingle.

"Okay." Sī Qīng stood up and went to pour him a glass of water first.

The three girls exchanged glances, making exaggerated motions—tongues pressed to the roofs of their mouths, lips bitten—to barely suppress their grins.

Then, in silent agreement, they turned their backs but kept their ears perked up to listen.

Sī Qīng placed the glass on the side table next to him and sat down beside him. "What’s wrong?"

Qī Fàng tilted his head back against the sofa, his soft hair sinking into the light, fluffy fabric. His beautiful fox-like eyes shimmered with tiny flecks of light.

Under her gaze, his long, fair fingers reached out, palm up, and simply held there in silence.

Sī Qīng understood. She focused on the red mark on the tip of his little finger, her gaze flickering slightly. "Does it still hurt?"

About forty minutes earlier, after they had finished ironing the beads, the shop owner’s golden retriever had run over to fetch its toy.

Its back leg had caught on a wire, nearly pulling the iron off the table. Qī Fàng’s left little finger had been burned.

The owner had rushed over to apologize, taking them to a nearby clinic for treatment before they returned with medicine.

Sī Qīng, worried he was in pain, had let him rest on the sofa.

Maybe he had woken up because of the pain.

Qī Fàng drooped his eyelids and didn’t say anything.

So it did hurt, but he was too embarrassed to admit it.

"I’ll reapply the ointment for you. Wait a second."

Sī Qīng took out an alcohol wipe from her bag. Her soft palm covered the back of his warm hand, gently removing the previous layer of ointment.

Given the last time he’d been scratched by a cat, she was extra gentle this time. Her fingertips brushed the burn as she looked up at him. "Tell me if it hurts."

"Am I that delicate?"

Sī Qīng gave him a speechless look.

Who had leaned on her shoulder last time, whining about the pain?

---

Lǐ Qīngyù finished the last chain and was about to tell the couple on the sofa to pack up and head back.

When he turned around, he saw the girl holding Qī Fàng’s hand, head lowered, doing something he couldn’t see.

Then he looked up—

And for no reason at all, his eyes locked with a pair of dark, still eyes.

Calm as stagnant water, staring right at him.

Like a male ghost.

Qī Fàng never lost his temper with them. Usually, no matter how much they joked around, he never got angry.

In fact, he was quite indulgent with them.

In all the time they’d known him, this was the first time they’d seen him like this.

Lǐ Qīngyù’s eyes darted around as he thought back.

Just now, no matter how much the girls had teased, Qī Fàng hadn’t made a single sound.

But the second he, Lǐ Qīngyù, had called Sī Qīng "little sister," the guy had woken up.

…No way.

Lǐ Qīngyù’s eyelid twitched, and he pulled at the corner of his mouth.

"You men, *your* little sister, *your* little sister—enough! You’re the only brother she’s got, alright?!"

After mouthing a long string of silent words, he miraculously noticed the corner of the man’s lips lift by three pixels.

Lǐ Qīngyù: "…"

So it *was* because of that!

Was his territorial instinct *that* strong? Was he a dog or something?!

---

After finishing the medicine for Qī Fàng, Sī Qīng habitually blew on it.

Warm breath settled over the ointment, and her fingertips were cool.

It still felt numb.

Qī Fàng’s gaze followed his own fingertips, unconsciously drifting to the girl’s plump, glossy lips—just half an inch away from his.

His white Adam’s apple rolled up and down.

"Sī Qīng."

The girl’s fair, clean face turned toward him. "Does it hurt?"

"Why do you always assume I’m in pain?" He flipped his hand in hers, gripping it back. "Am I *that* delicate?"

Sī Qīng didn’t answer. Her bright, deer-like eyes blinked slowly twice, then curved into a crescent as she continued staring at him.

Those eyes conveyed everything in just a couple of blinks.

—*You are delicate.*

"…"

Qī Fàng had come to a realization.

This little girl might look obedient, but out of her 100 pounds, 99 were made of rebellion.

Just a while ago, she had avoided him like the plague.

Now that she’d been spoiled, and realized he wouldn’t be harsh with her, she was running wild.

Qī Fàng’s eyelids twitched. "You’re getting bold."

Sī Qīng subtly pulled her hand out of his grip. "What?"

Qī Fàng glanced at her hand, now hanging loosely at her side.

"Taking a man’s hand whenever you please—isn’t that being bold?"

chapters.title: Ideal Type
chapters.content:
Si Qing’s eyes curved into a smile. This guy really knew how to play dirty—just opening his mouth and the lies came pouring out.

Just like dreaming and saying whatever came to mind.

She pouted. How could he just say he wanted to touch a girl’s face? He was really something.

But she couldn’t say that.

It had taken so much effort to get close to him. She was afraid that one wrong move would push the distance between them right back to where it started.

She blinked, suppressing the urge to argue with him.

The other girls and Li Qingyu went downstairs first. There was a pet café on the lower floor, and they went down to pet the fluffy animals while waiting.

Qi Fang watched the little girl’s expression shift—her lips downturned, then flattened again.

Probably upset by his harsh words, stewing in silence.

“Upset?” His knuckles lifted, almost brushing her cheek before stopping.

Si Qing’s neck stiffened. “No.”

He had always known that girls needed to be coaxed.

But Qi Fang never bothered with trouble.

To put it bluntly, none of these people were family or close friends. Why waste his energy on them?

His patience had always been limited.

The only one who could throw a tantrum at him was Si Qing.

Qi Fang was well aware that he gave this little girl far more leeway than anyone else.

But spoiling was one thing—some things needed to be said clearly.

“You might not want to hear it, but I have to say it.”

The little girl was kind. Even when applying medicine for him, she was afraid of hurting him, gently cradling his hand, rubbing it, even blowing on it.

He already treated her like a beloved little sister, never bullying her. But others might not be the same.

Being defenseless around men was dangerous.

“Be more cautious. Don’t smile at everyone. Especially men—if a man approaches you out of nowhere, he’s got ulterior motives.”

Qi Fang softened his voice. “So don’t blame me for being harsh just now, okay?”

“I know all that.” Si Qing lifted her gaze, her dark, clear eyes shimmering with a thin layer of moisture, bright and transparent. “And I haven’t touched anyone else.”

She paused, then corrected herself. “Haven’t touched any men.”

Qi Fang’s eyebrow twitched. “Am I not a man?”

“Or… am I not ‘anyone else’?”

He leaned back lazily against the soft cushion, as if nothing were wrong, lowering his lashes. He untied the decorative silk ribbon bow on her sleeve and re-tied it into a neater one, waiting for her answer.

But this question was impossible to answer correctly.

If she said he wasn’t a man… she’d get hit.

But if she said he wasn’t “anyone else”…

That would be emphasizing his specialness.

And in Si Qing’s eyes, Qi Fang *was* the most special one.

But their relationship wasn’t intimate enough for her to confess that.

…

After a while, the sofa beside Qi Fang’s leg, which had been pressed into folds, suddenly emptied.

Si Qing methodically packed her things and the medicine, holding them in her hand. “Going downstairs?”

Changing the subject, huh.

Qi Fang lifted his lashes to glance at her. “That hard to answer?”

So, the implication was—he was both “someone else” and *not* a man?

Si Qing sensed he was about to make trouble. Her doe-like eyes curved into crescents as she softly said, “Let’s go.”

A fair, slender hand—much smaller than his—reached over. Her soft, cool fingertips poked at his wrist, which was draped over the back of the sofa.

The moment he felt that chill, Qi Fang’s brows suddenly furrowed. He glanced at the air conditioning temperature.

His lashes half-closed, and he stayed still for a few breaths.

Then, his wrist turned over, and without warning, her soft fingers fell into his palm.

Qi Fang’s hands were always warm. His palm was large—if fully spread, it could probably enclose her entire hand.

Si Qing came to her senses, her shoulders tensing. Just as she was about to pull her hand back, it was gently enclosed by his warm, dry palm.

From downstairs, Li Qingyu’s voice suddenly carried up. “Are you awake now?”

Si Qing replied, “We’ll be right down.”

Qi Fang pressed his tongue against his lower lip, lost in thought.

A moment later, he nudged the hand in his palm, which had regained some warmth. “Help me up. My leg’s numb.”

A flat, emotionless remark.

The backstreet to Jingda University was only a quarter of an hour’s walk, but in the end, they still took a taxi back.

The reason was simple: Tan Lexi was drunk, wobbly, and couldn’t walk straight.

After getting back to school and stepping out of the car, the wind revived them a little.

Afraid that Tan Lexi would feel unwell if she went straight back to the dorm, the girls deliberately wandered around campus for a while until her drunkenness had mostly worn off before returning.

When Si Qing finished washing up and came out, the three girls had already set up a chair for her. Each held a handful of melon seeds, their eyes signaling: *Come, we’re about to gossip about you.*

“…”

Zhu Xing narrowed her eyes, pretending to be profound. “Qingbao, how come you and Qi Fang came down holding hands just now?”

Cen Weiwel’s cheeks were puffed with laughter she couldn’t contain. “What were you two doing up there? Can we, the children’s channel, listen in?”

Si Qing helplessly waved her hands. “Nothing happened. His leg was numb, so he asked me to help him.”

Zhu Xing leaned in. “My god, two steel legs. It hasn’t even been ten minutes, and they’re already numb? That’s fast.”

“He was giving me a *moral education* up there.” Si Qing added, “The serious kind. Big brother mindset.”

“Big brother is good.” Tan Lexi said, “There’s an old saying in my hometown: first be friends, then be like a little sister, and finally become a little treasure. If there’s chemistry, you’re already at step two.”

Cen Weiwel: “We who write romance novels rely on physical contact to advance the relationship between the leads. Qingbao, pay attention—does he have that *reluctant yet lingering, wanting to speak but holding back* kind of seduction toward you?”

For her, Qi Fang didn’t need to seduce.

Just standing there, breathing.

And Si Qing would secretly praise his skills.

He was originally a very gentle person. As for whether his current care for her was just that, or if he truly had some feelings for her… she couldn’t tell yet.

Zhu Xing laughed until she trembled. “It’s not like you can touch anywhere—don’t be like Qiqi, touching people’s—”

“STOP STOP STOP!” Tan Lexi bristled, covering her ears. “I didn’t touch!”

The girls burst into laughter in the dorm.

When girls got together, they could talk about anything—topics ranging from the heavens to the earth, spanning the highest and lowest, yet always circling back to one evergreen subject.

—*Ideal types.*

---

chapters.title: Use Me and Then Kick Me Away
chapters.content:
For Si Qing, the term “ideal type” was just a set of words used to describe Qi Fang.

But in reality, her falling for Qi Fang wasn’t something that happened overnight.

She considered herself a very rational person. To her, a racing heart and genuine affection were two distinctly separate concepts.

And with Qi Fang, her curiosity—sparked by that initial flutter—led her to observe him. Over time, she realized that he and she came from two different worlds.

Their tiny overlap wouldn’t bring about a fundamental change. Since she already knew her feelings would never be reciprocated, she had to convince herself to stop liking him.

Though longing and excitement were hard to suppress, she *had* been gradually reducing the attention she paid to Qi Fang.

Until that winter in her first year of high school. Si Qing remembered it was a Tuesday.

It was her turn to be on duty for the week. By the time she left school, the senior high division had already started evening self-study.

Mountain City No. 1 High School’s first-year students didn’t have evening self-study in the first semester, so she headed straight for the Bus 629 stop after leaving campus.

Once on the bus, she made her way to the very last row.

In the middle seat sat a boy in a white-and-purple school uniform, his head covered as he slept. Si Qing sat down with one seat between them.

Judging by the uniform color, he was from the same school’s second-year division—probably skipped evening self-study.

Mountain City High had a large student body, and the school uniforms were color-coded by year.

First year: blue and white. Second year: purple and white. Third year: gray and yellow—beautifully named “Towards Glory.”

But from afar, it looked like an overcooked egg yolk. Ugly as sin.

It wasn’t until Si Qing herself reached third year and put on that egg-yolk cosplay uniform that she finally understood why Qi Fang and her only good sister in Mountain City, Lian Zi, had both transferred back to Beijing in their second year.

By the latter half of the bus route, more than half the seats were empty.

That made the man standing in the aisle all the more conspicuous.

It wasn’t that his refusal to sit was strange—it was that, with so many empty seats, he chose to stand next to a girl.

The girl seemed to notice, getting up to switch seats.

Before long, the man followed.

In the span of two minutes, she changed seats four times and still couldn’t shake him off.

At that point, aside from the driver, only four people remained on the bus. The upperclassman from the second-year division next to Si Qing was still asleep.

She glanced at the bus stops.

The stop before hers was Wutong Road Police Station.

After a moment’s thought, she clenched her fists, psyching herself up, and went to explain the situation to the driver.

The driver pulled over at the next stop and asked the man about it.

The man raised his voice, accusing them of slander, even shamelessly judging the girl he’d been following based on her appearance.

“What bad luck!” The girl shot him a resentful look, picked up her bag, and stood to leave.

Then, as if remembering something, she turned back to Si Qing. “Little sister, which stop are you getting off at? If it’s really bad, you can come with me, and I’ll call you a taxi home. I’m afraid that guy might retaliate.”

Si Qing suddenly grew alert.

Not that she wanted to assume the worst, but recently, kidnapping tactics had been getting more creative. She was afraid this girl and the man might actually be in cahoots.

“Thank you, but it’s fine.” Si Qing smiled gently, her eyes curving. “I’m getting off at Wutong Road Police Station. My brother is picking me up at the bus stop.”

The girl didn’t press further. She just reminded Si Qing to be careful before turning to leave.

The bus fell silent again.

Then, the boy in the last row suddenly coughed.

“Come sit here.”

His voice was hoarse, like he had a bad cold.

A moment later, when the hand with slightly raised fingertips emerged from beneath the school uniform, Si Qing’s heart skipped a beat.

Qi Fang pulled down the uniform covering his head, lifting his eyelids wearily, as if he’d been woken by the earlier commotion and had only caught the gist.

He tilted his head toward the seat beside him, gesturing for Si Qing to sit there.

His hair was a little messy from the uniform, but it did nothing to diminish his looks.

He just seemed a bit grumpy from being woken up, his brows furrowed, looking fierce.

Si Qing hurried over and sat down beside Qi Fang, moistening her dry lips.

Just as she was wondering how to greet him, she heard Qi Fang’s voice again.

“Wake me when we arrive. I’m going back to sleep.” His tone was indifferent.

Okay, no chance for conversation.

“Alright,” she obediently replied. “Senior, which stop are you getting off at?”

“Same as you.”

“Okay.”

And that was the end of it.

She felt a little disappointed but quickly recovered.

Just seeing him was good enough.

Qi Fang never took this bus.

He stayed at school from Monday to Friday and returned to his apartment near the school gate on weekends.

Their routes didn’t overlap, and with the senior division having evening self-study, it was already a stroke of luck as rare as a star falling on her head for Si Qing to encounter Qi Fang outside of school.

She just didn’t know what he was doing at the police station.

Si Qing hugged her schoolbag, her gaze falling on the window.

The night outside was deep, and she could openly admire him through the window’s reflection.

The boy leaned back against the seat, his profile sharp and smooth, his bone structure exceptionally refined. His lips were full, slightly pursed.

Suddenly, she saw him frown. Si Qing almost panicked and looked away.

Qi Fang turned his back and coughed violently for a long time.

There were even a few deep breaths in between, making Si Qing’s heart ache.

It was unbearable.

Like a butterfly fluttering at the water’s surface, her heart was suspended in uncertainty.

Seeing him in discomfort made her feel terrible.

Si Qing barely suppressed the heaviness in her chest, unscrewed the press lid of her thermos, and held the cup out to him.

“Senior, I haven’t used this cup mouth. You can use it if you need to.”

Before long, the cup was pushed back by his fingertips.

“Thanks.”

He declined politely.

It was normal. Qi Fang was someone with strong boundaries, and she didn’t think much of it.

She just felt a little regretful that she couldn’t help him.

“Okay.”

Si Qing worked up the courage to observe him. Once she confirmed that his discomfort had subsided, she sat back properly.

Her hand still clutched the hand warmer she’d found in her bag while reaching for the water cup. It was unopened.

Noticing that Qi Fang didn’t seem to intend to sleep anymore, Si Qing tentatively called out to him.

Those eyes, still carrying a hint of fatigue, looked over.

Afraid he would refuse if she asked, she decided to just hand it to him directly.

Even though it wasn’t freezing yet, the wind was strong and dry. A hand warmer was better than nothing.

“Senior, can you put out your hand?”

As soon as she spoke, that hand—which she had silently praised countless times—slowly extended.

Si Qing dropped the hand warmer into his palm and immediately stuffed her hands into her pockets.

No chance for him to return it.

“What’s this?”

“It’s warm. Keep it.”

After saying that, she was surprised to find another hand warmer in her pocket.

A pleasant surprise. Her mood suddenly improved, her tone unconsciously rising a couple of notes.

“Senior, there’s another one.”

Qi Fang pinched the two small objects in his palm, raising an eyebrow at her. “Both for me?”

Si Qing’s eyes curved into a smile. “Both for you.”

He didn’t respond.

A few minutes later, the voice announcement notified them of their stop. The two stood and moved to the back door.

The suspicious man also wobbled over, standing diagonally behind Si Qing.

The bus had stopped properly at the station, and the passengers boarding got on through the front door.

Perhaps noticing that there was no “brother” waiting for Si Qing at the stop as she had claimed, the man followed closely.

According to Si Qing’s original plan, regardless of whether the man followed her or not, she was going to sprint to the police station the moment she got off the bus.

The moment the doors opened, Si Qing was pulled into an embrace by a certain someone’s arm.

A faint orange scent, along with the slightly higher body temperature of the person behind her, invaded her senses.

It was the laundry detergent scent she had smelled on Qi Fang before.
