An inexplicable sense of relief washed over her.

“Let’s go.”

The two stepped off the bus side by side.

Whether it was the driver’s perfect timing or coincidence, the suspicious man standing one step behind them was precisely blocked by the closing back door.

The bus’s engine noise faded away, replaced by the rustling of the evergreen tree leaves above them in the wind.

The boy’s loose strands of hair were lifted by the breeze, his silhouette softened by the warm yellow streetlight.

Si Qing’s heartbeat was drowned out by the rising sense of loss.

“Senior, I’ll go now.”

Qi Fang withdrew his hand, scanning the area before asking her, “You live here?”

“My house is at the next stop. It’s not far. I can walk back.” Si Qing pointed toward the police station. “You should go in. It’s cold out here.”

She heard a soft scoff from above her.

“Use me and then kick me toward the police station, huh?”

His brows and eyes held a smile, his dark gaze bright, completely lacking the distant air he’d had on the bus.

He looked like he’d woken up properly.

Before she could react, Qi Fang reached out and patted her schoolbag. “I’ll walk you home. Lead the way.”

The moon hung high in the sky, bright and dazzling.

Her eyes held only Qi Fang.

At that moment, the moonlight shone upon her.

He would probably never know—how much her heart had raced in that instant.

chapters.title: She Wanted to Chase the Moon
chapters.content:
She quickly collected her thoughts, not wanting to delay him any longer.

Her strides were so large that she occasionally walked ahead of Qi Fang, then subtly slowed down to fall back beside him.

When they reached Si Qing’s neighborhood entrance, he lifted his chin slightly. “Go back.”

After saying goodbye to him, Si Qing entered the neighborhood first, then secretly doubled back and hid by the entrance to watch him.

Qi Fang didn’t head toward the police station but walked to a nearby bus stop and sat down.

It was the bus going back to school.

…

A string of thoughts flashed through her mind, and Si Qing’s hand gripping the doorframe unconsciously tightened.

—Before she got on the bus, Qi Fang was already on it.

—He had skipped the evening self-study session, but hadn’t returned to the apartment near the school gate. Moreover, he looked unwell.

—Bus Route 629 started at Shancheng No. 1 High School West Campus and ended at the Third Central Hospital.

So Qi Fang had originally intended to go to the hospital.

But because he ran into her halfway, worried that the man might follow and retaliate, he got off early and endured the discomfort to walk her all the way home.

As for why he didn’t go to the hospital anymore, Si Qing had no standing to ask about his choices.

Since the school didn’t allow smartphones, she couldn’t check the bus schedule. All she could do was rush home as quickly as possible, gather all the cold and flu medicine she could find, then run upstairs to her bedroom for her phone.

She tripped over her slippers halfway, nearly tumbling down the stairs.

The more anxious she was, the more mistakes she made.

By the time she returned to the bus stop, Qi Fang was leaning against the platform with his eyes closed, looking pale.

Si Qing asked if he wanted her to go to the hospital with him. Qi Fang said no, he just wanted to go back and sleep.

Not trusting him to take the bus alone, she hailed a ride and forcibly stuffed him inside.

This way, if anything happened to him, the driver would at least have someone to contact.

The red glow of the taillights grew from dots into lines, cutting through the night softened by warm yellow streetlights.

Si Qing stayed at the bus stop, occasionally checking her phone to track the trip.

Only after confirming Qi Fang had arrived safely did she stand up and leave the platform.

Suddenly, the sky turned white.

Petal-like snowflakes settled on her lashes. She looked up, reaching out to catch a few.

Si Qing remembered it was the third snow of that year—heavy, long-lasting, and the first to accumulate.

At that moment, she was just relieved that Qi Fang hadn’t been caught in the snow.

…

The fluttering emotions of youth were not like the fleeting ripples stirred by a seagull skimming the water’s surface. They were a long, recurring snow season.

Si Qing finally understood: she had fallen for someone with a gentle nature, a truly good person.

There was probably no one else in the world who could make her heart race like he did.

So even if he was as unattainable as the moon, it didn’t matter.

At least for a moment, the moonlight had gently fallen upon her.

And she wanted to chase the moon.

---

Wen Weiying placed the washed cherry tomatoes on the table. “So, Qingbao, do you have an ideal type?”

“Ah,” Si Qing’s lashes trembled slightly as she came back to her senses. “Probably… someone attentive and gentle.”

Zhu Xing: “What about the kind who’s a little arrogant, roguishly handsome, has a sharp tongue but a good personality, takes care of people, can joke around, and has a bit of humor? Like Qi Fang.”

This was important to Zhu Xing.

It directly determined whether the ship she was rooting for could end up together.

It also indirectly determined whether she should jump off a building during Si Qing and Qi Fang’s baby-making phase to reincarnate as their beautiful and rich child.

“Don’t always bring him up. What if he sneezes in the dorm?” Si Qing said, slightly embarrassed, smoothly shifting the topic. “What about you, Zhu Zhu?”

“My ideal type?” Zhu Xing propped her chin, opened WeChat to send an emoji to someone before continuing. “The abstinent type, a bit old-fashioned. Even if he’s a little clueless, he’s really fun to tease.”

At the top of her phone screen, the contact labeled [Yuyu] sent a question mark. “You done having fun? Finally remembered me?”

Zhu Xing casually typed back.

“Instant reply?”

“So obedient. Been waiting for me?”

Yuyu: “Do you talk to all your good brothers like this?”

Zhu Xing’s eyes curved into a smile. “Yuyu gege is the most obedient.”

Yuyu: “…”

The other girls could tell who she was talking to just from her expression.

Tan Lexi swept the sunflower seed shells into the trash and raised an eyebrow playfully. “Teasing your quiet guy again?”

Zhu Xing laughed and slapped the table, turning her phone screen toward the girls. “You guessed right.”

Cen Weiying stuffed two cherry tomatoes into her mouth, speaking with a full mouth. “Three sentences, and you’ve got Se Yi wrapped around your finger.”

Tan Lexi cupped her face, eyes sparkling. “It’s so nice to have someone you like. Just thinking about seeing them makes you happy.”

Cen Weiying poked Tan Lexi’s cheek. “So many guys chase you, and you don’t like any of them?”

Tan Lexi shrugged. “None of them are my type.”

Si Qing remembered Tan Lexi had once described her ideal type—both concrete and abstract.

—Long bangs, black-rimmed glasses, usually so unnoticeable he might as well be a blade of grass in the corner. But take off the glasses, lift the bangs, and—wow, a stunningly handsome man.

At its core, it was still about looks, but not *obviously* so.

She was after the thrill of discovering that the quiet, unassuming guy was actually a super handsome heartthrob.

Since she hadn’t met anyone like that yet, she remained single to this day.

And her ideal type evolved with every new game or comic she encountered.

For example, a few days ago, she became obsessed with the soft, puppy-like second male lead in a certain drama.

She decided that guys who said “okay?” and “right?” in a cutesy way were adorable, and suddenly, she was in love.

Si Qing couldn’t help but laugh. “Qiqing’s ideal type is abstract, but her *un*ideal type is very specific.”

Cen Weiying: “You mean the trendy guys who always ask people to work late at night?”

“That damn Liu Liu! He’s deliberately making things difficult for me!”

At the mention of him, Tan Lexi was ready to lose it. “There are seven people in our group. The other day, I asked the rest to check some data, only to find out they never even had the task! What the hell!”

After her outburst, she paused, then made an OK gesture with her hand. “Whatever, I accept it. It’s my fault for being too reckless back then—I nearly scalded him into a little girl.”

Zhu Xing closed her WeChat and joined the conversation. “I actually looked him up on a forum the other day. I have to say, being in a band *is* cool. He’s a sunny, handsome guy with fangs—you can tell he’s full of energy. Doesn’t seem like the petty type.”

Tan Lexi sighed. “Who doesn’t maintain a persona in public?”

Lu Yeti was like a concept—whenever Tan Lexi heard his name, within half an hour, his name would appear at the top of her WeChat with unread messages.

Seeing Tan Lexi instantly wilt, the girls knew she was in for it again.

Tan Lexi impatiently swiped open her phone.

Old Liu: “Where’s your work report?”

She sent the report she had just finished that afternoon, tossed her phone aside, and continued chatting with her friends.

Soon, a voice message popped up.

Tan Lexi grabbed a cherry tomato and stuffed it into her mouth, intending to tap to convert it to text. Her damp fingertip slipped—

A deep, sexy male voice abruptly cut through the girls’ laughter.

“Your eyes are so beautiful.”

Her hand trembled, and she quickly turned off the screen.

She looked up, and the three girls were staring at her like they’d seen a ghost.

chapters.title: Afraid of Me?
chapters.content:
Si Qing blinked several times without moving. “Cen Cen, is this what you call ‘enemy-to-lovers’ literature?”

Cen Weiying, expressionless: “Enemies are enemies. Enemies can’t turn into boyfriends.”

Zhu Xing: “This isn’t something a handful of glutinous rice can fix.”

“I’ve been wronged!” Tan Lexi felt her soul ascending to heaven. She replayed the full voice message.

—“Your eyes are so beautiful… what the hell is this last paragraph you wrote? At least delete the AI-generated summary!”

Her face was ashen. She spread her hands, as if to say, *I have no words*, yet also as if she had said everything.

If taken out of context, her chat history with Lu Yeti could compile a book titled *Ambiguous Quotes*.

Examples included, but were not limited to:

*You’re so beautiful.* — *That’s a beautiful thought you have there.**Can you keep me company?* (voice message) — *Can you compensate me for emotional damages?**Why don’t you like me?* — *Why doesn’t the secretary like our proposal? Go fix it.*

Tan Lexi gave up and sent a voice message back: “If you don’t like it, delete it yourself. No need to ask me.”

Si Qing’s eyes widened. Such defiance toward a superior was rare in Shancheng.

“Qiqing, are you trying to get yourself fired tomorrow?” she asked softly.

Tan Lexi flicked her short hair with a swagger and coldly scoffed. “The crimes on my head are longer than his life. Afraid of him? Ridiculous.”

In reality, she rarely saw Lu Yeti, so even if she disobeyed, he couldn’t do much—at most, he’d give her a harder time.

---

“Tsk.”

Li Qingyu chewed on cold noodles, glanced back at the person behind him who was venting at the computer, then at the WeChat interface on his screen, and chuckled.

Considering that a certain ancestor with a biological clock as precise as an atomic clock was already asleep, Li Qingyu lowered his voice. “What’s up, Ti Ti? Did that little girl from your department mess with you again?”

Lu Yeti didn’t respond. He opened a document, his fingers flying across the keyboard.

Li Qingyu dragged his chair over, watching his hardworking buddy endure the hardships. “I’m just saying, she’s the only girl in your department. Be nicer to her, you know? Show some chivalry?”

Lu Yeti spared him a glance. “Does gender matter? She’s the only clear-headed one in the group. I have to teach her properly so there’s at least one smart kid left for the next leadership change.”

Li Qingyu thought his rigid mindset was beyond saving. “Still, you can’t keep asking her to work late. She probably hates your guts by now.”

“When do I have time to teach her during the day?”

“…Fair point.”

Lu Yeti finished his annotations on the document and sent it back. «Fix it.»

---

Due to scheduling, the Career Life Planning Competition was postponed until after the National Day holiday.

At the same time, the notice for the school debate competition was released. Although it offered practical course credits, few were interested.

Military training had exhausted everyone—no one had the energy to prepare for a competition.

Ke Mingyuan pulled every favor and highlighted every benefit until he finally gathered enough participants.

Si Qing was one of the reluctant recruits.

She had no choice—Ke Mingyuan mentioned that the debate competition *might* invite the president to be a judge.

The word “might” was enough to sway Si Qing.

Since their last meeting, she had only seen Qi Fang once.

—When the military training squad left the North Stadium, they passed by the college building, and she saw him walking inside.

Only his back was visible.

A girl was walking beside him, almost jogging to keep up with his pace.

Qi Fang indeed wasn’t the type to adjust his stride for others. He walked at his own rhythm, with long steps, so anyone walking with him had to match his pace.

That was why, during the few times they had walked together before, Si Qing would subtly adjust her steps, though she sometimes still fell behind.

Later, as she got used to it, she could keep up with him, even occasionally walking ahead.

But he never noticed.

Qi Fang was very busy and didn’t spend much time at school.

During military training, she could see him occasionally since he was a teaching assistant.

But after military training ended, if she wanted to see him, Si Qing had to seize every opportunity outside of her studies.

Since she had never participated in a debate competition before, she had to burn the midnight oil, watching recorded debates online, studying them frame by frame, and revising her arguments.

She skipped evening training and endured three consecutive days of preliminary rounds, barely making it through the final selection for the School of Management’s team.

The next day was the second-to-last day of military training. The intensity of the later training was far less than at the beginning.

The instructors took every opportunity to slack off. At the first sign of overcast skies, they claimed it would rain and led the freshmen to the auditorium to enjoy the air conditioning.

With nothing new to learn in the last two days, it was decided that a freshman mixer would be organized on the school’s public holiday.

After the morning training was dismissed, they were free to do as they pleased. The afternoon mixer on the field was optional.

Rare free time—Si Qing planned to nap in the dorm.

Tan Lexi, ever the social butterfly, was naturally going.

Zhu Xing and Xi Yu had gone to Global Studios. Cen Weiying, worried that the sound of her typing would disturb Si Qing, decided to go to the self-study room to write.

After pulling several all-nighters, Si Qing’s head was foggy. She had a few bad dreams, drifting in and out of sleep until 12:30 PM.

After checking her phone for unread messages, she was shaken awake by Chen Chengyan and taken to the college to organize certificate holders and competition props.

At this hour, all the department’s staff were preparing to go to the mixer on the field. No one was active in the group chat.

With nothing better to do, unable to sleep, and unwilling to attend the mixer, she decided to help out at the college.

Chen Chengyan and Dai Wan were both there. When Si Qing arrived, the two were rummaging through boxes, searching for a flash drive.

Seeing Si Qing, Dai Wan lifted her arm to push back her hair. “Hey, Si Qing, go check the duty room. Chen Chengyan was on duty there this morning—it might be in there.”

“Oh, okay.”

Chen Chengyan cleared the desk, scratching his head in frustration. Suddenly remembering something, he added, “If the door won’t open, knock a few times. Qi Fang is sleeping inside.”

At the mention of that name, Si Qing’s steps faltered subtly.

Then she looked down at her sloppy shorts and T-shirt, touching her half-dry hair, which she had hastily tied up.

Her deer-like eyes drooped in despair.

“…”

She was even wearing *slippers*!

Though they were outdoor slippers, who would want to meet their crush looking like this?

She could pass for someone out grocery shopping.

Qi Fang hadn’t been at school much these days—who knew today would be the day he decided to show up?

Murphy’s Law struck again.

She hesitated for a moment, then bit her lip and silently retreated back to the organization department’s activity room.

Chen Chengyan caught a glimpse of the girl floating back to the doorway out of the corner of his eye. He looked up. “What’s wrong? He won’t open the door for you?”

Si Qing curved her lips slightly, speaking softly. “Senior, maybe you should go instead. I’ll help Sister Dai here.”

She would rush back to the dorm to change, then find an excuse to come back and see Qi Fang in the afternoon.

Chen Chengyan raised an eyebrow with a smile. “Afraid of him?”

Si Qing blinked, absentmindedly responding with an “Ah.”

A moment later, most of the light spilling through the doorway was blocked as a shadow fell over her. The shadow on the floor belonging to her was now overlapped by the person behind her.

*Click.* The flash drive was pressed onto the low cabinet by the doorway with a fingertip.

As he straightened up, warm breath carrying a crisp, citrusy scent brushed lightly against the side of her neck.

Si Qing’s shoulders shrank back, and a tingling sensation spread to her earlobes.

“Afraid of me?”

chapters.title: Probing
chapters.content:
Ghost!

A jolt of electricity shot down Si Qing's spine, and her shoulders trembled uncontrollably.

A hint of unfamiliarity and embarrassment, along with a great deal of anticipation and excitement—all because he was right in front of her—rushed up her cheeks, scorching hot.

Si Qing couldn’t explain why, but after not seeing him for a few days, she felt awkward when they met again.

She missed him so much, yet she didn’t know how to start the conversation.

She turned her head, blinking awkwardly. "Senior, hello."

The fox-like eyes, usually devoid of emotion, drooped slightly.

Facing the flicker of fear in the girl’s eyes, he gave a faint, almost imperceptible tug at the corner of his lips.

"Hello."

Chen Chengyan spotted the USB drive Qi Fang had left on the cabinet and sighed in relief. "You’re a lifesaver, bro."

Qi Fang gave a small nod. "Busy?"

Dai Wan lifted her head from the box. "Of course. Cleaning up the mess left by the previous organizational department."

Si Qing quickly turned around and rushed to Dai Wan’s side. "Let me help."

Dai Wan, afraid the clutter on the floor might trip her, reached out to pull Si Qing over, then turned back to Qi Fang. "It’s too messy in here."

*—So please leave quickly. Don’t just stand there taking up space. Do you have any idea how much room you’re occupying?*

She didn’t say it.

Mainly because she didn’t dare.

After all, this man was personally recruited by the former president—the only fresh blood among the new recruits.

Sharp-tongued, but capable, generous, and respected.

Just too stingy with his time, with no regard for reason.

No matter the time, if I ask you for a plan, you make it. If I say it’s not good enough, you revise it.

I’m not sleeping, so why are you?

Inhuman. Truly inhuman.

And yet, despite all that, there were still plenty of girls chasing after him. Tsk.

Anyone who followed him for more than two days would be in for a rude awakening.

At the end of last semester, after the leadership change, many girls found out they could catch him in the office. They took turns coming.

Qi Fang’s preferences were quickly figured out.

Once or twice, he’d politely decline.

Three or four times, disrupting the office? Then don’t blame him for being harsh.

This man had no patience. Previously, a few girls had cried as they left the duty office, and he hadn’t shown the slightest intention of softening his words.

Dai Wan and Chen Chengyan had discussed this in private.

They both agreed this guy was only suited for a relationship with money.

No living person could tolerate that mouth of his.

Not just the sharp tongue—he did whatever he pleased. When he didn’t want to understand you, he’d act like an idiot.

Like now.

"Messy? Then clean it up." Qi Fang casually pulled over a chair and sat down.

His long legs stretched out carelessly, leaning back in the chair as he lowered his head to play on his phone.

Chen Chengyan: ?

"Are you moving in here?"

"If I want to." He kicked the box beside his feet. "There’s still stuff here to clean up."

"Qi Fang, your—"

Qi Fang stingily lifted an eyelid.

Chen Chengyan gritted his teeth. "How’s your grandfather’s health lately?"

"None of your business. Get back to work."

"..."

Si Qing couldn’t help but tilt her head and smile.

Every response was sharp, and none were pleasant.

The three of them cleaned the room while Qi Fang lounged by the door like a king, playing games without a hint of sleepiness.

Sure enough, people never tired of causing trouble.

Si Qing was about to carry an empty box out when, in the middle of his game, he managed to stretch out his leg to block her path.

In her hometown, there was a saying: stepping over someone was bad luck for them.

She peeked out from behind the box. "Senior, your legs are too long."

Qi Fang didn’t look up. "There are two seniors in this room. Which one are you talking to?"

Just then, a moth had flown in from the window, and Chen Chengyan and Dai Wan were busy shooing it away. How could Qi Fang not know which senior she was addressing?

Si Qing lifted her leg and gently nudged his. Softly, she said, "Stop messing around."

His eyelashes lifted, and he glanced at her with little emotion before slowly retracting his leg.

Si Qing curved her eyes at him, then quickly carried the box past him.

She hoped he wouldn’t notice what she was wearing.

After placing the box in the stairwell, she turned back.

Chen Chengyan had contacted the scrap collector. Soon, all this clutter would be sold.

From the hallway, they could hear faint shrieks and Dai Wan’s voice scolding Chen Chengyan.

"On the wall! Chen Chengyan, jump and press it there!"

"Stop hitting me first! Give me a piece of paper! Do you expect me to catch it bare-handed?"

Later, it seemed Qi Fang had helped. Si Qing could hear Dai Wan’s voice from afar.

"Chen Chengyan, what the hell are you good for? Huh?"

Chen Chengyan, his pride shattered: "Heaven gave me talent for a reason! I can reach it on my tiptoes!"

Immediately after came a slow, unhurried voice: "Heaven gave me, useful, you, talent must."

Chen Chengyan: "...Damn."

When Si Qing reached the doorway, Dai Wan was already laughing so hard she was bent over.

She glanced at the tissue in Qi Fang’s hand and took it from him. "Give it to me."

Qi Fang pulled out a few wet wipes to clean his hands, then sat back in his chair, his gaze lazily following the little girl who was holding a wad of paper and circling the room.

Actually, Si Qing hadn’t found the trash can.

She remembered there used to be one in the room, but it must have been kicked somewhere during the cleanup.

The second time she passed Qi Fang, she heard a soft, low chuckle.

Si Qing stopped in her tracks, her deer-like eyes blinking. "What’s wrong?"

Qi Fang looked at her hands, which were piously holding the paper. "Are you going to raise it, send it to school, buy it a house and a car, help it get married, and have kids?"

Si Qing was a little confused. "It’s already dead."

"Then why aren’t you throwing it away? Physically transcending it here?"

"I couldn’t find the trash can."

Si Qing spoke softly, her voice carrying a rare hint of amusement—not anger at him, but genuine amusement.

Dai Wan found the trash can and brought it over, placing it at Si Qing’s feet. She chimed in, "If you’ve got energy, take it out on Chen Chengyan. Be nicer to our little friend, won’t you?"

Qi Fang indifferently nodded. "Oh, so my life doesn’t matter?"

Chen Chengyan was practically laughing in frustration.

The three of them worked together, joking around as they cleaned, and soon the room was mostly tidied up.

Chen Chengyan checked the time. The freshman mixer on the field had already started.

Noticing that Si Qing hadn’t said much while cleaning, just quietly working away, Chen Chengyan figured she was probably eager to get to the field.

The mixer was hosted by the Business School and co-hosted by the School of Information.

The Business School had a male-to-female ratio of 3:7, while the School of Information had a ratio of 7:3—a perfect match.

As the name suggested, it was essentially a freshman dating event.

After all, with the iron rule in place—if you didn’t find a partner in your first year, it would be hard to experience campus romance in the following years.

Fast-food romance was better than fast-food breakups. At least it was an experience.

Take him and Dai Wan, for example. They were so busy with club activities in their first year that by the time they looked around, everyone else had paired up. Now, they had no way to find a partner.

Chen Chengyan lifted his chin toward Si Qing. "Junior, it’s not busy here anymore. You should go quickly. The mixer has just started. It’s only a five-minute bike ride from here. You’ll make it."

Si Qing had originally wanted to say she wasn’t going to the mixer, but catching a glimpse of the lazily seated man beside her out of the corner of her eye, she bit her lip.

At the last moment, she changed her mind. "It’s fine, Senior. I’ll help finish cleaning first."

---

chapters.title: Rivals
chapters.content:
As she spoke, her peripheral vision remained fixed on him, quietly observing.

After a long while, there was still no reaction from him—not even a lift of his eyelids.

The tiny bud of hope that had sprouted in Si Qing’s chest withered back silently.

She had probably realized that Qi Fang had a high tolerance for her.

He didn’t resist physical contact; in fact, he seemed to enjoy teasing her.

But whether that was because he saw her as a little sister or because he had a hint of genuine interest in her, Si Qing wasn’t sure.

So she steeled her heart and tested him.

Qi Fang knew this mixer was essentially a dating event. His indifference likely meant he had no possessive feelings toward her.

Even though she had expected this, she still couldn’t avoid a small pang of disappointment.

But it was just a little.

It was a taboo to hope and feel disappointed on her own. Greed would backfire.

When liking turned into an obsession, he would become the anchor that controlled her emotions. If she couldn’t control it, her entire heart would tilt toward him.

She would lose herself.

Si Qing was good at balancing her own emotions. She just needed to empty her mind for a while, to clear her feelings.

During her third year of high school, when she was so exhausted she couldn’t go on, she would go to the badminton court across from the teaching building and sit for a while.

Watching the clouds outside soaked in the purple-red glow of the sunset, smelling the faint, unknown floral scent in the wind, her mood would improve a lot.

She was so focused on her own little world.

So much so that from following the two department heads out of the Student Organization activity room to being pulled into another room by someone grabbing her arm, she didn’t react in time. She plunged headfirst into a cool, bitter fragrance wrapped in warmth.

A short, rising gasp escaped her, colliding with him along with the soft warmth that had tumbled into his arms.

Like one of those plush toys she often saw as a child—the kind with a small squeaker inside that chirped when squeezed.

Qi Fang’s eyelids lifted slightly, the curve of his eyes barely noticeable.

He had intended to hold back, but he still ended up pulling her off balance.

Si Qing’s consciousness returned, and a dull pain shot through her nose.

She sniffed, lifting her hand to press against his chest, pushing lightly.

But she didn’t budge him. Instead, the reaction force pushed her back two steps until her back hit the door.

"..."

Embarrassment spread across her brows. And then Qi Fang laughed softly.

Si Qing’s still unsettled emotions were stirred again by that hint of shyness. She lifted her lashes, restraining herself as she glared at him. "What are you doing?"

There was a lack of the usual gentle indulgence in her voice. To Qi Fang’s ears, it somehow felt... spirited.

Like training a dog.

His dark eyes lowered, sweeping over her fair, delicate face.

"Not afraid of me anymore?"

His emotions were scarce, his tone almost cold.

Si Qing’s gaze flickered, and she lowered her head, muttering softly, "If you’re not mean to me, I won’t be afraid of you."

Qi Fang’s lips twitched. "You’re taking advantage of the fact that I’m not mean to you to pin labels on me."

Seeing that she wasn’t responding, he raised his hand and pressed it against the girl’s soft, fluffy head. "Admit you’re wrong and now you’re playing dumb?"

Si Qing’s head swayed with the movement of his palm, silently patting his arm.

"Tsk."

His hand stilled, and he leisurely fixed his gaze on her. "Acting unfamiliar in front of others, but throwing a tantrum with me in private?"

Si Qing slowly lifted her eyes. "I’m not throwing a tantrum, and I’m not acting unfamiliar with you."

"Not acting unfamiliar?" He bent down to meet her gaze. "Then who are you calling ‘Senior’ for?"

His extremely sharp, handsome face suddenly loomed large before her eyes. "Go on. Let’s hear your excuses."

Her heartbeat thudded powerfully against her eardrums. Si Qing forced a dry smile, shrinking her neck slightly. "Because I didn’t know you were here, and then—"

*—And then I hadn’t seen you for days, and I was too nervous, so I didn’t know how to talk to you.*

Qi Fang silently raised an eyebrow, his expression urging her to continue.

"And then... you *are* a senior. If I wanted to greet you, I couldn’t very well say ‘Hello, Qi Fang,’ could I?"

He let out a light scoff. "You’ve got a point."

His fingertips lifted the strands of hair that he had messed up on her forehead, smoothing them back into place before patting the top of her head.

"Alright, go back and change your clothes before heading to the field. There are a lot of bugs, and you’ll get bitten in shorts."

Si Qing’s lashes trembled, and her lips tightened.

Suddenly, she recalled an autumn when she had gone out in her summer home clothes to get a delivery. When she returned, Aunt Qin had scolded her.

Uncle Tang had tried to comfort her, but Aunt Qin had a fiery temper and ended up scolding Uncle Tang as well.

She had said that not taking care to stay warm when you’re young would lead to rheumatism in old age.

That day, she and Uncle Tang had been confined to the balcony for half an hour of reflection before being let out.

When Tang Youmin came home for dinner and passed by the balcony, he had teased them. As a result, Uncle Tang had rushed out the moment the time was up, grabbed him by the neck, and delivered a profound lecture on brotherly love.

In that fleeting moment just now, Si Qing felt that Qi Fang was a lot like Aunt Qin.

As if he truly cared for her like someone very close.

"Okay," she said, her eyebrows curving into a smile. "Then I won’t go. It’s really hot outside."

And the person she liked wasn’t there.

Qi Fang shifted his gaze away from her bright, smiling eyes, turning up the air conditioning a few degrees. He then took a blanket from the cabinet and draped it over the back of the sofa before lifting his chin toward Si Qing.

"Then come sit here."

Si Qing blinked. "Huh?"

"You still owe me half a day."

Earlier, when Si Qing had borrowed Qi Fang’s phone, she had accidentally sent a flood of emojis, causing a mess.

Afterward, they had negotiated, and she had agreed to compensate him with half a day of her time.

"Ah, right." Her clear, black-and-white eyes shimmered with a mix of surprise and delight as she stared at him.

"Okay."

Qi Fang sat back in the office chair, leaning back against the chair. "Let’s settle the debt, little rival."

chapters.title: Inch Photo
chapters.content:
However, what Qi Fang meant by "repaying the debt" was to let her sit comfortably on the soft sofa, covered with a blanket, and act as a living mascot.

The two of them sat quietly in the room, the air heavy with silence.

Every slight movement she made caused the leather sofa to emit faint sounds, which stood out sharply in the stillness.

Compared to Qi Fang, her small movements seemed too loud.

Afraid he might find it annoying, Si Qing moved to a chair by the conference table.

Since she hadn’t brought headphones, being farther away from Qi Fang allowed her to turn up the volume slightly to watch debate competition videos.

From a distance, it was also easier to look at him.

Qi Fang was deeply focused, his pen pausing without any unnecessary fidgeting.

Occasionally, his upturned fingertips brushed across the paper. His nails were neatly trimmed, and his fingertips and knuckles had a faint pink hue, smooth and translucent like fine jade—long, elegant, and sensual.

Si Qing didn’t consider herself someone with a hand fetish, but his hands were simply too beautiful. Every movement was a pleasure to watch, and once she fixed her gaze on them, it was hard to look away.

Suddenly, the hand holding the pen lifted, fingers spreading as it waved the pen at her.

"Snap out of it."

The boy’s voice, laced with amusement, reached her. Si Qing’s lashes trembled, her teeth gently biting her lower lip as she lifted her gaze.

Qi Fang curled his finger, lightly propping up his chin. "Bored?"

Si Qing shook her head. She got up, poured two glasses of water, took a sip from one, and placed the other near Qi Fang, taking the opportunity to glance at what he had been writing.

It was an English test paper, with long reading passages. The question format was different from CET-4, CET-6, or the domestic Gaokao.

It looked more like IELTS or TOEFL.

The surprise in the girl’s doe-like eyes was too obvious. Qi Fang raised his eyebrows slightly. "What, do I not look like someone who studies?"

"No, with your grades, how could you not study?" Si Qing didn’t want to disturb him further. After delivering the water, she returned to her seat.

People who could effortlessly score high without studying were either geniuses or protagonists from novels.

Before high school, Si Qing used to read novels and once envied certain male leads who could casually top the class without lifting a finger.

She read a variety of genres, but without exception, the male leads—whether they were cold and academic gods or roguishly handsome school bullies—never studied.

Later, after getting into Shanyi High, she was disillusioned.

Books were full of lies. The students at the provincial key high school were more competitive than washing machines. After a round of exams, she barely managed to secure a place in the top ten of her grade, and even that left her frayed at the edges.

Every major exam, the honor roll at the school gate would be updated with a new batch of names.

The red honor rolls for first-year and second-year high school were placed side by side.

After her first monthly exam in first year, her photo appeared on the list. Coincidentally, she was tenth in first year, and Qi Fang was first in second year.

Their photos were placed next to each other.

It was her little desk mate who dragged her to see it before she noticed.

Red-backed inch photos, separated by a small gap.

One day, a bizarre photo suddenly spread through the grade.

The dividing line between her and Qi Fang’s inch photos on the honor roll had been edited out.

The girl looked youthful and pure, gentle and quiet, while the boy had a slightly raised chin, his eyes brimming with unrestrained arrogance and sharpness.

The two faces, with completely opposite auras, placed together, created an inexplicably eerie feeling.

The level of eeriness was equivalent to a child about to give birth to a wife, then being asked on the operating table whether to save the doctor or the nurse.

Like two people who couldn’t stand each other but had to get married due to a business arrangement, forced to go to the civil affairs bureau for a certificate.

...

Later, Si Qing indirectly asked Tang Youmin and only relaxed after confirming that the photo hadn’t spread to the West Campus.

In the next monthly exam, she jumped to fifth place in the grade and never appeared next to Qi Fang again.

After all, in a place like Shanyi High, where competition was fierce both openly and secretly, no one would deliberately hold back their scores just to stay next to someone they liked.

---

Qi Fang stared at her leisurely for a while. The little girl was quietly hunched over her phone on the table.

Presumably bored out of her mind, every time he looked up, he caught her just as she was closing her eyes.

Yet she stubbornly refused to give in to her drowsiness, straightening her back and rubbing her eyes each time.

Qi Fang suddenly realized he might be a bit of a jerk.

—Keeping her here, yet ignoring her.

Something like that.

On the other hand, Si Qing was impossibly well-behaved, afraid of disturbing him, even pouring water for him as quietly as possible.

"..."

As his conscience pricked him, he looked at her again and felt the little girl was pitiful.

Si Qing had just adjusted to a comfortable position, leaning over the table, when the sunlight spilling on the desk was suddenly blocked.

Then, inexplicably, she was pulled up by him.

She looked up in confusion, facing the boy who leaned against the edge of the table.

Seeing Qi Fang looking down at the video on her phone screen, Si Qing instinctively swiped to mute it.

"Was it too loud?" she asked.

"Don’t hunch over your phone." Qi Fang didn’t answer her question, lazily resting his hand behind him, lifting his chin slightly. "Signed up for the debate competition?"

Si Qing nodded.

"What position?"

"Third speaker."

Qi Fang’s eyelids lifted slightly. "Impressive."

"I haven’t competed in a formal match yet," Si Qing’s shoulders slumped. "I’m still learning."

The third speaker was a high-intensity position, requiring anticipation of every possible argument the opponent might use, spotting logical flaws on the spot, and using reductio ad absurdum to refute.

Before she started debating, she hadn’t realized how impressive it was for Qi Fang to win Best Debater multiple times in a row while serving as the third or fourth speaker.

Now she understood.

Qi Fang asked her, "Has the debate topic been announced?"

"Not yet. We’ll know after the draw tomorrow afternoon."

At the mention of this, the girl’s small face scrunched up, as if all the energy had drained out of her.

Suddenly, as if remembering something, her clear, doe-like eyes flicked up, staring straight at him.

The little girl was quite good at speaking with her eyes.

Qi Fang suppressed a laugh, reached out, and tapped her head. "Say something nice, and I’ll help you."

Si Qing was afraid of wasting his time, so she didn’t dare to ask directly. This way, even if he pretended not to understand her intentions, she had an out.

But Qi Fang had agreed to her request.

Her heart gave a small leap.

Si Qing pressed her lips together and blinked tentatively. "Gong xi fa cai."

"?" Qi Fang gritted his teeth, his fingers pinching her cheek. "How generous of you."

"Ow." Si Qing flinched, rubbing her face. "Not good enough?"

"Not as good as the sound of you saying ‘ow’."

"..."

This man’s words were always so colorful.

To prevent him from noticing her blush and to stop him from pinching her again, Si Qing covered her face with both hands.

"Then what do you like to hear?"

His gaze lingered on her. "If I like it, you’ll learn it?"

Si Qing cautiously leaned back. "...It has to be legal."

Qi Fang let out a low laugh.

No conscience, treating him like a hooligan.

He wasn’t angry. On the contrary, he found it unexpectedly amusing to tease her into a fluster.

"You say it,"

The boy stretched out his long legs, hooking the leg of her office chair with his shoe, pulling her in front of him. He leaned forward, pressing his hands on the armrests on either side of her.

"‘Brother Qi Fang is the best’—then I’ll help you."

chapters.title: Comforting Herself
chapters.content:
The afternoon light was still a bit dazzling, flickering through the window lattice and dancing in his dark eyes, which were brimming with playful charm.

The distance between them wasn’t particularly close, but she somehow felt subtly enclosed within his domain.

His presence filled every inch of the air she could perceive.

Si Qing did her best to ignore the heartbeat that seemed to have risen to her throat, struggling to maintain a calm exterior.

She repeated the phrase extremely quickly.

Qi Fang almost caught it.

It was so infuriating it was almost funny.

"Speaking so fast, did you rent that mouth? In a hurry to return it?"

Si Qing adjusted her composure and looked up again. "I said it. Don’t back out."

He tapped her forehead with his fingertip. "Who taught you to be so unreasonable?"

Si Qing met his gaze openly and frankly.

She said nothing, yet said everything.

—You.

A faint, ambiguous arc appeared at the corner of his lips.

It was definitely his own doing.

"Tch."

He wanted to get angry.

He knew his words were harsh.

Afraid of scaring her into tears and then not being able to comfort her, he’d be the one left with no choice.

Forget it. If she wanted to be unreasonable, so be it.

"...Fine, I’ll help you." He lightly flicked her forehead, grinding his teeth to suppress his frustration.

---

After reviewing two debate matches, it was past four in the afternoon when a message from Tan Lexi popped up in the dorm group chat.

搞点夜宵七七叭: "sos"

Si Qing exited the video software and looked down to type: "What’s wrong?"

搞点夜宵七七叭: "I got heatstroke. I’m at the infirmary. Damn, the first thing I saw when I opened my eyes was the doctor on duty, Lu Yeti. Reporting to my family, I’m playing dead first."

A few short sentences told a complete ghost story.

Back then, this girl had relied on her busy boss having no time to catch her and had managed to offend everyone online.

Si Qing’s eyes widened in shock.

Chen Wei Ying was usually busy typing and didn’t check her phone. Zhu Xing wasn’t at school, so Qi Qi’s life was in her hands.

Qi Fang had just summarized the arguments of both sides’ third speakers. His pen was still poised on the paper when the girl beside him suddenly stood up from the sofa.

A short line appeared on the paper.

He lifted his gaze, inevitably sweeping over the girl’s long, straight legs.

The light outlined the porcelain-like skin, dazzling for a moment.

Qi Fang consciously averted his eyes and spoke, "Standing there like a soldier. Did military training fry your brain?"

Si Qing looked down to type her reply in the group chat. After sending it, she turned back to Qi Fang. "Qi Fang, I have something to do. I need to leave first. Can I make up for the time I owe you next time?"

"No need." He uncrossed his legs, pressed a message on his phone, and stood up.

"Let’s go."

Si Qing blinked, her doe-like eyes shifting to the boy who was tidying up the desk. "It’s your shift change already?"

Qi Fang neatly folded the paper filled with arguments and handed it to her. "Where to?"

"The infirmary. My friend got heatstroke. She can’t wake up right now. I need to pick her up." She said, "She’s the short-haired girl we ate with last time."

Qi Fang raised an interested eyebrow. "What do you mean, she can’t wake up?"

"She said if she wakes up, she’ll be chopped into atoms."

---

About half an hour earlier, Tan Lexi had been dancing on the field when she was brutally struck down by ultraviolet rays.

She collapsed to the ground in an "ORZ" pose and was carried to the infirmary by two unfamiliar girls.

Her vision was a blur of green, the world spinning, her heart pounding, and her temples throbbing.

After lying on the bed for a while, she fell asleep.

She dreamed of the apocalypse—black winds swirling, a massive tornado approaching, about to swallow her whole. She desperately ran toward a utility pole behind her.

But her steps were heavy, as if she couldn’t move. Panicked, she crawled while crying.

Perhaps God was moved by her will to survive, because the utility pole started walking toward her (?)

She grabbed it with all her might—

"Tsk." A bright, impatient male voice.

The wind stopped.

She suddenly opened her eyes.

The dizziness in her head hadn’t completely subsided. Everything in front of her was white, and her nose was filled with the faint scent of disinfectant.

She was still confused when something suddenly knocked her head.

It was a real, solid tap. *Pia.*

Her head became even more muddled.

Soon, a cold male voice came from above her.

"What the hell do you want? Huh?"

Oh, that familiar accent.

Down-to-earth to the point of being a little intimidating, yet the voice was pleasant.

She knew someone like that.

"..." Lu Yeti glared at his own leg, which she had hugged.

It was a rare half-day off from training, and he had thought he could finally rest for an afternoon.

But no, right before the end of his shift, someone was brought in.

If he remembered correctly, this girl had it out for him.

She had scalded him with corn and ordered him around like a servant.

He didn’t want to deal with her, but ever since Tan Lexi had been lying there, she had been tossing and turning, making the metal bed creak.

The air conditioning was already broken, which was annoying enough, and now this made it worse.

Assuming she was uncomfortable from the heat, Lu Yeti casually picked up a music score and stood at the head of her bed, fanning her.

He hoped she would fall asleep and stay still for a while.

But after a short while, she started crying, and before he knew it, she had reached out and hugged his leg.

Now that she was awake, she still showed no sign of letting go.

Lu Yeti scraped his tongue against his back molars. "Nice grip?"

Tan Lexi rubbed her eyes, her mind clearing as she finally realized she was still holding onto something.

At the same time, she recognized his voice.

*Click.* She froze on the spot.

Without a word, she naturally loosened her grip, pretending to still be asleep. She turned over, facing away from him.

"You better still be asleep."

She heard the gritted teeth in his voice.

She was all talk online, but in person, she was a coward.

If she dared to wake up, there was a 100% chance she’d be doomed.

Taking advantage of Lu Yeti walking away, Tan Lexi trembled as she pulled out her phone to call for help.

---

When Si Qing arrived, she saw a boy in front of the door, head lowered, wiping his phone.

The infirmary was dimly lit, and the boy’s hair was tinged dark red by the dull white incandescent light.

Hearing the movement at the door, he lifted his eyelids, his gaze dark.

Si Qing’s shoulders trembled. She poked her head in, then retreated a few steps, waiting for Qi Fang to catch up.

Could she say something?

He was wiping his phone like it was a knife.

Qi Fang had one hand in his pocket, leisurely raising the other to knock on the door. Without waiting for a response from inside, he walked in as if returning home and casually sat on an empty bed.

"Eaten yet?" he asked indifferently.

Lu Yeti’s eyes were hollow, a laugh vibrating in his throat. "Thank you for your concern. Did you come empty-handed to ask if I’ve eaten?"

chapters.title: Toy
chapters.content:
The moment the boy spoke, the subtle Liaoning accent in his tone carried an overwhelming sense of familiarity.

It made the whole person seem sunny.

Si Qing gave a slight nod. "Senior, hello. I'm here to pick up Tan Lexi."

Lu Yeti tilted his head toward the innermost bed. "Not sure if she's awake yet."

Si Qing jogged over, pulled back the curtain, and poked her head in.

"Qixi, are you awake?"

Tan Lexi jolted upright from the bed with a loud creak, followed by a soft scoff from the doorway.

"Been awake for a while, huh? Just pretending to be asleep with me?"

Tan Lexi: ..............

She quickly faked a yawn, her voice weak as a dying breath. "Qingbao, my head is so dizzy, and I feel like throwing up. Am I just heat-stroked? I want to go back to the dorm right away."

Si Qing suppressed her laughter, ruffling Tan Lexi's curly hair as she whispered, "Your director is talking to you. Aren't you going to answer him?"

Tan Lexi shook her head slightly and silently made a "shh" gesture with her hand.

Lu Yeti drawled, "Tan Lexi, come out."

Tan Lexi's eyes widened in shock. How did he see her through the curtain?!

Si Qing pointed at the window beside her, helplessly curling her lips. "The curtain is sheer. I could see everything when I came over."

Tan Lexi: "Tsk."

Suddenly, she wished she could die right now, reincarnate as a cicada in the next life, sleep soundly for 17 years, wake up and shout at the world, pee shamelessly at passersby, and then drop dead for no reason.

Instead of living like a knife stuck in her armpit, aching and laughing every day.

"What do you want?" she demanded, putting on her shoes with fierce momentum before timidly hooking her arm around Si Qing's and stepping out—only to slip and kneel with a thud.

"Even if my attitude toward you was a bit off, it doesn't mean I'm completely in the wrong. Sure, talking back to you was my mistake, but didn't I finish my work well?"

Si Qing: 6112066113)?

Tan Lexi: 770377

Using a conjunction like a comma, huh?

Lu Yeti frowned deeply. "Find time to get your brain checked. I suspect there's something wrong with your speech center."

After saying that, he gestured with his eyes for Tan Lexi to sit in the chair in front of him. "Stick out your hand. Let me feel your pulse."

Si Qing: 35)?!.

If it weren't for the fact that she knew this man usually spoke in half-finished, breathy sentences, Tan Lexi would have slapped him long ago.

"What are you feeling for?" she asked.

"Your pulse, of course. Aren't you dizzy and nauseous? You should have recovered from early-stage heatstroke by now. I need to check if there's something else wrong with you."

He stretched out her arm and pressed it onto the table. "What do you think I'm feeling for? Do you take me for someone like you, who can't get enough of being a pervert?"

Si Qing saw Tan Lexi clench her teeth hard, her soft, rounded jawline jutting out.

She obediently stepped back.

Then, she turned to look at Qi Fang, who was sitting on the bed playing on his phone. She pursed her lips, moved next to him, and lightly perched on the edge of the bed, waiting for Tan Lexi.

After a moment, the man beside her suddenly hummed, his dark, deep eyes flicking over her.

Perhaps she had grown familiar with his petulant ways, because Si Qing was surprisingly able to decipher the general meaning from that single glance.

—Qi Fang thought she was sitting too far away, as if she were avoiding him or pretending not to be close to him.

But...

She lowered her gaze to Qi Fang's absurdly long legs—one stretched out, the other propped up on the bed frame, half-bent.

Did he even realize how much space he took up?

He occupied nearly half the bed.

If she sat any closer, she'd be sitting on his lap. Was that appropriate?

Si Qing looked wronged. "There's nowhere else for me to sit."

Qi Fang slowly withdrew his gaze, and as he swiped on his phone, he stretched both legs out, crossing them, his heels pressing into the floor.

A large space opened up on the bed.

The pure white bedspread dipped slightly as the girl softly asked, "Is this okay?"

Qi Fang lifted his lashes to glance at her.

Like he was just going through the motions.

She obediently scooted closer, but her attention was not on him at all.

What was so interesting about those two feeling each other's pulses at the door?

Tsk.

"Too far."

Hearing this, Si Qing looked down at the less-than-two-fists' distance between them. She dug her nails into her knuckles and scooted a little closer.

This man had absolutely no self-awareness of his own antics.

"Too far."

He didn't even look before saying that.

Even the closest of people shouldn't sit pressed together.

Besides, the infirmary's air conditioning was broken. It was hot.

Realizing he was messing with her again, Si Qing puffed out her cheeks slightly and lifted her face. "Qi Fang."

"Finally willing to look at me?" he said lazily, then shifted his dark eyes away.

Si Qing choked, her breathing shallow.

"Oh." She gritted her teeth lightly against her lower lip before noticing he had already put his phone away.

She knew his attention span was short.

His phone held little appeal to him; it seemed like he did everything just to pass the time.

If you opened Qi Fang's mind with the logic of a pretty cat, his intention in that sentence would be easy to understand.

—I'm so pretty. If you don't play with me, you're wasting my beauty.

In reality, he was just bored by himself and wanted to flick his tail at her.

The more he acted like this, the more she shouldn't let the fluffy creature distract her. She needed self-control. She needed to follow the rules.

Otherwise, she'd end up as a human-shaped cat toy.

Si Qing spoke softly, "I'll play with you, but you can't treat me like a toy."

What was that saying? i people are e people's toys.

The girls in the dorm, those e people, teased her like a toy every day.

While squishing her face, they'd say, "Why are you so fun to play with?"

Especially Tan Lexi—she found playing with her more exciting than playing on her phone.

Si Qing was used to it. When she said this to Qi Fang, she didn't feel there was any hidden meaning.

—Until she caught the flicker of surprise in Qi Fang's eyes, followed by a growing playful smirk.

Qi Fang's shoulders slumped slightly, his dark eyes studying her with a hint of scrutiny, yet those eyes were inherently alluring.

Si Qing watched as the boy's long, dense lashes slowly moved from her eyebrows down, the shadow beneath his eyes deepening as they lingered at her jaw for a moment before suddenly lifting.

"Si Qing, I don't understand."

She lowered her lashes, leaning back slightly to force herself to calm down. "Aren't you just trying to have fun at my expense?"

"Wronged me."

Qi Fang propped one hand behind her. "What do you mean by 'I'll play with you, but you can't treat me like a toy'?"

She fluttered her lashes, her gaze brushing past his straight nose before settling firmly on his fox-like eyes, which held a teasing glint.
